nothing else.  The edge/level register at 4D0h is read, on a machine
with a PCI bus, and never written.

3.  A CARD'S MEMORY (pg_mapphys, IOS_MAPPHYS, INT 31h 0800h).  The
page tables stopped at 256MB and a card's registers are in the last
gigabyte.  They are mapped WHERE THEY ARE - the identity again, so a
pointer to a frame buffer is still a number that could go on the bus -
four megabytes at a time and only when asked.  A processor with 4MB
pages is given a directory entry and nothing else; one without takes a
table from a pool of eight behind the ordinary ones (PG_DEVTABS), and
when the pool is empty the call fails.  Nothing is ever unmapped.
0800h refuses the first megabyte, as the specification says.

4.  THE BUS, ALL OF IT (IO\PCI.INC).  pci_scan walks the machine at
boot, following each bridge to the buses behind it, and keeps up to 64
functions in a table.  They are found by position, by class, and by
vendor and device, each with an index.  A register is read and written
a byte, a word or a dword at a time, the write going to the one port
of the four that holds it rather than being read, changed and written
back, which would clear every write-one-to-clear flag in the dword.
pcx_bar measures a base address register with the device's decoding
switched off and interrupts off.  pci_read and pci_write put the
address port back as they found it: a box's access is two instructions
and a call from the kernel can land between them.

pci_find is as it was, first match on bus 0, because the IDE driver's
argument for that has not changed.  STILL NO RESOURCE ASSIGNMENT.

All of this is one service with the function in AH (IOS_BUS, BUS_* in
PMDOS.INC), and 21h/F1h AL=12h hands a program's registers to it.  THE
FUNCTION IS IN BITS 16-23 OF EAX THERE, because AH is F1h.  PMDOS.SYS
had 6.8K left, so everything is in PMIO and the DOS side is a boot
call, the pass-through and 0800h: 173 bytes.

5.  WHERE A BUFFER REALLY IS (IO\VDS.INC).  A bus-master card is
handed a physical address and a real-mode driver works one out as
segment times sixteen, which is the address of a hole for anything in
upper memory.  INT 4Bh AH=81h answers 8102h to 8106h, 810Bh and 810Ch
by reading the page tables; bit 5 of 40:7Bh says it is there.  8107h
to 810Ah, which lend out a buffer, are refused with the
specification's own codes: there is no buffer, and 8102h says so.  A
region not in one piece is reported as that, with how much of it is.
Reached through a HLT in a stub, like the mouse; IOS_MSHLT and
IOS_MSPARK are box_hlt and box_park now and ask the mouse first.
Anything else on INT 4Bh goes to whatever had the vector.

WHAT IT COST.  Three paragraphs of conventional memory for the stub,
32K of extended memory for the pool, and PMIO's body is 33.3K of its
64K, from 27.6K.

TRAPS MET.
  - wasm's case folding, four more times: NE_RESET and ne_reset,
    RTC_A and rtc_a, and two that were seen coming, IRQ_CHAIN and
    VP_GUEST.  An equate and a label cannot differ only in case.
  - POWERSHELL FOLDS CASE TOO.  A parameter $Root and a variable
    $root are one variable, and the second assignment wins: the rig
    handed MKDISK an array where a path belonged.  $Conf and $conf
    did the same to the emulator's configuration, which is why the
    Sound Blaster was never there to find.
  - MKDISK names a file by the last part of its path.  A kernel kept
    as self_PMIO.SYS went onto the disk under that name and the disk
    did not boot.  Keep a second kernel in a directory of its own.
  - A VIA 686B's IDE function reads back FF00FFF9 from a port
    register written with ones.  Sixteen bits of a port register are
    the register; the rest is whatever the chip says.
  - THE ROM ABOVE 4GB IS NOT THE ROM BELOW 1MB.  The copy at F000 is
    shadow memory the BIOS unpacked itself into.  DPMIIRQ compared the
    two and failed on the 440BX; it looks for the jump a processor
    starts at instead.
  - INT 15h AH=87h is refused here on purpose, so it cannot be the
    second road to a physical address.  VDSTEST goes into protected
    mode and reads it through a descriptor.
  - DOSBox-X'S VOODOO CARD FOLLOWS A REGISTER BEING MEASURED, decoding
    switched off or not: its log says "LFB now at ff000000" and then
    "at d0000000", and when it moves back whatever was under FF000000
    is gone - the ROM at the top of the address space among it.  So
    DPMIIRQ's last check finds the ROM when it runs before PCITEST
    and sixteen bytes of nothing when it runs after.  86Box does not
    do it.  It is why pcx_bar runs when it is asked and not at boot.
  - DPMI.INC, DOSMAIN.ASM and BUILD.CMD end their lines CR LF and
    nothing else in the tree does.  A pattern ending in a bare line
    feed matches in one file and not the next.

VERIFIED.  DOSBox-X, headless: VPICTEST 11 of 11 (line 8 sixty-four

WHAT WAS FOUND AND LEFT, AND WHAT WAS UNDER IT (2026-09-27)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The entry above ends with two things found and left.  Both are put
right here, and testing them found seven more, one of which was the
worst thing in the DPMI host: A CLIENT THAT CALLED THE BIOS A HUNDRED
TIMES TOOK THE MACHINE WITH IT.  New: TOOLS\DPMIVEC.ASM, which
assembles to DPMIVEC.COM and DPMIV32.COM, and DPMII32.COM out of
DPMIIRQ.ASM.  Still v0.60.

1.  THE TRACE BUILDS.  DBGSINK.INC ended with three buffers, which
are 40,192 zeros, in an image the stub blits 64K of.  They are at
DBG_MEM now, below the arena, in a kernel built with DBG_LPT and in no
other: ARENA_BASE is 0A000h higher there and dbg_init clears what
nothing loads.  MEM.EXE takes the arena's start from PMDOS.INC, so
BUILD.CMD gives it %DEFS% too.  The body is 34,586 bytes and the
release kernel came out of that change byte for byte the same.

Two more things were behind the size check, which stops a build
before anything after it is tried.

THE TRACE'S QUIET TRIGGER COULD NOT FIRE.  Its counter was a dword
called v86_watch, wasm folds case, and V86_WATCH is a build switch:
every IFDEF V86_WATCH after the label was true in a build that had
only asked for the trace.  So the loud watchdog was assembled in
beside the quiet one, and put the counter back to zero on every tick
that did not find the guest in V86 mode.  Five seconds of silence
never came and the only trace there has ever been was the forty-five
second deadline's.  It is v86_wtick.  The same kernel, one HELLO.COM
and a prompt: the trace was written at tick 334h, and is written at
5Bh now.  This was true of the tree before the bus work as well.

And RMXMS.INC's pf_out is a label RMNAME.INC has had since the write
path was repaired.  It is inside XMSPOOLSTAMP, so BUILD lpt and lptfrz
would have stopped there if they had got that far, and BUILD stamp and
stampfrz did stop there.  It is pfs_out.

2.  A CLIENT'S OWN HANDLERS (DPMI.INC, "A CLIENT'S OWN HANDLERS, AND
WHAT IS THERE WHEN IT HAS NONE").  What was left was one defect.  It
was four:

  - THE HANDLER HAD NO FRAME.  dre_client pointed the host's return
    at the handler and pushed nothing, so the handler's IRET took
    three words of whatever the client had last pushed.  dpmi_enter
    puts the address and the flags on the client's stack first.
  - 0204h ANSWERED THE FIRST INSTRUCTION OF THE CLIENT: its own code
    selector and offset zero, for every vector nobody had set.  A
    handler passes on what it does not want, to the address it was
    given, and that restarted the program.  There is a table of
    defaults now (DPMI_IDX_DEFVEC, selector 0047h): 256 two-byte
    entries, each an INT 31h, and the host knows the vector from
    where it was called.  The first selector 0000h hands out is 004Fh
    and was 0047h.
  - INT n ON ANY VECTOR WITHOUT A GATE KILLED THE CLIENT.  Ring 3 may
    use the gates for 10h to 17h, 1Ah, 21h, 2Fh, 31h and 33h; an INT
    60h is a general protection fault, PMIO had nothing to emulate,
    and the DOS side was told a client had died.  dpmi_fault looks at
    the instruction first (dpmi_swint).  IOS_PM3HOOK MAY RETURN NOW,
    which it never did, and PMIO resumes the client through the frame
    it handed over; the four segment registers exc_common keeps are
    saved round the call, because a DOS box runs inside it.
  - A HANDLER ON INT 21h OR INT 31h WAS NEVER CALLED.  Both gates go
    to the host.  Both ask dpmi_enter first now.  Their defaults
    cannot be an INT 31h the host would take for the default again,
    so they send the client to two pairs behind the table: the
    interrupt itself, executed from there, then an INT 31h that hands
    the answer to whoever was waiting.

What a default does when it is reached is run the interrupt in real
mode and then return through the frame the handler was given
(dpmi_leave) - which is an IRET the client could not have done for
itself.  At ring 3 an IRET leaves the interrupt flag alone, and the
one a client believes in is a byte of PMIO's; the host puts it back
to what the frame says.  IOS_BUSINIT answers with that byte's
address.

THE FLAGS GO IN AS WELL AS COMING OUT.  The first version ran the
real-mode handler with no flags and gave the client the ones it came
back with, which is right for a service and wrong for an interrupt
nobody called.  DPMIVEC's handler on the clock's interrupt passes
every one of them on, and counted 31 in a second where DPMIIRQ counts
61.  Nothing was lost.  The second was short: the loop that waits for
the BIOS's clock to move sits between a compare and a jump, came back
from an interrupt with real mode's flags, and left the loop.  Real
mode is handed the caller's flags and what it hands back is what the
handler did to them.  And all six come back - the reflector kept the
carry flag and nothing else, so INT 16h AH=01h could not say whether
there was a key.

0205h refuses a selector that is not code (8022h), and given a
vector's default back it means no handler.  INT 2Fh AX=1686h is still
answered by the host, after the client's own handler on 2Fh and not
before it.

3.  WHAT WAS UNDER IT.

A HUNDRED CALLS TO THE BIOS.  Every interrupt run in real mode for a
client is a DOS box started on the host's ring-0 stack, and v86_run
points TSS_ESP0 at its own frame.  Nothing pointed it back.  The
client's next call came in where that frame had been, its next
simulated interrupt went lower still, and the stack walked down
through eight kilobytes into the TSS.  DPMIVEC on the kernel as it
was gets through 80 calls to INT 10h and not through 120; a program
that reads the keyboard through INT 16h makes that many in seconds.
dpmi_simint keeps the pointer and dpmi_rmdone puts it back.

THE SECOND DPMI PROGRAM SINCE BOOT.  0002h keeps the selector it made
for a segment, and kept it for the next client, whose descriptor
table is a new one.  DPMIVEC run after DPMIIRQ asked for the BIOS
data area, was given the selector DPMIIRQ had had, and faulted
loading it.  And the vectors a client had set were still set for the
next.  A new client starts with neither.

A 32-BIT CLIENT, WHICH NOTHING IN THE TREE HAD EVER BEEN.  The switch
gave it a 32-bit code segment.  It returns to the instruction after a
far call made in real mode, which is 16-bit code, and the
specification gives every client a 16-bit CS for that reason.  And A
HANDLER'S FRAME IS AS WIDE AS THE CLIENT, not as wide as the
handler's segment: an extender is a 32-bit client with 16-bit
segments of its own, and its handlers in them end with an IRETD.
That changes what the entry above says of vpc_pmchk, which went by
the segment.  IOS_BUSINIT is told where the host keeps the client's
size.

WHAT IT COST.  PMIO's body is 33,396 bytes, 78 more.  PMDOS.SYS is
191,387, 1,422 more, and has 5,221 left.  No conventional memory.

WHAT A PROGRAM WILL SEE THAT IT DID NOT.  Selectors from 0000h and
0002h are 8 higher.  A 32-bit client's first code segment is 16-bit.
0204h on an unset vector answers 0047h and twice the vector.  0205h
can fail.  Flags other than carry come back from an interrupt run in
real mode.

TRAPS MET.
  - wasm reports a jump out of range AT THE LABEL, not at the jump.
    Seven jumps go to pm3_done with SHORT written on them and the
    message named none.  Taking the word off each in turn found it.
  - DOSBox-X's log of port E9h is a line at a time: nothing is
    written until a line feed is.  A marker is two bytes.
  - A test that dies with its output redirected leaves no file, and
    the kernel as it was left DOSBox-X deaf to its own time limit.
    What it got as far as was found with copies of the test cut off
    after each check.
  - DPMITEST wants ARGS.COM and HOOKTEST.COM in the current
    directory.  Without them it reports two failures that are not
    the host's.

VERIFIED.  DOSBox-X, headless.  DPMIVEC and DPMIV32, 14 of 14 each:
a thousand calls to INT 10h and a thousand to a vector with no gate,
a handler that answers and one that passes on, INT 21h, 10h and 31h
through handlers with the stack where it was afterwards, the clock's
interrupt passed on to real mode 60 times in a second, and half a
second between a compare and a jump with thirty of them arriving.
DPMII32 8 of 8.  Each after the other and twice over, which is what
found 0002h.  On the kernel as it was the second check ends the
machine; on this one before the flags went in, the last two fail.
The whole regression against the run in the entry above: every
difference is a size, a count of interrupts or a new test.

86Box, TOOLS\BUS86.PS1, the same three boards: all eight programs
pass on all three.

The trace kernel writes its trace, with DPMIVEC's 199Bh traps in it.
Every lpt target, stamp, stampfrz, watch, watchq, trace, kbio, debug

NOT VERIFIED.  Real hardware.  AN EXTENDER - DOS/4GW, DOS/32A, any of

  - 0202h and 0203h, a client's own handlers for exceptions.  The

NINE BUFFERS OUT OF PMDOS.SYS, AND SIXTY-NINE KILOBYTES TO GROW
INTO (2026-09-27)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The entry above left PMDOS.SYS 5,221 bytes short of the shell's slot.
It is 127,491 bytes now and has 69,117 left.  No routine in it was
rewritten: nine buffers are somewhere else, and the link puts them
there.  Still v0.60.

WHAT HAPPENS PAST 196,608 BYTES.  The build stops, at FSIZE, and that
is all that does.  load_dos copies the file by its cluster chain and
compares its length with nothing.  The four kilobytes after DOS_LIMIT
are the guard page at the foot of the shell's slot, which is not
present, and the rest is where CMD.EXE goes: a kernel that long would
fault on its own tail or have it loaded over.  Read, not run.

WHAT THE FILE WAS MADE OF.  100,535 of its 191,387 bytes were in runs
of 256 zeros or more.  wlink's map names only what is PUBLIC, so a
copy of DOSMAIN.ASM was made that declares every data label public,
and it linked to the same bytes as the kernel.  The large ones:

    clus_buf    32,768      sft_tbl       3,840
    cfg_buf     16,385      cache_hash    3,080
    fat_buf      8,192      iso_buf, iso_cebuf, udf_fbuf, img_sbuf,
    udf_dbuf     4,096      cdx_buf and dpmi_pmvec, 2,048 each
    exec_env     3,840

WHAT MOVED is the ones that are buffers and nothing else: sec_buf,
clus_buf, cfg_buf, iso_buf, iso_cebuf, udf_dbuf, udf_fbuf, img_sbuf
and cdx_buf.  64,001 bytes.

WHAT DID NOT.  fat_buf and fatsec_buf are 8,704 bytes of exactly that
kind and are INSIDE vol_state, which is copied whole to the arena and
back whenever the volume changes.  They look like the others in a
listing of zeros and are not.  The tables were left alone: there is
room now, and a table has a shape somebody may be counting on.

HOW.  Not the way the trace's buffers went.  Those became equates and
every line that named one was edited; these are named in two hundred
lines.  They are in a segment of their own, _KBSS, in one group with
the code, and the link is told where each class goes:

    wlink form raw bin ... order clname CODE offset=0x110000
                                 clname KBSS offset=0x269000

wlink's raw output stops at the last byte that has a value, which was
a trap for CHKDSK and is the whole mechanism here: a segment of
"dup(?)" costs the file nothing wherever it is put.  A label in it is
still a label and still has a size, so "mov al,[sec_buf+BPB_MEDIA]"
assembles as it did.  A file that has a buffer closes _DOS, declares
it in _KBSS, and opens _DOS again.

KBSS_BASE is PG_TOP, 269000h, and KBSS_LEN is 64K, of which 1,532
bytes are not used.  THE ARENA STARTS 64K HIGHER, at 279000h.  In a
kernel built to trace DBG_MEM follows the buffers and the arena
starts at 283000h.  KBUF_HI3 is ARENA_BASE, so buf_ok refuses a
caller's pointer into them as it did when they were in the file.

dos_entry clears them before it does anything else, since nothing
loads them.  It is 44 bytes; kbss_lost and its message are 61.

FOUR THINGS THAT CAN GO WRONG, and what stops each.

  - THE LINK AND PMDOS.INC DISAGREE.  0x269000 is in BUILD.CMD as a
    number and KBSS_BASE is an equate, and nothing at build time can
    compare them.  dos_entry does, and says "PMDOS.SYS: linked for
    the wrong KBSS address" and halts.  Run: a kernel linked a page
    out prints that and nothing after it.
  - MORE THAN KBSS_LEN.  The end of DOSMAIN.ASM will not assemble,
    and dos_entry checks the length as well.
  - SOMETHING WITH A VALUE IN _KBSS.  The link then writes every
    byte between the code and it, and the file is 1.4MB, which FSIZE
    refuses.  THAT IS WHY "noemit" IS NOT ON THE LINK LINE: with it
    the value is dropped, the file is the right size, and the
    variable starts at zero with nothing said.
  - A BUFFER ON AN ODD ADDRESS.  ata_dmaok sends a transfer to an
    odd address by PIO.  Each piece of _KBSS ends on a dword or does
    not assemble; cfg_buf is 16,385 bytes and has three after it.
    Not ALIGN, which writes its padding and so gives it a value.

THE 64K LINE.  A bus master's transfer is described in regions that
may not cross one, and ata_prdbuild cuts a buffer at each.  Where
clus_buf was, 1145B0h to 11C5B0h, it crossed none - by luck; nothing
said so.  Put first in _KBSS it would have crossed 270000h, 28K in.
The driver cuts a program's own buffers all day and would have cut
this one, but the kernel's cluster buffer had never been cut, and
moving a buffer was not the day to find out.  So it is in _KBSS2, a
second segment of the same class, which comes last: 270A04h to
278A04h.  DOSMAIN.ASM will not assemble if it crosses.

TRAPS MET.
  - "option offset" IS IGNORED ONCE "order" IS ON THE LINE.  The
    first attempt kept both and linked the code at zero.  The
    code's address is the first offset in the order.
  - wasm's .ERR prints "forced error:" and the line number.  The
    text after it is for whoever reads the source.
  - A LABEL MINUS A LABEL IN ANOTHER SEGMENT ASSEMBLES, AND IS WRONG.
    Each is counted from the start of its own segment: clus_buf
    minus kbss_start is zero.  So the two segments are measured
    apart, each between labels of its own, and added.
  - FATGET.PL is for text: it turns CR LF into LF.  A kernel read
    back through it is not the kernel.  Whether a file is on an
    image was settled by looking for its bytes there.

WHAT IT COST.  64K of extended memory, on every machine: MEM says
1,508K reserved where it said 1,444K.  No conventional memory.
PMIO.SYS and RMDOS.SYS are byte for byte what they were.

WHAT A PROGRAM WILL SEE.  64K less extended memory, and 52h's first
arena header 64K higher.  Nothing else.

VERIFIED.

The link alone, with nothing moved, gave the kernel that was: the
same 191,387 bytes.

THE NEW KERNEL IS THE OLD ONE AND THE MOVE.  A script (reloc.pl, in
the scratchpad, not kept) walked the two images together, skipping
what was taken out and what was put in, and required every byte that
differed to be part of an address that the move accounts for.
106,507 bytes are the same; 4,736 addresses and 561 distances
changed to what they should be; 12 are ARENA_BASE; NONE IS
UNEXPLAINED.  All 789 labels the two maps share are where the move
puts them, and what was taken out was all zeros.

Both assembly checks fail four bytes past their limits and pass at
them.  All 43 sets of switches BUILD.CMD knows assemble and fit.

DOSBox-X, headless.  The whole regression against the run in the
entry above, bus tests included: 32 lines of 5,239 differ, and they
are the 64K, addresses 64K higher, the kernel's size in a DIR, a
temporary file's name and one count in CACHETST that has been 4 or 5
in every run there is.  The printer's half is the same bytes.

The three CD readers, which no regression runs: four discs through
MOUNT (Joliet, Rock Ridge twice, UDF), each listed and copied off
with XCOPY, on the kernel that was and on this one.  The same 181
lines, and the files copied are the same bytes.  A CONFIG.SYS of 20K
with a SET inside the first 16K and one past it: the first is set
and the second is not, on both.

A kernel built to trace writes its trace.

86Box, p3bf, cuv4xls and vs440fx, with IDEDMA=ON and a disc in an
ATAPI drive: IDETEST passes with the disk and the drive both moving
data by bus master, CDXTEST's nine answers are right, and the disc
lists and copies.  On p3bf the kernel that was gives the same output
but for the checksum, which covers the FAT and so the kernel's
length.  TOOLS\BUS86.PS1: all eight programs pass on all three.

Both HD16 images refreshed in place, HD32 made again, and the floppy
copied to the VM.  A copy of HD16 passes DPMITEST and BUSTEST from
its own files and CHKDSK finds nothing; a copy of HD32 boots to a
prompt.

NOT VERIFIED.  Real hardware.  A volume with clusters of 32K, which
is the only thing that fills clus_buf: every disk here has clusters
of 1K or 2K.  A machine with less than 2.5MB, where the buffers are
memory that is not there - it had no arena before, either.

NOT DONE.  load_dos still loads a kernel of any length.  IOPM.ASM
already refuses one of length zero, just before it jumps to it, and
the same place could refuse one past DOS_LIMIT.  It would change
PMIO.SYS, which this did not.

STILL ZEROS IN THE FILE.  About 36K: fat_buf and fatsec_buf, which
cannot go; exec_env, sft_tbl and cache_hash, 10,760 between them,
which could; and tables of two kilobytes and less.

THE COPROCESSOR, MMX AND SSE: AN ERROR THAT ARRIVES, A BIT ONLY RING 0
CAN SET, AND A CHILD THAT CLEARS UP AFTER ITSELF (2026-09-27)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The question was whether an operating system has to save and restore
the processor's registers, and whether PM-DOS should do something
about MMX and the rest.  A system that switches between tasks has to.
PM-DOS runs one program at a time and executes no floating-point
instruction of its own, so there was nothing to save and MMX already
worked - it lives in the coprocessor's registers and was designed to
need nothing.  Three smaller things were missing, and they are in.
Still v0.60.

1. THE COPROCESSOR'S ERROR ARRIVES.  A program that unmasks divide-by-
zero expects to be told, on INT 75h, because the board wires the
coprocessor's error pin to interrupt line 13.  Line 13 was masked and
nothing else had been asked for, so the error went nowhere.

IO\FPU.INC, new, sets NE in CR0 on a 486 or later (EFLAGS.AC can be
changed), which makes the error exception 16.  From there:

  - A DOS BOX is given INT 75h through its own table (vfe_fperr in
    VM86.INC), at once, whatever its interrupt flag and mask say: the
    instruction it stands on cannot run until the error is dealt with.
    Line 13 and the cascade are marked in service in the box's 8259s
    if the box has hooked the vector, so that the two EOIs its handler
    sends end that interrupt and not some other (vpc_fptake).
  - A DPMI CLIENT gets it on the handler 0205h put on INT 75h, and on
    the real-mode one if it has none (dfa_fperr in DPMI.INC).
  - A NATIVE PROGRAM is ended: "Program fault: exception 10 ... -
    floating point".  It has nowhere to be handed it.

A 386 has no NE.  There line 13 is opened and is the kernel's
(fpu_line), and irq_common turns the interrupt into the same exception
on its way out - unless it interrupted the kernel, in which case it
waits for an interrupt that finds the program outside a call.  BUILD
fpuirq makes any machine do it that way.

2. SSE IS SWITCHED ON.  With OSFXSR clear in CR4 every SSE instruction
is an invalid opcode, and a DOS box or a DPMI client cannot set it.
fpu_init does, if CPUID has FXSR.  OSXMMEXCPT is left CLEAR: set, an
SSE error a program unmasked is exception 19, and vector 13h is the
disk BIOS.  Clear, it is an invalid opcode - INT 06h to a box, the end
of anything else.

3. A WAITING PROGRAM'S STATE IS KEPT.  EXEC is the one place a second
program runs in front of a first.  DOS\FPSTATE.INC keeps the parent's
state when a child starts and puts it back when the child ends, and
the child starts with a fresh one.  A slot a nesting level: exec_stk's
depth for a native program, FPS_BOX + vdm_stack's for a DOS one, so
fn4B/fn4C and vdm_push/vdm_pop are the only four places that had to
know, and every way out - ^C, a fault, an Abort - passes one of them.
Sixteen slots of 512 bytes, out of the arena at boot, and none on a
machine with no coprocessor.  PMIO does the keeping (IOS_FPU), with
FXSAVE where there is one and FNSAVE where there is not.

DOS does none of this.  A child there gets its parent's state and the
parent gets the child's back.

21h/F1h AL=13h answers the FPUF_* flags: is there a coprocessor, may
SSE be used, how errors arrive.  CR0 and CR4 say it and ring 3 can
read neither.

PARKED, THE MACHINE IS AS THE BIOS LEFT IT.  rm_park puts CR0's four
coprocessor bits and CR4 back to what they were at boot, and the
state away; coming back undoes both (fpu_park, fpu_unpark).  Windows
and every DOS extender look for the error on line 13.

THE BUG WORTH THE ENTRY: VECTOR 10h IS TWO THINGS.  Intel reserved it
for the coprocessor's error and IBM gave it to the video BIOS.  The
DPMI host has a gate on 10h that ring 3 may call, put there through
IOS_SETVEC over the exception's.  So the first kernel with NE in it
sent a program's divide-by-zero to dpmi_reflect, which said "protected-
mode interrupt with no client: 10" and returned to the instruction
that had faulted, for ever.  DOSBox-X could not show it (below); the
first run on 86Box was a screen of that line.

The gate is FPU.INC's now (fpu_gate), and what the DOS side asks
IOS_SETVEC to put on vector 10h is kept and jumped to.  An arrival
from a DOS box or from ring 0 is the error.  From ring 3 with nothing
outstanding in the status word it is a call.  With something
outstanding the instruction decides: CD 10 before the stacked address
and no coprocessor instruction at it is a call.  The one case that can
be read either way - an INT 10h made with an error outstanding and a
coprocessor instruction straight after it - is read as the error,
which costs that program one call; read the other way it would be a
call made for ever.

11h to 17h have the same gates and no exception behind them that can
happen here: 17 needs AM in CR0, 18 needs MCE in CR4, and 19 is why
OSXMMEXCPT is clear.

A HANDLER THAT CLEARS NOTHING is stopped at again the moment it
returns.  vf_exc counts thirty-two identical faults for vectors 0 to
7; for this one it is TIMED - two seconds of this error at this
address and no call to DOS - because the error is reported at the
instruction after the one that caused it, and a loop that overflows on
every turn with a handler that copes faults at one address as often as
it likes.  The box ends with "stuck on its own handler for vector 75".

TWO THINGS ABOUT THE EMULATORS, both found by running the same program
with no PM-DOS under it.

  - DOSBox-X's COPROCESSOR NEVER REPORTS AN ERROR.  One over nought
    with divide-by-zero unmasked is infinity, under its own DOS as
    much as here.  The tests read the status word before the FWAIT: a
    coprocessor with an error to report has its summary bit set, and
    on one that has not the checks are passed over and say so.
  - 86Box WITHOUT fpu_softfloat LEAVES THE TOP OF STACK OUT OF WHAT
    FXSAVE WRITES.  The status word in the image is 0000 where FNSTSW
    says 3000, and a state put back from it has its registers and has
    forgotten which is the top.  fpv_keep follows FXSAVE with an
    FNSTSW into the image, which on a processor writes the bytes that
    are already there.  That FPU reports no errors either; with
    fpu_softfloat = 1 it does both properly.

THE TESTS, all built by BUILD.CMD (with -fpi87: without it wasm writes
a coprocessor instruction as a fixup for an emulator library) and on
every image:

    FPUTEST.COM     a DOS box: ten checks.  /C is its own child.  /S
                    is the handler that clears nothing
    FPU32.EXE       a native program: nine, with a native child and a
                    DOS one.  /F is the error nobody masked
    DPMIFPU.COM     a DPMI client's handler, and the real-mode one
    DPMIFP32.COM    the same as a 32-bit client
    DISK\FPUTEST.BAT    all of them
    TOOLS\FPU86.PS1     the 86Box rig: -Machine, -SoftFloat, -Kernel,
                        -Shot for the screen

WHAT IT COST.  PMIO's body is 34,978 bytes, 1,582 more.  PMDOS.SYS is
128,024, 533 more, with 68,584 left.  8K of extended memory on a
machine with a coprocessor.  RMDOS.SYS is byte for byte what it was.

VERIFIED.

86Box with fpu_softfloat = 1, p3bf (Pentium II: MMX, FXSAVE), cuv4xls
(Celeron) and vs440fx (Pentium Pro: neither, so FNSAVE): every check
of all four programs, the error delivered once with ZE in the status
word; FPU32 /F ended with the message above; FPUTEST /S ended its box
after two seconds; FPUTEST passes again afterwards.  The same on p3bf
with the kernel from BUILD fpuirq, which says 53h where the other says
33h.  With fpu_softfloat = 0 everything that does not need an error
passes, check 9 because of the FNSTSW.

DOSBox-X, headless: cputype 386 (the kernel chooses line 13 by
itself), 486, auto and pentium_iii.  On the last, SSE runs in a box, a
native program and both clients, and MXCSR comes back across a child.
THE KERNEL THAT WAS, on the same disk: SSE is an invalid opcode, a
child is not fresh and the parent's control word is the child's.

The whole regression against the kernel that was: 52 lines of 5,080
differ, and they are the 8K, the block it is in, the kernel's size
and five more files on the disk.  The printer's half, which is RMDOS
and two parks, is the same bytes.  All 44 sets of switches assemble
and fit.  SYMCASE.PL finds nothing.

Both HD16 images refreshed in place, HD32 made again, the floppy
copied to the VM.  A copy of HD16 passes FPUTEST.BAT, APITEST and
DPMITEST from its own files and CHKDSK finds nothing; a FAT32 disk
made from the same files boots and passes FPUTEST and FPU32.

NOT VERIFIED.  Real hardware.  A REAL 386 WITH A 387: the line-13 path
has run only as BUILD fpuirq on a Pentium II, where CR0 has an NE to
clear.  A machine with no coprocessor at all.  SSE and the error in
one run - no emulator here has both.  A real run-time library's
handler, or a real extender's.  Windows, parked, using the
coprocessor.

NOT DONE.  INT 31h 0E00h and 0E01h, DPMI 1.0's coprocessor status: no
0.9 client asks.  0202h and 0203h are still not there, so a client's
error is an interrupt and never an exception.  AVX wants XSAVE and a
processor nothing here will ever run on.

WHAT A REAL MACHINE SAID THIS TIME: NO C:, AND DIR/W IS A BAD COMMAND
(2026-09-27)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The floppy went into a real machine whose hard disk is FAT16 with
MS-DOS 6.22 on it, and two things came back.  "C:" said "Invalid drive
specification".  "DIR/W" was a bad command, where "DIR /W" worked.
Still v0.60.

THE SECOND ONE FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS UNDERSTOOD.

CMD.EXE's verb scanner ended a verb at a '/' only when a '?' followed,
for the sake of "C:/TESTS/APITEST.COM".  COMMAND.COM has always ended
one at any '/', as 6.22 does, which is why C16TEST never saw it.  The
scan still runs on past a '/', so the path still works, but where the
first one stood is kept (verb_slash) and two places go back to it:

  - tbl_prefix, when no row of the command table IS the verb.  A row
    whose name is the front of it, with '/' next, is that command and
    its arguments start at the '/'.  For the rows flagged CF_PREFIX -
    DIR, CD, CHDIR, MD, MKDIR, RD, RMDIR, COMMAND.COM's own list - a
    '.' or a '\' does as well: CD.., CD\DOS, DIR\TESTS.
  - ext_fail, when nothing is called that as a path or as a name.
    The name in front of the slash is tried, once, with the rest as
    its tail - and the tail has no blank in front of it (tail_glued),
    because DOS hands "MEM/C" its "/C" that way.

So a path with forward slashes is tried as typed FIRST and the DOS
reading second.  "DIR/W" with a directory called DIR and a program W
in it lists the directory; that is DOS's answer too.

AND ONE NOBODY REPORTED, found by testing the first: a switch in FRONT
of the name found no files.  "DIR /W *.TXT" - which is where most
people type it - left sw_scan's caller with " *.TXT", and a pattern
that begins with a blank matches nothing.  sw_scan trimmed what the
removal left at the end and never at the front.  DIRTEST puts every
switch after the name, so it passed.  DEL is the other caller.

DISK\GLUETEST.BAT is all of it, on every image and in AUTOEXEC.BAT's
list.

THE FIRST ONE IS NOT DIAGNOSED.  WHAT FOLLOWS IS THE LIKELIEST CAUSE
AND WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT, AND THE MACHINE HAS NOT SAID YES.

What the symptom pins down: no critical error and no "invalid media",
so there was no letter to mount - disk_scan read the partition table
and found no volume in it.  ds_mbr is silent on purpose.  And a disk
the IDE probe has claimed is never handed to the BIOS instead, so a
read that goes wrong there is final.

What has changed in that read since a real machine last confirmed a
C: (v0.40, 2026-08-26) is v0.43: bus-master DMA, which falls back, and
32-BIT PIO, WHICH DOES NOT AND CANNOT TELL.  IDE32=AUTO believed
IDENTIFY word 48.  That word is the DRIVE's account of itself, and the
question is about the HOST: on an ISA or a plain VLB card a doubleword
read of 1F0h is two word reads, of 1F0h and of 1F2h, and every other
word of the sector is the sector count register.  No error.  A
mid-nineties drive sets the bit whatever it is plugged into.

DOSBox-X's IDE is such a host, which nobody knew because nothing there
sets word 48: the kernel that was, with IDE32=ON, stops at "C:".  And
a kernel that takes every drive as a candidate and believes it (BUILD
trust32, below) gives, on that host, EXACTLY the report - no C:,
"Invalid drive specification", nothing else on the screen.

WHAT WAS DONE.

  - ata_prove32 (ATA.INC).  Under AUTO a candidate is asked for its
    IDENTIFY block again, the block is taken a doubleword at a time,
    and ATDF_PIO32 stays only if it is the same 512 bytes the probe
    had just read a word at a time.  ata_pick32 said this could not be
    measured; it can, given something there is another copy of.  What
    a halving host leaves in the drive is drained, or the next command
    is written to a drive still waiting to be read.  IDE32=ON is not
    measured: it is an instruction.
  - ATI_NO32 (08h, PMDOS.INC) says it was tried and refused, and
    IDETEST prints "(32-bit tried, host cannot)" beside the disk.
    THAT LINE ON THE REAL MACHINE IS THE CONFIRMATION, and its absence
    with C: still missing means the cause is something else.
  - disk_rescan (FAT.INC), through cfg_atacfg (CONFIG.INC).  IDE32=OFF
    and IDEDMA=OFF are the escape hatches for a machine that reads a
    disk wrongly, and on that machine the scan had already found
    nothing before CONFIG.SYS was opened - so the one line meant for
    it could not give it a C:.  After any of the three IDE statements
    the partition tables are read again, but only if no partition has
    a letter: a table with one in it is left alone.  The CD-ROMs step
    aside and are placed again after (drv_dropcds, out of drv_addcds).
    sec_lba is thrown away, because this time a volume is mounted and
    the passes read into sec_buf.

BUILD.CMD has three more:

    BUILD ataq      the probe trace on a release boot.  BUILD ata
                    reads CONFIG.SYS out loud and scrolls it away
    BUILD eager32   every drive is a candidate, and is proved
    BUILD trust32   every drive is a candidate, and is believed -
                    the kernel that was, on a drive that sets word 48

TOOLS\DBXRUN.PS1 has -Floppy: boot from A: with -Hd as the machine's
C:, and read what the guest wrote to A: with FLOPGET.PL.

IMAGES\PMDOSATA.IMG is a BUILD ataq floppy, for the machine.  Its
second line, four times over, a slot each:

    +0A0000410010003F/00000006=0000
    | |   |   |   |    |   | |  what a refused IDENTIFY signed
    | |   |   |   |    |   | ATD_FLAGS: 10h = 32-bit PIO in use
    | |   |   |   |    |   ATD_ID: 08h = tried and refused
    | |   |   |   |    word 48: 0001 = the drive says doubleword
    | |   |   |   sectors per track
    | |   |   heads
    | |   cylinders
    | word 49: 0200h = LBA
    '+' a disk; any other letter is where the probe stopped

and "LBA0 sig=" ends in AA55 when sector 0 was read, and is "!" when
it could not be.

WHAT IT COST.  PMIO's body is 35,655 bytes, 677 more, 512 of them the
second block.  PMDOS.SYS is 128,172, 148 more.  CMD.EXE is 59,896,
247 more.

VERIFIED, all headless in DOSBox-X, booted FROM THE FLOPPY with a copy
of HD16.IMG attached - which is what the machine did and what no run
before today had done.

GLUETEST, every line.  The release kernel: C: mounts, IDETEST nine of
nine.  BUILD eager32: the same, and IDETEST says the host cannot.
BUILD trust32: no C:, "Invalid drive specification"; with IDE32=OFF as
the last line of CONFIG.SYS, C: is there.  The whole regression
against the kernel that was, run side by side: 12 lines of 5,082
differ, and they are three file sizes, two totals and a temporary
file's name.  IMAGES\HD16.IMG and the VM's refreshed in place, HD32
made again, the floppy copied to the VM; a copy of each hard disk
boots to a prompt.

NOT VERIFIED.  REAL HARDWARE, which is the only place any of the disk
half means anything.  THE MACHINE, as Charlie described it afterwards:
a 486 DX4 at 100MHz, ISA SLOTS ONLY, the disk on the one IDE header on
the board.  That is a host with no way to latch a doubleword, which is
the host this entry is about - but what the drive says in word 48 is
still not known here, and IDETEST on that machine is what says.  A host that
passes the proof and still reads a sector wrongly.  The rescan with a
block driver loaded before the IDE statement.

ONE THING LEFT AS IT IS.  After trust32's halved reads the re-probe
that IDE32=OFF causes does not find the disk - it was left waiting to
be read - and C: comes back through the BIOS.  It works, and a release
kernel drains the drive before it can get there.

AND TWO THINGS ABOUT BOOTING FROM THE FLOPPY that the machine will
meet next.  AUTOEXEC.BAT's PATH names C:\TESTS, so from A:\ a test
does not run by bare name - CD \TESTS, or PATH A:\TESTS;A:\ - and if
the machine's C: has an older \TESTS on it, those are the ones that
run.  CONFIG.SYS sets TEMP=C:\TEMP.


A BOOT SAYS WHAT THE MACHINE HAS: THE MOUSE, AND THE CD-ROM'S LETTER
(2026-09-27)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The rule was that a release boot says one line.  Charlie changed it:
a line for the mouse if there is one, a line for a CD-ROM drive and
its letter if there is one, and nothing for either on a machine
without.  Still v0.60.

    Starting PM-DOS...
    Mouse detected on PS/2
    CD-ROM drive detected as D:

THE MOUSE is ms_announce (MOUSE.INC), called by pm_entry after ms_init
and not from inside it.  "PS/2", or "COM1" or "COM2": ms_serfind
writes the digit, from which of the BIOS's port words it was trying.
It is PMIO's line and comes before PMDOS.SYS is started.

THE CD-ROM is cd_announce (FAT.INC), called once after config_run and
above shell_restart.  AFTER CONFIG.SYS, because CDROM= moves the
letter and disk_rescan can; a line printed by disk_scan would have
named a letter the drive did not keep.  A line for each drive.  It is
the DRIVE that is announced: the letter is there with the tray empty.
A slot that is also DRVF_IMAGE is passed over - an .ISO given a letter
by MOUNT is a file.

CONFIG.SYS's own silence is what it was.  Neither line is a statement
being read out.

WHAT IT COST.  PMIO's body is 35,755 bytes, 100 more.  PMDOS.SYS is
128,262, 90 more.

VERIFIED, DOSBox-X headless, from the floppy, off the screen (-Cap and
ZMBVSHOT.PL).  A PS/2 mouse: "PS/2".  [keyboard] aux=false and
serial2=serialmouse: "COM2".  aux=false alone: no line.  A hard disk
and a disc on the secondary master ("imgmount y: X.ISO -t iso -ide
2m", before the boot): "D:", and DIR D:\ lists it.  The same with
CDROM=M as the last line of CONFIG.SYS: "M:".  No hard disk: "C:".
No drive: no line.  The whole regression against the run in the entry
above, the clock's minutes apart: 10 lines of 5,082 differ, and they
are PMDOS.SYS's size, CONFIG.SYS's, two totals and a temporary file's
name.

NOT VERIFIED.  Real hardware.  TWO DRIVES, which should be two lines:
DOSBox-X did not show the kernel a second one on "-ide 2s".

THE SECOND REPORT FROM THE 486: NO MOUSE, NO CD-ROM, AND A FORMAT
THAT COULD NOT MAKE A DISKETTE (2026-09-27)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The floppy went back to the machine.  C: IS THERE NOW, which is the
entry before last confirmed as far as it can be from here: nobody ran
IDETEST, so that the cause was the 32-bit read is still the likeliest
thing and not a known one.  Three more things came back with it.  The
PS/2 mouse was not found.  The CD-ROM drive was not found.  FORMAT
wants /U, /F, /B and /C.  And the PATH is to name A:\ and nothing
else.  Still v0.60.

NEITHER PROBE FAILURE IS EXPLAINED, and that has to be said first.
Both probes find their device on DOSBox-X and on 86Box, before these
changes and after them.  What was done is what can be done without
the machine: each probe was read against what real hardware is known
to do that an emulator does not, the three places that turned up were
changed, and BOTH PROBES NOW WRITE DOWN WHAT THEY READ, so that the
next report is a screen of numbers and not "it was not found".

THE MOUSE (MOUSE.INC, ms_ps2start and ms_kbcaux).

  A9h WAS THE GATE AND ITS ANSWER HAD TO BE ZERO.  That is the
  controller's test of its second port, and real controllers answer
  it with an error on a port that works - Linux's i8042 driver says
  so in a comment and asks it only when everything else has failed.
  The gate is now the one Linux uses: bit 5 of the command byte is
  the port's disable, A7h sets it and A8h clears it, and on a
  controller with no second port neither command means anything and
  the bit stays where it was.  A9h is asked only if the bit did not
  follow, and FAh counts as working.

  THE MOUSE CANNOT SPEAK WHILE THAT IS ASKED, because A7h stops its
  clock.  So the answers are read by ms_kbcany, which takes the next
  byte whoever the status register says sent it; ms_kbcreply, which
  throws away a byte flagged as the mouse's, is what the old gate
  read with, and a controller that flags its own answers that way
  would have been refused by it.

  ONE RESET AND A SECOND TO ANSWER IT became two resets and two and a
  half seconds each, and a third of a second for an acknowledge where
  there was a sixth.  The ID byte after the self-test is waited for
  and not insisted on.

THE CD-ROM (ATA.INC, ata_identify; ATAPI.INC, atapi_ident).

  A STATUS OF ZERO AFTER IDENTIFY MEANT NO DEVICE, read once, four
  port reads after the command.  Zero is also what a packet device
  idles at, and an old drive is a processor that has to notice the
  command before it can raise BSY.  ata_wake reads until the status
  is something else or 20,000 reads have all been zero.

  NO SIGNATURE MEANT NOT A PACKET DEVICE.  14h/EBh in the cylinder
  registers after a refused IDENTIFY DEVICE is what the standard asks
  for, and drives from before the standard refuse and sign nothing.
  A device that refuses with no signature is now asked IDENTIFY
  PACKET DEVICE anyway, and taken for a packet device if it answers
  with bits 15 and 14 of word 0 saying it is one.  A disk refuses at
  once.  The wait is ata_probedrq, which gives up after two million
  reads where ata_waitdrq takes sixteen.

  TWO CHANNELS BECAME FOUR.  1F0h and 170h are the board's; 1E8h and
  168h are where a sound card's CD-ROM connector or an add-in card
  answers when those are taken, and on a 486 with one IDE header that
  is a likely place for the drive to be.  ATA_MAXDEV is 8, ata_ports
  is the table, ata_cbl has a byte for each of four channels, and
  ata_pickbm gives a bus-master engine to the two channels a PCI host
  has and to no other.  F1h AL=0Ah takes a device index up to 7, and
  IDETEST asks all eight.

  WHAT IT CANNOT FIND is a drive that is not ATAPI - the Panasonic,
  Mitsumi and Sony interfaces on a sound card are not IDE at all -
  and a Plug and Play card's connector that nothing has switched on,
  which on a machine with no PnP BIOS is a driver's job under DOS.

THE LOG (PROBELOG.INC, new; IOS_PROBELOG; 21h/F1h AL=15h).  128 bytes.
The mouse's sixteen: the last step begun, as a letter; the command
byte as the BIOS left it, after A7h and after A8h; A9h's answer if it
was asked; what the reset, the self-test, the ID and F4h were answered
with; the BIOS's equipment byte.  Then twelve for each of the eight
IDE positions: the port, how far ata_identify got, ATD_FLAGS, the
status register before anything was written, after the select, after
IDENTIFY and after IDENTIFY PACKET, the signature and the error
register.  A bit says which were read.

\TESTS\HWPROBE prints it.  This is what the floppy says on DOSBox-X
with a disk and a CD-ROM drive on one cable:

    Mouse: PS/2
      stage +  resets 01  equipment 67
      command byte 65  after A7 65  after A8 45  A9 --
      reset FA  self-test AA  id 00  enable FA

    IDE:     stage flags  status           signature
      1F0 m  +     07     50 50 80 --      0000 err 00  disk
      1F0 s  A     20     50 50 41 80      14EB err 04  CD-ROM
      170 m  Z     00     00 00 00 --      ---- err --

  The mouse's stage: C the controller, 7 and 8 the two commands, 9
  the test, W the command byte written, R a reset sent, T the
  self-test waited for, I the ID, E the enable, + found.  A device's:
  F a bus with nothing on it, S the select, Z a status of zero, B
  busy for ever, P a signature that is neither, K and k IDENTIFY
  PACKET with a signature and without, Q no data offered, + a disk,
  A a packet device.

FORMAT (CMD\FORMAT\FORMAT.ASM, most of it new).

  IT COULD NOT MAKE A DISKETTE.  It rewrote the FATs and the root of
  a volume that already had a BPB and refused anything else, which
  is all a hard disk needs and is no use for a box of blank disks.
  /U and /F: are both about laying down tracks, so that came first.

  A TRACK IS INT 13h AH=05h and a native program has no INT 13h.
  IO\FLOPPY.INC, new, is IOS_FLOPPY and 21h/F1h AL=14h: what the
  drive is (AH=08h, then CMOS register 10h), what is in it, begin,
  a track formatted and read back, end.  Begin is AH=18h, which
  answers with the diskette parameter table for the medium, and
  vector 1Eh is pointed at it until end puts it back.  A BIOS
  without 18h gets AH=17h where that has a meaning and a table of
  our own in GV_FDPT, sixteen bytes of the globals block at +80h.

  A DISK WITH NO BOOT SECTOR HAS NO LETTER INT 26h COULD BE POINTED
  AT, so its sectors go by F1h AL=0Dh and 0Eh, which now take drives
  0 and 1 as well as 80h and 81h.  sec_read and sec_write in FORMAT
  choose, and nothing above them knows which it is doing.

  THE SWITCHES.  /Q as it was.  /U: every track of a diskette, a new
  boot sector, and no mark carried over; on a hard disk, no mark
  carried over.  /C: clusters marked bad are tested instead of
  staying marked.  /F:size: 160, 180, 320, 360, 720, 1.2, 1.44 and
  2.88, with or without K, KB, M or MB, 1440 and 1.44 being one
  size; refused if the drive cannot make it.  /B: taken and ignored,
  because PM-DOS's loader follows the FAT and SYS needs no room
  kept, and refused together with /S as DOS refuses it.  Switches
  may be run together: FORMAT B:/U/F:720.

  A BAD CLUSTER MARK IS KEPT, which it was not.  FORMAT wrote fresh
  FATs and a quick format therefore handed every bad cluster back.
  fat_carry reads the old FAT a run of sectors at a time and frees
  everything but the marks.  Under /Q /C the marked clusters are
  read there and then; under /C or /U without /Q the surface check
  that follows finds them again.  mark_fat says when the entry held
  the mark already, so a cluster is counted once.

  A DISKETTE IS ASKED FOR.  "Insert the diskette to format in drive
  A: and press ENTER when ready", and the volume is looked at AFTER
  the key and not before.  The current drive may be formatted if it
  is a diskette drive, because on a machine started from its one
  floppy drive there is no other way to format a disk.

  WHAT IS DONE TO A DISKETTE is decided from what is in the drive.
  The format that is there is kept if it is the capacity wanted and
  /U did not ask for more; otherwise every track.  /Q on a disk with
  nothing to keep says so and formats every track.  A bad track is
  160 bits in bad_tracks and becomes bad clusters in the new FAT; one
  on cylinder 0, where the FATs and the root are, is "Track 0 bad".

  THE BOOT SECTOR OF A NEW DISKETTE boots nothing: it prints "This is
  not a system disk" and waits for a key.  Sixteen-bit code, so it
  is bytes in a table.  The serial number is the clock.

A DISKETTE'S GEOMETRY IS THE DISK'S (FAT.INC, fm_layout).  The block
layer's cylinder, head and sector came from INT 13h AH=08h, once, and
a real BIOS answers that for the DRIVE.  A 720K disk in a 1.44M drive
was read with eighteen-sector arithmetic, which is right for track 0
and wrong for every track after it.  No emulator shows this: they
answer with the image's own figures.  fat_mount now hands the block
layer what the boot sector says, if sectors a track times heads
divides the total into between 40 and 84 tracks.

THE PATH.  DISK\AUTOEXEC.BAT says PATH A:\.  The tests are run from
\TESTS or by their whole names.  A hard disk started from C: with that
line would look in an empty drive for every command, so MKHD.CMD
makes BIN\HD\AUTOEXEC.BAT - the same file with that line taken out by
FIND and C:'s put at the end - and that is what goes on HD16 and HD32.

WHAT IT COST.  PMIO.SYS is 41,944 bytes, 2,093 more.  PMDOS.SYS is
128,578, 316 more.  FORMAT.COM is 7,293 and was 3,951.  HWPROBE.EXE is
1,638.

TWO THINGS THE ASSEMBLER SAID.  ms_resets and MS_RESETS are one symbol
to wasm, and so are fpy_tries and FPY_TRIES: "invalid instruction
operands" at the use, as always.  They are MS_NRESETS and FPY_NTRIES.

VERIFIED, DOSBox-X headless, from the floppy.  HWPROBE as above, and
with [keyboard] aux=false, a serial mouse, no CD-ROM.  A CD-ROM found
and DIR of its disc on 1F0h slave behind a disk, 170h master, 1E8h
master and 168h slave.  FMTTEST.BAT, new, against a second floppy
image that was all zeroes: /U, no switch, /Q, /F:720 with a file
copied and CHKDSK clean, /U/B/F:1.44MB glued, /Q /U, and the five
refusals.  FORMAT A: /Q on the drive the machine was started from.  A
FAT16 volume with three clusters marked bad from the host: /Q keeps
3,072 bytes in bad sectors, a full format keeps them and counts them
once, /Q /C reads them and frees them.  The whole regression against
the run in the entry above: FORMAT's help, the sizes, a temporary
name and one count the cache test prints.

VERIFIED, 86Box, vs440fx.  The mouse found, a CD-ROM found on 1F0h
slave, IDETEST's nine checks.  An empty channel there reads 7Fh and
not FFh, and ends at P.  IDE86.PS1 said "the guest never finished":
the guest had, and the rig did not see DONE.TXT until 86Box was
closed.  Not looked into.

NOT VERIFIED, AND IT IS MOST OF WHAT MATTERS.  Real hardware, all of
it.  That either probe now finds what it did not.  A TRACK ACTUALLY
FORMATTED: the image was all zeroes before and a filesystem after,
which the sector writes alone would have done, so nothing here shows
that AH=05h laid anything down or which of AH=18h and AH=17h the
emulator took.  A bad track.  A 720K disk read in a 1.44M drive.  A
5.25-inch drive of either kind.

THE CD-ROM WAS ON A SOUND CARD: ISA PLUG AND PLAY (2026-09-27)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The question the entry above ended on was answered the same evening.
The drive is on a Creative card's IDE connector, the card is Plug and
Play, and on that machine it is CTCM from CONFIG.SYS that gives the
card its addresses.  PM-DOS started from a floppy runs no CTCM.  THE
PORT WAS NOT THERE: the four-channel probe of the entry above asked
1E8h and read FFh, which is the right answer from nothing.  Still
v0.60.

IO\ISAPNP.INC, new, and pnp_init is called from pm_entry before
blk_init.  It does the one part of CTCM's job the kernel needs.

  ISOLATION.  The key to 279h, every card's number back to nought,
  the key again, Wake[0], and then 72 pairs of reads at a port of our
  choosing: 55h and AAh is a one, anything else a zero.  A checksum
  that agrees is a card and it is given the next number.  It is
  Linux's isapnp_isolate, step for step, and that was deliberate.

  THE READ PORT IS A LIST, pnp_rdps, ten of them from 20Bh, and each
  is tried until one finds a card.  A MACHINE WITH NO SUCH CARD PAYS
  EIGHT BIT-TIMES AT EACH AND NOT SEVENTY-TWO: the first byte of an
  identifier is a vendor's letters and cannot be zero, so eight
  zeroes is nobody sending.  That is four milliseconds a port.

  THE PAUSES ARE READS OF PORT 80h, because this runs with interrupts
  off and the clock stopped.  500 for the 250 microseconds between
  reads, 2000 for a millisecond.  An emulator takes no time over them
  and needs none.

  WHAT A CARD HAS is its resource data, read a byte at a time through
  register 04h when 05h says there is one.  pnp_scan walks the items:
  a logical device is an IDE controller if its ID or a compatible ID
  is PNP0600, or if it is CTL2011.  Large items are skipped.  4096
  bytes and it stops, because a read port with nothing behind it is
  always ready and always FFh.

  WHERE IT MAY GO is in the data too, and it is not one answer.
  Creative's says 168h/36Eh preferred, 1E8h/3EEh acceptable, anything
  from 100h to 1F8h, or 170h/376h - four DEPENDENT FUNCTIONS, each a
  whole set.  A channel is allowed if one set has its command block
  in the first port descriptor and its control port in the second.
  pnp_chans makes the masks and psc_endblk ands them a set at a time.

  WHERE IT IS PUT is pnp_order: 1E8h, then 168h, then 170h.  Never
  1F0h.  1E8h first because that is where CTCM had put this one and
  what its owner calls it.  A channel is passed over if another
  controller was given it or if an IDE interface answers there
  already - pnp_chanfree, which writes 55h and AAh to two latches and
  reads the first back, so that a bus nobody drives reads AAh and
  fails.

  ONE THAT IS ON ALREADY, at a channel ata_init looks at, is left
  where it is.  A BIOS that knows Plug and Play does that.

  NO INTERRUPT IS GIVEN.  Registers 70h and 72h are written zero.
  The driver polls with nIEN set, so a line would be one more thing
  to collide on and nothing would use it.

  NOTHING ELSE ON THE CARD IS TOUCHED.  The audio, the game port and
  the wavetable are as they were found, which is off.  A DOS program
  that wants the sound card wants CTCM run first, as it always did.

THE LOG has its last sixteen bytes for this, PLP_FIRST = 112: how it
ended, how many cards, the read port, the card's ID, its number, the
device, where it was and where it is.  HWPROBE prints two more lines
and lost a blank one to stay on a screen:

    Plug and Play: 01 cards  read at 20B  stage +
      IDE on CTL0044  card 01  device 01  was 000  now 1E8/3EE

  N no card answered, I cards and no IDE controller among them, T a
  controller and no channel it may have, V it did not read back what
  was written, K on already and kept, + switched on.

WHAT IT COST.  PMIO.SYS is 43,801 bytes, 1,857 more.  HWPROBE.EXE is
2,053.  PMDOS.SYS did not change by a byte.

ONE THING THE ASSEMBLER SAID.  JECXZ reaches 127 bytes and psc_tag
was further: OR ECX,ECX and JZ.

VERIFIED, 86Box 4.2.1, WITH THE CARDS' OWN ROMS.  86Box's Sound
Blaster 32 PnP and AWE32 PnP answer with the resource data read out
of real cards (CT3600, CT3980), and its IDE channel for them does not
exist until the device is activated.

  ASUS VL/I-486SV2G, a 486 with no Plug and Play in its BIOS, which
  is the user's case.  THE KERNEL HE WAS GIVEN DOES NOT FIND THE
  DRIVE THERE: 1E8h reads FFh, DIR D: is "Invalid drive
  specification".  This one finds the card at 20Bh, switches device 1
  on at 1E8h/3EEh, says "CD-ROM drive detected as D:" and lists the
  disc.  Both cards.

  ASUS PCI/I-486SP3, Award, Plug and Play BIOS, from the floppy.  The
  BIOS had numbered the card and left the controller off.  Switched
  on at 1E8h, the disc listed as C:.  AND THE MOUSE FOUND, on a 486's
  keyboard controller: command byte 45h, 65h after A7h, 45h after
  A8h.

  Intel VS440FX, AMI.  The BIOS had put the controller at 168h/36Eh.
  Stage K, left there, found there.

VERIFIED, DOSBox-X.  No card, "no cards", and the boot is as it was.
The whole regression, 5,082 lines against the run in the entry above:
the times, the bytes free and one temporary name.

86BOX WANTS ITS CREATIVE ROMS IN roms\sound\creative\ AND THIS
INSTALL HAS THEM IN roms\sound\.  "AWE32.RAW not found", in a message
box the main window's picture does not show.  -R names another ROM
