FDISK'S SCREEN AGAIN, LAID OUT LIKE DISKSTAT: THE BAR TAKES THE MOUSE
(2026-10-01)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for the screen to be like DiskStat's "but with a bar
instead of a PIE chart", the bar clickable and its partitions movable
with the mouse "if there's space on the drive", and sizes for a resize
typed in megabytes - "not cylinders because that's too tedious".

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE.  DiskStat's text screen, colours and all: a title
row with the close box in its corner, a File / Disk / Partition / Help
menu bar, grey single-line panes on a blue desktop, a cyan status
line, bright-white-on-blue boxes with double borders and shadows.
Where DiskStat has its usage chart there is the disk, across the full
width, three rows deep: each partition a block in its own colour with
its number and drive letter on it, the extended partition a dark shade
under its logical drives, free space a light one, a bracket under
whatever is selected and a scale in megabytes below.  Under that, the
partitions as a list in disk order - free space a cylinder or longer
gets a row of its own, at the level it is at - and beside it what the
selection is.  A partition's colour follows its NUMBER, not its place,
so deleting one does not repaint the rest.

THE DRAG.  A press on a block selects it; moving the mouse off that
cell moves a copy of the block along the bar.  Where the copy goes is
worked out the way a partition's place always is here: its END goes to
the nearest cylinder boundary (which keeps the first partition one
track into the disk and a logical drive one track behind its record),
and the whole is held inside the free space either side of it, so the
block stops against its neighbours instead of going through them.  It
is green while it fits and red for a partition with no FAT volume in
it, which the engine will not move.  Letting go runs the move as a dry
run; the engine's answer is either a red box saying why not, or the
question - Yes or No - and then the move.  M does the same from the
keyboard, with the start typed in megabytes and the bar redrawn as it
is typed; a typed start may jump over another partition, and the dry
run decides.

MEGABYTES.  S asks /P first, so the box can say how small (what is
stored) and how big (the room, and the FAT width's ceiling) the
partition can be, and the bar turns red as soon as the number typed is
outside that.  The size typed ends on the nearest cylinder boundary,
held inside those two limits.  C creates in the free space that is
SELECTED - which needed one engine change, below - offering all of it
to a tenth of a megabyte; a size typed there also ends on the nearest
cylinder, and anything within a megabyte of all of it is all of it
(the first version took the offered 3.4 MB literally, rounded down
twice, and came out a cylinder short).  An extended partition is asked
for with a check box in the same box, offered only where the disk has
none.

WRITES.  W is gone.  Every change is a dry run first and a Yes/No box
second - the delete's is red and its Enter is No - and only a Yes arms
the writes, for that change, as tui_write always did.  The verbs' own
words are not lost: the end of what the verb said is the box that
follows a change, and File > Output log shows all of it.

FOUR FILES NOW: FDTUI.INC (the session and the commands), FDDRAW.INC
(the screen), FDDLG.INC (menus, boxes, the line builder, megabyte
parsing, the viewer), FDEVENT.INC (keyboard, mouse, key file).  Every
equate is at the top of FDTUI.INC - wasm will not take one it has not
met.  The mouse is read as EDIT reads it: 21h/F0h AL=8 woken by the
mouse too, INT 33h 05h/06h/03h turned into press, release, drag and
double-click events on cells.  FDISK.EXE 31,677 -> 47,407 bytes;
TUI_BSS_LEN is 82 + 140*40 + 512*4 + 8192 + 4000 (rows grew to 40
bytes, and to 140 of them, because free space has rows now).

THREE ENGINE CHANGES, two for the screen and one bug.
  - gp_want: fd_gap and fd_lgap take the run of free space holding that
    sector instead of the biggest, when it is not zero.  The command
    line never sets it.
  - fd_plan keeps the limits it prints in pl_minsz and pl_maxsz.
  - A LOGICAL DRIVE COULD BE MOVED IN FRONT OF ITS OWN BOOT RECORD.
    fd_entptr gave it the whole container as its region, and its own
    record as a wall one sector wide - so a volume small enough to fit
    wholly in front of that record, in space a shrunk or deleted
    neighbour left, passed every check.  Its start is written as an
    offset FROM that record, unsigned: the table would have said four
    gigabytes on.  The old FDISK approves /M 1:6 108864 on MULTI.IMG
    after /S 1:5 8M and /S 1:6 7M; this one says it is outside the
    region, and still approves moving 5 up inside its own link.  pl_lo
    for a logical drive is now its own record plus one.  The drag
    cannot ask for it; a typed move could, and so could the command
    line all along.

THE TEST.  FDTEST key files carry the mouse now as EDIT's do: FEh, the
buttons, a row and a column, put to the driver through INT 33h 04h and
21h/F0h AL=0Bh and read back like the real thing; TOOLS\MKFDKEYS.PL
has {PRESS r,c} {RELEASE} {DRAG} {MOVE} {CLICK} {DCLICK} and {ALT+X}.
A press on the cell of the last click with nothing typed between is a
double click, as in EDIT - which bit the first script.  DISK\FDM1.KEY
(249 bytes) drags partition 2 against its neighbour, deletes 3, drags
2 into the space (75600), creates there (68544 + 7056), resizes
logical 5 to "8" (91854 + 16002), drags it inside its link (102942),
opens both kinds of menu and the help, moves it by typing "46"
(93870), shows its details, then empties, deletes and remakes the
extended partition with the check box (91728 + 73584) and a logical
drive in it (91791 + 73521) - 35 screens, every number as predicted.
FDHOLD=anything with FDTEST hands the keyboard over when the file runs
out, so a recording of the screen ends on whatever was left showing;
that is how its pictures were taken (DOSBox-X headless, ZMBVSHOT.PL).
FDTEST, FDLTEST, FDRTEST, /STATUS and /? give output identical byte
for byte to the old FDISK's.

NOT VERIFIED: real hardware; a real mouse being moved (every press and
drag here was injected through the driver); a list longer than its 11
rows, and its scroll bar; FAT32 through the screen; 43/50-line
screens (the top 25 rows are drawn and the mouse is scaled to the real
height).  NOT DONE: dragging an edge of a block to resize; moving a
logical drive's record along with it, so it could go into space in
front of its record; the /G graphics screen DiskStat has.  AND STILL
TRUE OF THE ENGINE: a disk with no AA55 signature cannot be given a
partition table here, by the screen or the command line.

A NATIVE PROGRAM IS NOT 512K ANY MORE: A SLOT OUT OF THE ARENA, AND
IT GROWS (2026-10-01)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie wants native programs that need a great deal of memory to be
able to have it - a D32 port of XArc whose decompressor wants 1.5GB,
a web browser.  A native program's whole address space was one fixed
512K slot at 180000h, and 4Bh made room for a child by copying the
parent out of that slot into the arena, and 4Ch copied it back.  It
is now a block of the arena that grows when the program asks 48h for
more than it has.  Done in three steps, each run on all seven of
RUNTESTS.PS1's machines before the next.  Still v0.61.

ALL OF MEMORY IS MAPPED, NOT 256MB.  The 64 page tables at PG_TABS are
a fixed 256MB and arena_init stopped there, so the 260MB, 1GB and 3GB
machines all had 262,059K.  pg_hiram (PAGING.INC) builds a 4K table
for every 4MB above that at the TOP of memory and lowers GV_MEMTOP
below them - a megabyte of tables a gigabyte, 704 tables on the 3GB
machine.  4K tables even with 4MB pages, so that any page can still
be taken out of the map: a slot's guard page can be anywhere now.
arena_init asks the directory whether the top is mapped rather than
believing the number, so a new PMDOS.SYS on an old PMIO.SYS stops at
256MB as before.  MEM counts the tables as OS Reserved (the BIOS top
less the arena's end, from F1h AL=4's EBX), so its total still adds up.

EVERY PROGRAM HAS A SLOT OF ITS OWN.  slot_new (RING3.INC) takes one
from the arena when 4Bh starts a native program and slot_free gives
it back in 4Ch, in f4B_loadfail, and - slot_sweep - at every restart
of the interpreter.  The block is owner 0, for the cache's reason: a
block stamped with the parent's owner is swept when the PARENT ends.
r3_useslot reads a table by depth instead of choosing between two
constants, nobody is copied anywhere, and XN_SAVE is gone.  The guard
page is taken out of the map by a new PMIO service, IOS_PGPRES
(pg_guard, IOSVC+0E8h), and put back BEFORE the block is freed - after
would hand a page that is not there to whoever the arena gives it to
next.  The interpreter's slot is still the fixed one at 140000h.

AND THE TABLES MOVED INTO THE OLD SLOT.  180000h-1FFFFFh was nobody's
once programs left it, and on the 4MB 386 that cost a level of
nesting.  The directory, the 72 fixed tables and _KBSS are 388K of
it, so they live there now (PG_DIR 180000h, KBSS_BASE 1C9000h - on
BUILD.CMD's wlink line too) and the arena starts at 220000h for every
build: 388K more arena, and the 386 nests two levels again, as it
did before.  KBUF_LO3, the bottom of the kernel range buf_ok guards,
moved down with them.  pg_init no longer takes the page at PROG_SLOT
out of the map - that page is the page directory now.

A SLOT GROWS.  When the heap cannot meet a 48h, slot_grow resizes the
slot's arena block in place (in 64K steps, or exact pages for the
last of it), and the new memory becomes a free block at the old top.
Three things make that work.  THE STACK IS A BLOCK IN USE in the heap
chain (r3h_init): it is at the top of the first 512K and cannot move,
so the chain steps over it to reach what grows above it.  THE LIMIT
IS IN PAGES past 1MB (r3_setdesc sets DGRAN_G), since a byte limit is
twenty bits; every slot is whole pages for that reason.  THE SLOT IS
PLACED WHERE IT CAN GROW: slot_new takes the bottom of the biggest
free block (AF_LARGEST, a fit 58h cannot set), and the cache buys its
chunks last fit - which now takes the TOP of the highest block, as
DOS's did, where it used to take the bottom and land beside a slot.
48h's "largest" counts what the slot could still grow by (slot_room),
or a program asking for FFFFFFFFh is told its heap is the machine.

AND GIVES IT BACK AT EXEC.  A program that grew to all of memory and
freed it still holds it, in its own heap.  DOS programs shrank their
block with 4Ah before an EXEC; 4Bh now does it for them, slot_trim,
handing the free top of the caller's slot back to the arena before
either kind of child is started.

A VECTOR SAYS WHOSE IT IS.  get_vec/set_vec told a program's handler
from a kernel address by size - an offset below 512K, a kernel address
above 1MB - which a slot past 1MB ends.  25h now says from the
caller's CS, build_psp records whose each saved vector was
(psp_vtags), and 4Ch hands that back with it (term_vtags); a PSP field
the program rewrote itself falls back to the old rule.  THIS ALSO
FIXES AN OLDER BUG, by reading: a vector restored at 4Ch was put down
as the PARENT'S handler whoever had hooked it, so the shell's INT 23h
handler inherited two levels down came back tagged as the middle
program's, an offset in the wrong slot.  No test has exercised that.

FOUND ON THE WAY.  Rounding a request up with "add ebx,15" wrapped one
within 15 bytes of 4GB to zero: arena_alloc and r3h_alloc answered a
48h or a DPMI 0501h for FFFFFFFFh with a 16-byte block, and
arena_resize and r3h_resize SHRANK a block to nothing.  arena_avail's
"impossible" request was 7FFFFFFFh, which a 3GB arena meets: it
allocated 2GB, gave it back, and XMS 3.0 reported 2GB as the largest
block.  PCITEST's check 10 used 3FC00000h as "past any memory this
kernel maps", which is RAM on the 1GB machine now; it works its
address out from the arena's end.  And the RUNTESTS baseline had been
recorded on a tree without DISK\IMGFILE.TXT, which .gitignore keeps
out of the repository, so TESTIMG.IMG was not on its test disk:
RMFIND and RMTEST were re-recorded with it.

TESTS.  SLOTTEST.EXE nests itself as deep as it can - seven levels
below it where memory allows, two on the 4MB 386 - each level checking
its own memory survived its child, then a null store and a read of the
guard's last dword, each of which has to end its child with 255, then
counts the slots left in the arena.  BIGMEM.EXE asks 48h for all there
is: 1,059K on the 386, 29,215K on the 486 and 3,139,359K on the 3GB
machine, in ONE block, every page written and read back; frees it and
takes it as sixteen pieces; runs a child that has to grow its own slot
while holding all but 2MB; and checks the PSP's memory top.  Both are
in BUILD.CMD, both MKHD.CMD images and RUNTESTS.PS1.  RUNTESTS -All:
69 tests, all seven machines.  PARKTEST with XMSREPT on the 3GB machine
parks and comes back with MEM identical, so RMDOS's XMS takes a 3GB
pool.  PMIO.SYS 44,411; PMDOS.SYS 136,032; MEM.EXE 3,108.

NOT DONE.  4Ah on the PSP still neither grows nor shrinks the slot; a
program gets memory through 48h.  A slot shrinks only at EXEC.  The
interpreter keeps its fixed 256K.  A handler belonging to a program
waiting further up than the shell is still refused (r3_thunk), though
its code is no longer copied away and it could now be run.

NOT VERIFIED.  Windows 3.1 itself on a machine with more than 256MB:
RMDOS's XMS 2.0 answers still cap at 64MB, so it should see what it
saw, but it has not been run.  A DPMI client given all of a large
machine, beyond XMSTEST.  Real hardware.

FDISK: THE EXTENDED PARTITION MOVES, AND A RESIZE CAN CHANGE THE
CLUSTER SIZE (2026-10-02)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

A day of changes to the screen and the engine under it, each asked for
by Charlie after trying the one before.  Each round was checked
against a model of the screen written in JavaScript, compared picture
for picture with FDTEST's dumps of the real program in DOSBox-X: 167
pictures alike by the end of this entry, 255 by the end of the next.
The model and the harness that ran it are not in the repository.
Still v0.61.

NO BOX AFTER A CREATE OR A DELETE THAT WORKED: the bar shows it, and V
still shows the log.  One that failed still says why.  (Overtaken the
same day - see the next entry, where nothing is written until W.)

A PARTITION WITH NO FAT VOLUME IN IT MOVES AND RESIZES.  fv_read calls
a volume raw (fv_raw) when its first sector has no 55AAh or does not
start with a jump (EBh or E9h), and the plan marks it (pl_raw): a move
or a resize of one writes the table entry and nothing else, since
nothing in it is anything FDISK knows how to carry.  The question says
"not formatted, so only the partition table entry changes", and /P
says the same.  A partition created again where a deleted one started
finds the old boot sector still there, and is a FAT volume again.

THE EXTENDED PARTITION MOVES AND RESIZES.  A move carries the whole
chain in one copy, from the head record to the end of the last link
(rl_cxmove).  Every start in the chain is an offset from a record, so
the copy is already a correct chain; what is not relative is put right
after it - the CHS fields, the LBA spelling of a type that now ends
past CHS's reach, and the hidden sectors of each volume.  A resize
cannot cut a logical drive off (RL_HOLDS), and a chain that does not
read cleanly is not touched (RL_CHAIN).  On the bar, a press on the
free space inside the container drags the container, a whole cylinder
at a time (cx_snap).

TWO BUGS THAT WERE THE BAR.  An extended partition with a drive in it
could not be resized, and an emptied one could not be deleted: "select
a drive first".  No cell of the bar is the container itself - its
drives and its free space cover all of it.  M, S and D on free space
inside the container now act on the container (tu_tocont).  From the
list both had always worked.  Delete still refuses a container with
drives in it.

/W IS GONE.  The command line writes what it is asked to: dk_armed
starts at 1, and /W is an unknown switch now - the usage, and exit
code 1.  The screen still runs its dry runs with the writes held off
(tui_dryrun).  The "proposed:" line for a move or a resize is gone
from fd_change, with rl_opname, msg_prop, msg_from and msg_arrow;
create, delete, active and /MBR still print theirs.

F1 IS THE KEYS.  The command line's usage is no longer in the help,
and Help > Keys... is the menu item.

A RESIZE CAN CHANGE THE CLUSTER SIZE (FDREMAP.INC).  A new size that
the volume's cluster size cannot make a legal volume of - or not at
its FAT width - used to stop at RL_REMAP or RL_FATTYPE.  Charlie's
choices: every FAT type, a change only when one is needed, and FAT12
and FAT16 trading places.  rm_choose takes the nearest of three:
  - RM_WIDTH: the same cluster size at the other width, FAT12 <->
    FAT16.  Cluster numbers survive; only the FAT is written again.
  - RM_SPLIT: smaller clusters.  Each old cluster becomes k new ones
    in the same sectors, so no data moves, but every chain and every
    directory entry's first cluster is renumbered.
  - RM_MERGE: larger clusters.  One new cluster cannot hold two
    files, so every chain is packed from the front of the data area,
    by a permutation that follows its cycles.
FAT32 stays FAT32: going between FAT16 and FAT32 moves the root
directory into or out of the data area, which is a conversion and not
a resize.  Before anything is written, rm_prepare reads the FAT into a
table of 32-bit entries in 48h memory - which grows the slot, since
FAT32 needs megabytes - and the volume has to hold together: every
chain ending, none looping, no cluster in two chains, every directory
entry naming the start of a chain of its own.  Three new refusals:
RL_BADCLUS (the clusters would have to grow, and some are marked bad),
RL_DAMAGED ("Run CHKDSK first.") and RL_NOMEM.

TESTED on a 267MB image built for it, of four volumes - FAT16 at one
sector a cluster, FAT12, FAT16 at eight, FAT32 at four - holding 755
files in 32 directories, with long names and fragmented files.  The
first FAT16 grew twice (to two sectors a cluster, then four), the
FAT12 became FAT16 and back, the second FAT16 became FAT12 and back,
and the FAT32 shrank to one sector a cluster.  After every pass each
file's MD5 and each directory were the same, and a checker that does
what CHKDSK does found nothing wrong.  The same image with a cluster
marked bad in the first volume and a headless chain in the fourth is
refused for each, from the command line, with exit code 1.

AND A BUG IN MOVE, older than all of this.  A move wrote the FAT size
FDISK would CHOOSE for the volume's size into the boot sector it
moved, not the one the volume has.  A volume that FORMAT had given a
longer FAT came out of a move with its second FAT, its root and its
data in the wrong place: no files, and every cluster lost.  A move now
keeps the volume's own layout (rp_keep).

FDISK: CHANGES WAIT FOR W, F FORMATS, AND QUITTING RESTARTS THE
MACHINE (2026-10-02)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

QUITTING RESTARTS THE MACHINE after a change the running system cannot
see.  Drive letters are dealt out at the start, so a partition made,
removed, moved or resized leaves the volume table describing a disk
that is not there any more.  A new kernel call does the restart: INT
21h F1h AL=1Bh (fF1_reboot) runs dos_commit and then, if a cache block
is still dirty, returns CF and ERR_WRFAULT (1Dh) with the machine left
up, since a restart over a write that would not go loses the write.
Otherwise IOS_REBOOT (IOSVC+0F0h, sys_reboot in KEYBD.INC) puts 1234h
at 40:72h so that the BIOS skips its memory test, waits for the 8042
to take a command, and goes the way Ctrl-Alt-Del goes (kb_reboot).
FDISK shows "Changes require a reboot.  Restarting the system now..."
for three seconds first, and says so if the kernel came back.  The
active flag and the boot code do not count: they are read only at a
start.  Under FDTEST the box goes into the log and the log is closed;
the machine restarts only if FDBOOT= is set as well, or a batch file
of key files would start again from the top after every script.

CHANGES WAIT FOR W.  Charlie asked for an undo and a commit.  On the
screen nothing is written when a change is asked for: it is STAGED
(FDPEND.INC).  The verb runs exactly as the command line would run it,
with dk_armed at DK_STAGE, and every sector it writes goes into an
overlay in the BSS (ov_*) instead of to the disk.  dk_read lays the
overlay over whatever it reads, so every verb after it, and the table
the bar is drawn from, sees the disk as it will be.  The change goes
into a journal (jn_tbl): the verb, its arguments as the command line
would have had them, the free run a create meant (gp_want), and the
question the screen asked.  The status line counts them: "2 changes
waiting.   W Commit  U Undo  F1 Help  F10 Menus  Q Quit".

W COMMITS.  A box lists the changes - five, then "...and N more." -
asks "Write these changes to the disk?", and adds "This can take a
while.  Do not turn the machine off." when one of them moves data.
Yes throws the overlay away and runs the journal again with the writes
on, "Writing change 2 of 3..." on the status line.  Each verb plans
afresh against the real disk, which by then is what the one before it
left: the state it was staged against.  A change that fails stops the
commit there, and the box says which, why, and that the ones before it
were written.  U UNDOES the last change ("Undone: " and its question)
by staging the rest again.  Both are on the File menu.  V shows what a
commit ran; a staged run's log is thrown away.

A MOVE OR A RESIZE STAGES ITS TABLE ENTRY AND NOTHING ELSE.  The data
it would move is far more than can be held, and nothing on the screen
reads it - but a second change to the same volume would plan against a
boot sector and a FAT that are still where they were.  So the volume
is LOCKED until the commit (pd_locked): a second move or resize,
Details and a drag on it get "Partition 5 (E:) moves or resizes when
the changes are committed." and "Commit or undo the changes waiting
first."  A container move carries its records and its volumes' boot
sectors into the overlay (rcm_carry), because the chain is what the
bar draws, and the drives in it are locked all the same.  A partition
that is not formatted is not locked, nor is a container resize, and
deleting a locked partition ends its lock.

QUITTING WITH CHANGES WAITING asks "Commit the changes before
quitting?" - Yes commits and quits, No quits and writes nothing,
Cancel and Esc stay.  A key file that has run out has nobody to ask
(kt_eof), and its changes go: a test that wanted them would have
pressed W.

THE LIMITS are 256 staged sectors (128K of BSS) and 32 changes.  A
change past either is refused: "Too many changes are waiting.  Commit
them first."  A change that will not stage again after an undo is
dropped, with the ones after it, and the screen says so.

F FORMATS, ON THE SCREEN ONLY.  Charlie: "drive formatting should only
be done from within the TUI.  The command line is free to use FORMAT
instead."  fd_format has no switch; FDC_FORMAT is set by the screen
alone.  It is a quick format - a boot sector, the FATs, an empty root
- laid out the way Microsoft's FORMAT lays one out: FAT12 up to 8,400
sectors, FAT16 up to FAT16_MAXSECS, FAT32 above that or where the type
byte already says FAT32 and there are 66,600 sectors or more, with
Microsoft's cluster size for each size.  The root holds 512 entries;
FAT32 gets 32 reserved sectors, FSInfo in sector 1, a backup boot
sector in 6 and its root in cluster 2.  The boot code only says "No
system on this volume."  The type byte is set to match (rl_typebyte).
A format is NOT staged: it writes a volume, not a table, and only when
nothing is waiting ("Commit or undo the changes waiting before
formatting."), so what it formats is what is on the disk.  The
question is red and its Enter is No: "Format partition 3 as FAT12?",
"Everything stored on partition 3 will be lost.", and for the drive
PM-DOS started from, "PM-DOS was started from C:."

THE CACHE.  Charlie asked: "Should we only flush the cache on a commit
so that FDISK can benefit from cache at startup, and also if no
changes are made the existing cache doesn't get ejected?"  That is
what already happens.  Nothing ejects the cache: 4Bh's commit writes
the dirty blocks and keeps every block.  A session with nothing
committed or formatted does not restart, so the cache is left alone;
the only flush FDISK causes is fF1_reboot's, before a restart.  And
FDISK never reads through the cache: F1h AL=0Dh and 0Eh go to the
driver, around CACHE.INC, and FDISK's big reads - a FAT, 64K at a time
- are the size the cache lets past anyway (CC_BIGXFER).

TESTED in DOSBox-X with FDTEST key files.  Staging, undo, the lock and
the commit; growing a FAT12 volume into the room a waiting delete
made, committed as FAT16 with its file whole; a container move staged
and committed, every record and boot sector right; No at the quit
question leaving the disk as it was; a format of each width, CHKDSK
clean after the restart - FAT12 at two sectors a cluster, FAT16 at
four, FAT32 at one.  /D, /S and /M on the command line still write at
once.  DISK\FDM1.KEY now commits after its moves and resizes and at
the end (TOOLS\MKFDKEYS.PL; 256 bytes).  FDISK.EXE 61,673 bytes;
PMIO.SYS 44,954; PMDOS.SYS 136,410.  The floppy's files, less the 42
batch files .gitignore keeps out of the repository, come to 1,599 of
its 2,847 clusters.

NOT DONE.  FORMAT.COM reformats a volume that has a BPB and cannot lay
the first one down on a hard disk, so a partition the command line
makes cannot be given a file system from the command line yet.  F1h
AL=0Dh and 0Eh do not keep the cache honest: a sector written around
the cache leaves a stale clean copy in it until the restart, which
matters to the command line, since the screen restarts anyway.  Two
volumes formatted in the same second get the same serial number
(ff_serial is the date plus the time, as DOS's is); it happened to
the FAT16 and the FAT32 of the format test.

NOT VERIFIED.  MASM.  Real hardware.  A commit that fails half way;
changes on two disks in one commit; reaching either limit.

MASM ASSEMBLES ALL OF IT, AND WHAT CHECKING THE FDISK WORK FOUND
(2026-10-02)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The two entries above were checked from the outside the same evening,
and what that found is fixed here.  Still v0.61.

THE CHECK.  The old FDISK (8eff60a, with /W) ran FDTEST, FDLTEST,
FDRTEST and FD32TEST as they were; the new one ran them with /W taken
off and every dry run that said it wrote nothing left out.  All four
second disks came out byte for byte the same.  On the screen: two
changes staged and Q answered No left the disk as it started; U and
then W gave exactly what FDISK /D 1:3 gives; F made a FAT12, a FAT16
and a FAT32 volume that CHKDSK passed after the restart.  A resize
that merged clusters (one sector to two, the files packed) and two
that went FAT16 to FAT12, on volumes of fragmented files, each passed
CHKDSK and FC /B on every file afterwards, and a long name survived
all three.  RUNTESTS differed in two answers only, and FDISK.EXE's
size on the test disk is why: with the old FDISK.EXE put back,
CACHETST matched again and RMTEST's free count rose by the 15
clusters FDISK had grown by.  Both are re-recorded in BASELINE.

MASM.  ML 6.13 (C:\MASM611, which is 6.11 patched; any MASM 6.1x
is the target) refused fifteen of the 108 .ASM files, the kernel and
FDISK among them, and had since August.  Three kinds of line, 31 files:
  - `jmp short` to a label MASM places further away than wasm does.
    wasm quietly makes such a jump near; dropping `short` leaves
    wasm's output as it was.  Forty-seven of these.
  - a table written `name:` above its db lines is NEAR to MASM, so
    `mov al,[kb_lower + ebx]` needs `byte ptr`, as does a store to
    `[ebx+CONST+edx]`; `null_idtr:  dw  0` is a syntax error to it.
  - the size guards written IF / .ERR / ENDIF.  MASM evaluates IF on
    its first pass, before its jumps are sized, so BOOT.ASM, BOOTHD's
    BPB check and IORM's park entry all failed on sizes that were
    right.  The seven that measure code are .ERRE / .ERRNZ now, which
    both assemblers evaluate at the end and both still fire - each was
    tried with a size that should fail.
Every .ASM, and BUILD's -dFAT32BOOT, -dCLIENT32 and -dD32 variants,
assembles under ML.  Every file BUILD makes is byte for byte what it
was, except FDISK.EXE, and FDISK built by ML ran FDMTEST's 38
pictures and left the same disk as the wasm build.

/P SAID "Current size" OVER THE ROOM AT THE PARTITION'S START, not its
size - 30240 for a logical drive of 16002, in FDMTEST's Details.  It
prints the length now, and the three labels line up again.  The
messages that ended in a space before the line end lost it, and a
resize that changes the FAT width no longer says "No file moves." over
a line saying it is moving the data: the cluster numbers are what stay.

THE BATCH FILES, which .gitignore keeps out of the repository and so
were still the /W ones: FDTEST, FDLTEST, FDRTEST and FD32TEST write
at once now, FDTEST checks that /W is refused with the usage and
nothing written, and FDLTEST's refusal (4) is a shrink below the
smallest size, since one that needs FAT12 is no longer refused.
AUTOEXEC.BAT's notes on FDISK, and FDMTEST's, describe today's FDISK.

FDISK.EXE 61,688 bytes.  NOT VERIFIED: BUILD's debug targets
(%DEFS%) under ML.

A DMF DISK READS AND WRITES: THE BIOS'S TABLE SAID WHERE A TRACK ENDS
(2026-10-02)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked whether PM-DOS could take DMF diskettes natively.  DMF
is Microsoft's distribution format: a 1.44M disk laid down with 21
sectors a track instead of 18, 3,360 sectors, 2K clusters and 16 root
entries.  Still v0.61.

MOST OF IT WAS ALREADY THERE.  fm_layout takes a diskette's geometry
from its boot sector, and 21 x 2 x 3,360 is 80 whole cylinders, so
FDF_SETGEO took it; the block layer splits a request where the BPB
says a track ends; and to the FAT layer the volume is an ordinary
FAT12.  What was missing was below all of that.

THE BIOS STOPS WHERE ITS TABLE SAYS A TRACK ENDS, NOT WHERE THE DISK'S
DOES.  INT 13h gives the controller the last sector of the track out of
the diskette parameter table vector 1Eh points at.  The block layer
moves up to sixteen sectors a call without leaving a track, so a call
for sectors 17 to 21 asked for three sectors past a table that says
18.  A real controller ends the command at 18 and reports the end of
the cylinder.  86Box ends it at 18 and reports SUCCESS, so there the
bug is data that never arrived: on the vli486sv2g (Award BIOS, table
says 18) the old kernel read 85,177 bytes of a 700,000-byte file
wrong, and 49 of the 391 sectors of a file it wrote were never
written, without a single error.  The first wrong byte was at 1400h,
ten sectors into a file that starts at logical sector 8: sector 19 of
the first track.

WHETHER A MACHINE HAS IT IS WHATEVER ITS TABLE SAYS.  The vs440fx's AMI
BIOS points vector 1Eh at a table that says 36 - sized for a 2.88M
drive - so the old kernel read and wrote DMF there perfectly, by luck.
MS-DOS 6.0 lifts the byte only as far as the longest track of a drive
it knows (MSINIT.ASM, and install_bds in MSBIO2.ASM), never as far as
the disk's, so it has the same limit.  DOSBox-X's INT 13h does not read
the table at all, which is why no run there could have shown it.

THE FIX IS MS-DOS'S OWN TRICK, TAKEN AS FAR AS THE DISK.  fpy_rwup and
fpy_rwdown in FLOPPY.INC: when a diskette's GEO_SPT is more than the
table's last sector, vector 1Eh is pointed at a copy of that table in
GV_RWDPT (GV_BASE+0B0h, IORM's v_rwdpt) with the disk's count in it,
for the length of one blk_go call, and put back at each of its three
exits after the geometry is known (bio_done, bio_fail, bio_nocyl).  A
table that says more than a disk has costs nothing - the DMA count
ends the transfer, which is how a 720K disk is read through a 1.44M
drive's table - but the vector is moved only when it has to be, and
not at all while a format has it (fpy_open).  GV_RWDPT is separate
from GV_FDPT so that neither can be in the middle of using the other's.
A DOS box's INT 13h on a diskette is translated into blk_read
(INT13.INC), so a program reading the disk itself gets the same.

VERIFIED on 86Box with a DMF image holding two files of 700,000 and
800,001 bytes, every 512 bytes stamped with its file and offset, and
the same files on C:; FC /B compares them and a 200,000-byte W.BIN is
copied on and compared, then read back off the image on the host with
FLOPGET.PL:
  - vli486sv2g (Award, table 18): old kernel wrong both ways as above;
    new kernel no differences, W.BIN byte for byte on the image.
  - the same machine with a 1.44M disk: no differences.
  - vs440fx (AMI, table 36): no differences, old kernel and new.
  - vector 1Eh read by a probe program before the diskette is
    touched, after the first DIR and at the end: F000:EFC7 all three
    times on both machines, so it is always put back.
IOPM.ASM, IORM.ASM and DOSMAIN.ASM assemble under ML.  Of everything
BUILD makes only PMIO.SYS changed (44,954 to 45,117 bytes), and that
is the whole of what RUNTESTS saw on its seven machines: RMTEST's free
count is one cluster less, because PMIO.SYS now needs a 45th 1K
cluster, and CACHETST's "a write is owed" went from 5 to 4 on the six
machines that cache.  The OLD kernel padded with zeros to the new
PMIO.SYS's size gives exactly the new CACHETST, so that is where the
files lie and not what the kernel does.  Both re-recorded in BASELINE;
CACHETST is back to what it was before the FDISK work moved it.

RUNTESTS FROM A SCRATCH TREE SEEDED WITH S:\BIN finds RMFIND and RMTEST
different whatever the kernel: BIN\TESTS there also holds EXEHDR, MSD,
NMAKE, MEM622, DISKSTAT and REVEAL, which BUILD does not make and
BASELINE was recorded without.  Take them out first.

NOT VERIFIED.  Real hardware.  A 2.88M disk in a drive whose table says
18, which met the same limit.  Booting from a DMF disk (FATLOAD reads
one sector at a call, which a short table should not stop).  NOT DONE:
FORMAT /F:1.68 and DISKCOPY of a DMF disk, which are next.  And RMDOS
(DOS\RMDISK.INC) still takes a diskette's geometry from INT 13h AH=08h,
which describes the drive: a DMF or a 720K disk is misaddressed after
its first track while the kernel is parked under Windows - the bug
fm_layout had until 2026-09-27, not changed here.

RMDOS READS A 720K DISK, AND NO FILE ON A DISKETTE WRAPS AT 64K
(2026-10-02)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for the RMDOS half of the entry above to be fixed.  It
was two bugs, the second hidden behind the first.  Still v0.61.

THE GEOMETRY.  rd_mount asked INT 13h AH=08h, which describes the
drive, and never looked at the boot sector's figures.  On the
vli486sv2g, whose BIOS calls a 1.44M drive eighteen sectors a track,
a 720K disk was addressed as if it had eighteen: its files start at
logical sector 14, sector 15 of a track that has nine, so the first
read of every file failed (RMDOS's error 9) and so did the first
write.  A diskette's boot sector is believed now, after it has been
read, when its figures agree - at most 63 sectors a track, one or two
sides, a whole number of cylinders between 40 and 84 - which is
fm_layout's test.  The boot sector itself is sector 1 of track 0 under
any geometry, so reading it with the drive's is safe.

AND BEHIND IT, EVERY FILE ON A DISKETTE WRAPPED AT 64K.  With the
geometry right the reads went through, and from 64K into a file came
back as the file's first sectors again - the stamp read at offset
65536 said 00000000 - while a write past 64K went over the start of
the file.  A 1.44M disk, whose geometry was never wrong, did exactly
the same, so this had always been there.  rd_getvol mounts a diskette
every time it is asked for one, and file_io and sft_clus ask in the
middle of a transfer, holding the file position in EAX and the bytes
still to move in ECX.  rd_mount saved them with PUSHA, which keeps
sixteen bits, and worked in EAX, ECX and EDX; the top of the position
came back as nought.  A hard disk is mounted once, at its first use,
and never showed it.  PUSHAD and POPAD now, which also keeps the top
half of every register of a caller running 32-bit code.

SEEN AND LEFT: mounting on every call reads the boot sector twice for
every 512 bytes of a file, each time with a seek back to track 0.
100K takes over a minute on 86Box's drive.  It is correct; a
change-line check would make it quick, and is not done here.

VERIFIED on 86Box, vli486sv2g, by PARKTEST running a scratch program
(RMCMP.COM) on RMDOS that compares two files on A: of 100,000 and
80,001 bytes with copies on C:, copies a 70,000-byte file to A: and
compares that back, and writes what it found to C:; the written file
was then read off the diskette image on the host with FLOPGET.PL.
Before: 720K, the first read of each file and the first write failed;
1.44M, every block past 64K wrong in both files and the written one.
After: 720K, 1.44M and DMF, every block of all three right, and the
written file byte for byte on each image.  RMDOS.ASM assembles under
ML.  RMDOS.SYS 28,711 to 28,794 bytes.  NOT VERIFIED: real hardware,
and Windows itself using a diskette while the kernel is parked.

DISKCOPY AND DISKCOMP TAKE DMF, AND A DISK AND ITS COPY COMPARE OK
(2026-10-02)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for DISKCOPY and DISKCOMP next.  Still v0.61.

WHAT THEY DID WITH DMF BEFORE.  di_shape read the BPB and found no
row of di_sizes for 21 sectors, so g_row was FFh: a DMF disk could be
compared, and copied onto a disk that was already DMF, but nothing
could be formatted as one - "only a standard shape can be laid down" -
so a 1.44M or blank target was refused.

DMF IS NOW di_sizes' NINTH ROW, with FDM_1440 as its medium: the same
density, so DISKCOPY formats a 1.44M target as DMF and refuses a 720K
one as it would a 1.44M source.  di_can became words to have a bit 8
(1.44M and 2.88M drives take it).  FORMAT's fd_sizes still stops at
eight rows; DMF is a disk to copy, not to make.

FDF_BEGIN KNOWS DMF BY ITS 21 SECTORS: FDM_1440 with more than 18 in
CL.  No BIOS has AH=18h for it, so the BIOS is asked for 1.44M - which
sets the data rate - and the table it answers with is copied to
GV_FDPT and given 21 sectors and a format gap of 0Ch, Linux's figure
for its 1.68M type (drivers/block/floppy.c, "H1680").  A BIOS without
AH=18h starts from its own table, as before.  FDF_TRACK lays a DMF
track down two to one - 1, 12, 2, 13 ... 21, 11 - as Microsoft's DMF
disks are and as Linux does for any format gap under 22h: twelve bytes
between sectors is too little for anything that reads one sector a
call to catch the next, and such a reader would otherwise wait a whole
turn of the disk for every sector.

DISKCOMP SAID A DISK AND ITS OWN COPY DIFFERED.  DISKCOPY gives the
copy a serial number of its own, and the header of DISKCOMP.ASM said
"DOS's DISKCOMP said so too".  It did not: 6.22's DISKCOMP, run under
DOSBox-X's DOS on the same two images, says "Compare OK", and the 6.0
source says why - VOLSER copies the first disk's serial over the
second's in the buffer before track 0 is compared, when the first's
media byte is Fxh and its boot signature 28h or 29h.  dk_volser does
the same.  It hides nothing else: a pair differing in one more byte
of track 0 - in the second sector, or in the boot sector's OEM name -
is still "Compare error on side 0, track 0", in 6.22 and here.

VERIFIED on 86Box, vli486sv2g with B: added to a copy of its CMOS:
DISKCOPY A: B: of a full DMF disk onto a blank DMF-sized image -
"Copying 80 tracks, 21 sectors per track", "Formatting while copying",
a serial number - and the two images then differ in the four serial
bytes at 27h and nowhere else; the same for 1.44M onto a blank 1.44M
image.  DISKCOMP A: B: of each disk and its copy said "Compare error
on side 0, track 0" before dk_volser and "Compare OK" after, DMF and
1.44M; the DMF pair with a byte changed in track 0's second sector,
and with the OEM name changed, still "Compare error on side 0, track
0" - all four what 6.22's DISKCOMP says of the same images.  RUNTESTS
on all seven machines: SFTSCAN's four addresses moved by 53h, the 83
bytes RMDOS.SYS grew in the entry above, and nothing else; SFTSCAN
re-recorded in BASELINE.  The interleave was checked by running the
address-field arithmetic on the host - 21 places, 21 sectors, each
once - because a raw image keeps no order of sectors and 86Box's
formatter does not object to any.  IOPM, DISKCOPY and DISKCOMP
assemble under ML.

NOT VERIFIED: real hardware - and a real DMF format especially, whose
gap only a real drive can be too fast or too slow for; a DMF format
onto a disk that was a 1.44M one (an emulator's raw 1.44M image cannot
hold 21 sectors a track); a 2.88M drive.

FORMAT MAKES A DMF DISK: /F:1.68 AND /F:DMF (2026-10-02)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for FORMAT /F:1.68 and /F:DMF.  Still v0.61.

THE KERNEL HAD IT ALREADY.  FDF_BEGIN and FDF_TRACK learned DMF for
DISKCOPY in the entry above, so FORMAT only had to ask, and the entry
above's "DMF is a disk to copy, not to make" is no longer so.
fd_sizes has a ninth row: 1680, 3,360 sectors, 21 a track, 4 a
cluster, 16 root entries, 3 a FAT, media F0h, FDM_1440.  That is
Microsoft's own layout, so the BPB FORMAT writes is the one on a DMF
disk of theirs, byte for byte from 0Bh to 3Dh bar the serial number
and the label.  fd_can became words for its bit 8, which 1.44M and
2.88M drives have, as di_can did in DISKIMG.INC.  fm_size takes DMF,
in any case, as the name of 1680; 1.68, 1.68M, 1680 and 1680K are the
number, read as before.

DMF IS NEVER A DRIVE'S DEFAULT.  A disk becomes DMF when /F: says so,
and stays DMF when it was one and nothing says otherwise - what FORMAT
does with every size.  Before, a DMF disk was no row FORMAT knew, so
FORMAT A: on one laid every track down again as a 1.44M disk.

/S ONTO A DMF DISK BOOTS.  BOOT.BIN and FATLOAD read one sector a call
with the BPB's sectors a track, which a table that says 18 does not
stop, and from then on the kernel's fpy_rwup lengthens the table.

VERIFIED on 86Box, vli486sv2g (Award, table 18).  SYS wants its
source to be FAT12 like its target, so the runs boot PM-DOS from a
1.44M floppy in A: and format the disk in B::
  - FORMAT B: /F:DMF /S onto a blank DMF-sized image: "Formatting
    1.68M", 1,716,224 bytes, 838 units of 2,048, "System transferred".
    A 700,000- and a 200,000-byte file copied on.  Read off the image
    on the host with FLOPGET.PL: all seven files byte for byte, both
    FATs the same, the BPB as above, PM-DOS's boot code from 3Eh.
  - that disk in A: of a fresh boot: it booted, FC /B found both
    files the same as copies on C:, and CHKDSK found nothing wrong.
    With a 720K drive as B:, FORMAT B: /F:DMF and /F:1.68 each said
    "Size not supported by drive", and that disk was not changed.
  - on a copy of the same disk: FORMAT B: "Checking 1.68M" (format
    kept, surface read); /Q "Quick format 1.68M"; /F:1.68M /U
    "Formatting 1.68M", every track again, a new serial number;
    /F:dmf /Q quick again; /F:DM "Invalid size for /F"; /F:DMFX
    "Invalid switch".  The file copied on after all that matched on
    the host, and the BPB was still Microsoft's.
6.22's CHKDSK under DOSBox-X's DOS calls every used cluster of every
disk lost, a 1.44M disk MKDISK made as well, so it is no oracle for
this.  6.22's DIR lists the formatted DMF disk correctly.
RUNTESTS on all seven machines: 69 of 69 the same on each, BASELINE
unchanged.  FORMAT.ASM assembles under ML.  FORMAT.COM 7,236 to 7,375
bytes, nothing else changed.

NOT VERIFIED: real hardware, where the gap is the risk, as in the
entry above; a DMF format over a disk that was 1.44M; a 2.88M drive.

SCSI CD-ROMS: AN ADAPTEC 154X OR BUSLOGIC, A PRO AUDIO SPECTRUM, AND
ANY CARD WITH AN ASPI DRIVER (2026-10-03)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for both halves of the plan - a native Adaptec 154x and
BusLogic driver, and the 2940-class cards through their ASPI managers
- and "if at all possible" the SCSI CD-ROM on a sound card.  All
three are in.  Still v0.61.

A CD-ROM UNIT IS NOT AN ATAPI DEVICE ANY MORE.  Everything ATAPI.INC
did that was about the drive and not the bus - READY, the media check,
capacity, READ(10), the sense key that says a disc changed - moved to
IO\CDUNIT.INC (cun_*), working on a table of units, cun_tab, of up to
CDU_MAX (8) entries: a kind, the device behind it and where its
listener bits live.  ATAPI.INC keeps the packet transport and one
entry point, atapi_exec; SCSI's is scs_cdexec.  IOS_CDREAD, CDINFO,
CDCHG, CDPKT and CDUNIT index that table, so MSCD001, MSCDEX and CDEX
did not learn the word SCSI.  ATAPI units come first, so a machine
whose drive was D: yesterday still has it at D:.  CDD_MAXUNIT is
CDU_MAX now, not 4.

THE SCSI LAYER, IO\SCSI.INC, is one service, IOS_SCSI (IOSVC+0F4h,
SSF_* in AH), with a request block (SRQ_*) and an adapter record
(HBA_*) whose first dword is the routine that runs a request.  It
scans targets 0-7, LUN 0, with INQUIRY; keeps a row per device; makes
a unit of each type 5 (CD-ROM) and type 4 (WORM); and does the parts
no adapter should do twice: the bounce through SCSI_BUF (64K at
1F0000h, under 16MB, for a card that only sees 24 bits), REQUEST
SENSE when the card did not, READ(10)/(12)/READ CD split to what the
card can move at once, and MODE SENSE/SELECT(10) sent again as (6) on
an ILLEGAL REQUEST - and as (6) from then on for that drive
(SDF_MODE6).  BUILD scsi6 forces the six-byte forms everywhere, to
test that path on drives that never need it.

  IO\AHA154X.INC   Adaptec 1540/1542 B, C, CF and the BusLogic cards
                   that copy them, ISA at 330h/334h/230h/234h/130h/
                   134h and BusLogic PCI (104Bh:1040h, BAR 0).
                   Polled, one mailbox each way, auto-sense.  84h
                   tells a BusLogic from an Adaptec, 28h/29h unlock a
                   1542C's mailbox as Linux does, and the card's DMA
                   channel is set to cascade.  A PCI BusLogic's
                   ISA-compatible port is asked for (86h) and not
                   probed twice.
  IO\NCR5380.INC   the 53C80 on a Pro Audio Spectrum 16, at 388h,
                   384h, 38Ch or 288h.  No IRQ, no DMA channel: the
                   bus is worked phase by phase, a byte at a time,
                   except READ(10)/(12) in whole 512-byte pieces,
                   which go through the board's pseudo-DMA port
                   (+5C00h).

ASPI IS THE OTHER WAY IN, and it is in PMDOS, DOS\ASPI.INC, because a
manager is a DOS device driver.  After CONFIG.SYS, scsi_start looks
for SCSIMGR$, asks it for its entry point (an IOCTL read of four
bytes), and scans through it.  Every call is made from V86 through
two small stubs in an 8K block of conventional memory, and the wait
for the SRB's status is a loop in V86 too - the manager's interrupt
handler is real-mode code and is only ever delivered to a box.  This
is what reaches an Adaptec 2940, an AIC-7xxx on a motherboard, or the
AIC-6360 on a Sound Blaster 16 SCSI-2: whatever the vendor's manager
drives.

WHY THE PROBE WAITS FOR CONFIG.SYS.  A card a manager has taken must
not be taken again behind its back.  PMIO's probe runs once
CONFIG.SYS is done; told a manager is there (SPF_ASPI), it leaves
alone any 154x whose Return Setup Data shows mailboxes already set up
(the manager's), and a device seen both ways is marked SDF_DUP and
used once.  SCSI=OFF in CONFIG.SYS turns the native drivers off and
leaves ASPI working.

WHAT A PROGRAM SEES.  21h/F1h AL=1Ch reads the adapter and device
rows (SCF_ADAPTER, SCF_DEVICE); AL=17h fills the new CDU_KIND and
CDU_TARGET and gives CDU_DEV/FLAGS/MODE/BASE their SCSI meanings.
CDEX shows "SCSI ID 2", "SCSI 1 ID 2" when there are two adapters,
and lists the adapters under the table.  HWPROBE has a SCSI section:
each adapter's port, IRQ, DMA and own ID, and each device's INQUIRY
strings, CD-ROM or not.  CDATEST gained a volume check (IOCTL input
4, output 3: change output 0's volume, read it back, put it back).
MSCD001's MODE SENSE asks for the block descriptor a SCSI drive sends
and an ATAPI drive never did, and cuts it out before reading the page.

FIVE BUGS THAT WERE NOT IN THIS WORK, all found by it.

  DEVICE= GAVE INIT A BREAK ADDRESS OF 0:0, in a block the size of
  the file.  ASPI4DOS reads that field to see what memory it may use
  and said "Not enough memory available to load driver".  dl_load
  now takes the largest block there is and INIT is told where it
  ends, as DOS tells it.

  A DRIVER'S INT 21h DURING DEVICE= WENT TO THE KERNEL'S 32-BIT
  HANDLERS.  For most calls that is the same answer; for 25h it set
  an IDT gate instead of the real-mode vector.  ASPI4DOS's 25h for
  IRQ 10 vanished, its interrupt never arrived and the first command
  waited for ever.  25h, 35h, 34h, 50h, 51h, 62h, 2Fh, 52h, 38h and
  65h now go to the box's own handlers (dlx_v86fn), and a VDS or
  mouse HLT inside an excursion is served (dlx_nodvs) instead of
  ending it.

  EVERY BIOS CALL THE KERNEL MADE RAN WITH IRQ 9-13 MASKED.
  pic_to_rm forced the slave PIC's mask to 3Eh on the way down.  It
  now leaves unmasked whatever the BIOS had unmasked at boot (read in
  rm_main into GV_BIOSIMR).  Added while chasing the next one; whether
  that BIOS needed it on its own was not separated out.

  A DISK SERVED BY A SCSI CARD'S BIOS HUNG THE BOOT, every release.
  vd_setup sets bit 5 of 40:7Bh and points INT 4Bh at a HLT stub,
  which is right for a box and wrong for rm_int, where a HLT is a HLT.
  A bus-master ROM reads 40:7Bh before it hands its card an address,
  called INT 4Bh, halted till the next tick, and carried on with a
  descriptor nobody had filled in - on the kernel's very first INT
  13h, before CONFIG.SYS.  rm_int now takes VDS away for the call
  (vd_rmdown, vd_rmup) and puts it back.  Before: hung on a 1542CF,
  old kernel and new alike, with SCSI=OFF too.  After: boots from the
  SCSI disk on a 1542CF, a BT-545S and a BT-958D, each card's BIOS
  serving C: while PMIO drives the CD-ROM on the same card.

  THE REAL-MODE STUB DID NOT FIT UNDER MASM.  The BIOS-mask lines
  above pushed it to 0912h, past RMT_PARK at 0900h (wasm, which
  shortens more jumps, had 08EEh).  RMT_PARK is 0940h now; RMDOS is
  handed the unpark address, so nothing outside PMIO moves.  That also
  makes BUILD debug, and every target with PMDOS_DEBUG, assemble
  again - under wasm too they had been over the line before this work
  began.

VERIFIED on 86Box (p3bf, Pentium II, unless it says otherwise), CDEX,
CDXTEST and CDATEST each run - 26 checks - with FC /B of files read
off the disc:
  - native: AHA-1542B, 1542C, 1542CF; BusLogic BT-542B, BT-545S,
    BT-958D (PCI); Pro Audio Spectrum 16.  BUILD scsi6 on the 1542C
    and the PAS16.
  - drives: 86Box's own, Chinon CDS-431, Toshiba XM-3301TA, NEC 25,
    Plextor PX-32TS, TEAC CD-50 all pass; a Sony CDU-541 passes all
    but the volume check (below).
  - 300,000- and 1,600,000-byte files byte for byte through COPY, a
    DOS box's COPY and FC, on the 1542C, the BT-958D, the PAS16 and
    through ASPI.
  - ASPI: a 1542B with ASPI4DOS loaded by DEVICE=, with SCSI=OFF and
    with the native probe on (which left the card alone).
  - an ATAPI and a SCSI CD-ROM together: D: and E:, ATAPI first;
    CDROM=M made them M: and N:.
  - two SCSI CD-ROMs and a SCSI disk on one 1542C: HWPROBE lists the
    disk and both drives, only the drives get letters.
  - a 386DX/33 ISA board (asus386, 8MB) with a PAS16 and a 1542B at
    once: one drive on each, both read correctly.
  - the BIOS-served SCSI disk above: a 1.6MB file copied from the CD
    on the card to the disk on it and compared both ways.
RUNTESTS on all seven machines: 67 of 69 the same; HWPROBE (the new
SCSI lines) and RMTEST (free space, PMIO's first jump) re-recorded.
Every .ASM assembles under ML 6.13, and IOPM.ASM also with scsi6,
DBG_LPT, ATA_DEBUG and FDD_DEBUG.  PMIO.SYS 45,217 to 51,505 bytes,
PMDOS.SYS 136,410 to 138,206.

LIMITS.  Targets 0-7 and LUN 0 only, so a changer shows one drive
and IDs 8-15 on a wide card are not looked at.  Native cards are
polled and never use their IRQ.  Through ASPI, the card's IRQ has to
be one a box can have - 3-5, 7 or 9-11 (VP_GUEST); on 12, 14 or 15
every request times out.  At most 4 adapters, 16 devices, 8 CD units.

NOT VERIFIED: real hardware of any of it.  A real 2940 or any
AIC-7xxx manager - ASPI was proved with ASPI4DOS only, and only on a
1542B: on a 1542C or CF it says "Unable to read configuration from
host adapter", and says the same under MS-DOS 5, so that is the
emulation and that ASPI4DOS, not PM-DOS.  A Sound Blaster 16 SCSI-2
with its ASPI driver.  SDF_DUP, which nothing here could make happen.
A disc changed in a SCSI drive while the machine runs: it goes through
the same cun_note as ATAPI, which SWAPTEST proved, but the swap needs
86Box's menus clicked and was not run.  The Sony CDU-541's volume:
the drive has only its vendor's audio page (09h), not page 0Eh, so
CDATEST's volume step fails there and the rest pass.

THE FOUR THE PCI WORK LEFT: THE TIMER IN A BOX, A RESIDENT DRIVER'S
INTERRUPT AT THE PROMPT, THE 8237, AND ISAPNP.EXE (2026-10-03)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

The PCI entry ended with five things not done, each its own piece of
work.  Charlie asked for four of them.  New: IO\VTIMER.INC, IO\VDMA.INC,
DOS\IRQX.INC, CMD\ISAPNP\ (ISAPNP.C, DOSINT.ASM), IOS_BOXIRQ, BUS_DMASTAT
and BUS_PNPHERE/RES/REGS/SET, and four tests: TIMERTST.COM, IRQXTEST.COM
with IRQXWAIT.EXE, DMATEST.COM.  Still v0.61.

1.  THE TIMER, IN A BOX (IO\VTIMER.INC).  INT 08h and INT 1Ch had
never been called in a DOS box: IRQ 0 was the kernel's clock and went
nowhere else.  Every tick is now owed to the box (vpc_tick) and goes
in through the box's controller like a card's interrupt, in service
until the EOI - VP_DELIVER is VP_GUEST and line 0.  The box's INT 08h
reaches a STUB of the kernel's, not the ROM's handler: the stub calls
INT 1Ch and sends the EOI, and the rest of the BIOS's handler is the
kernel's, because 40:6C is counted in protected mode and the floppy
motor belongs to the kernel's floppy calls - the ROM's handler run in
the box as well would count every tick twice.  The stub hands real
mode to the ROM (SMSW: PE clear is rm_int or a park), and a byte of its
own hands Windows' V86 to the ROM too (vt_park clears it at a park).
Nothing listening - INT 08h still the stub and INT 1Ch still the ROM's
IRET - and the tick is dropped rather than delivered as five traps to
nowhere.  The stub lives in the bus paragraphs, so BUS_PARAS is 4.

A GAME THAT RUNS THE TIMER FASTER gets INT 08h as often as it asked:
43h and 40h are claimed and WATCHED, not stood in for - every byte
reaches the 8254 - and the divisor is kept, so irq_timer counts a tick
of 40:6C every 65536 counts of the timer's input (vt_tick).  The old
kernel's clock ran four times fast under a 4x timer: 146 ticks in two
seconds of the real-time clock.  The motor countdown is per tick too.
A key is no longer handed to a box whose timer handler is in service
(the 8259 would make it wait, and its non-specific EOI would have
ended the timer's).

2.  A RESIDENT DRIVER'S INTERRUPT WITH NO BOX RUNNING (DOS\IRQX.INC).
An interrupt owed to the box waited, line shut, for the next program
that ran in one - so at the native prompt a packet driver, a serial
port's driver or a clock TSR heard nothing.  Now the DOS side makes an
EXCURSION at the two moments it is idle enough to: dos_idle (every
wait for a key) and the end of every native program's DOS call
(i21_r3native).  The handler runs as a simulated interrupt through
dpmi_simint - INT 28h's own road - on the waiting box's stack, or the
scratch real-mode stack when there is no box.  IOS_BOXIRQ hands out
the lines most urgent first (BXI_TAKE is vpc_boxwant from outside the
monitor); while it runs, keys and mouse events stay the kernel's
(v86_irqx).  InDOS is 1 at both moments.  The four calls that start
or end a program fail in it (ERR_FUNC); INT 20h and 27h are ignored;
a fault, ^C or Abort in a handler ends the EXCURSION (irx_lost) and
not a box, which with no box would have unwound into nothing; nothing
parks for Windows from inside one.  A native program that makes no
calls at all still holds an interrupt off until it does.

3.  THE 8237 (IO\VDMA.INC).  A driver hands the DMA controller segment
times sixteen, which in upper memory and the page frame is the address
of somewhere else.  Both controllers' ports and seven page registers
are the monitor's now.  What a box writes to a channel is KEPT, and
the real channel is programmed at the UNMASK: the box's buffer looked
up in the page tables (vd_run) - where it says is where it is, and the
box's own numbers go to the controller; in one piece below 16MB and
across no 64K (128K) line, the controller is sent where it really is;
neither, and it goes through DMA_BUF, 32K at 1E1000h (16K in a trace
kernel, whose buffers move up behind it), copied in for a transfer
from memory and out as a transfer into memory goes - at every look at
a DMA port and before any interrupt reaches the box (vpc_take), which
between them are every moment a driver can learn a transfer ended.
Reading back tells the box its own story: the current address turned
back into the box's, the terminal-count bits kept until the box reads
them.  The flip-flop the box toggles is a copy; the real one is the
kernel's.  REFUSED, with the channel left masked and counted
(BUS_DMASTAT): an auto-initialising transfer that would need the
bounce buffer (a ring cannot be copied behind the card's back), the
buffer when another channel has it, and any buffer the box could not
write itself - a DMA channel was a way to write into the kernel.  A
channel the kernel keeps (4, and an AHA-154x's, from aha_cascade) is
not the box's to touch.  VDS 810Bh/810Ch now really switch translation
off and on for a channel, counted as the specification counts them.

4.  ISAPNP.EXE.  The kernel numbers the cards at boot and switches on
only the IDE port it needs; on a machine whose BIOS is not Plug and
Play everything else stays off, and that was CTCM's job.  ISAPNP lists
every card and device with what it uses; /A switches on every device
that is off, with the first set it offers in which nothing collides
with what can be seen - an AT's ports, all four COM and three LPT
addresses, PCI lines, lines the kernel keeps or a resident driver has
unmasked, the kernel's DMA channels, the other cards, ten-bit aliases
unless a descriptor says sixteen; "c.d IO=220,330,388 IRQ=5 DMA=1,5"
sets one by hand, what is not given staying as it is, and ON/OFF alone
switch it.  /A never chooses memory and leaves the kernel's IDE port
alone.  The kernel's half is four BUS_ calls in ISAPNP.INC (resource
data, registers 30h-0AFh, register writes - none below 30h); F1h/12h
has r3_pflags rows for their buffers and fF1_bus checks each with
cbuf_ok.

VERIFIED.  DOSBox-X, seven machines, RUNTESTS 75 of 75 twice over
(the baselines re-recorded: the bus paragraphs moved everything three
paragraphs, PROBE13 now shows INT 08h at the stub, CACHETST's "a write
is owed" is 5 again with PMIO bigger).  The OLD kernel on the new
tests: TIMERTST fails every check, IRQXWAIT waits for ever, DMATEST
gets nothing into upper memory or two EMS pages and lets the card
write 256 bytes into PMDOS.SYS.  DMATEST with a Sound Blaster (DBXRUN
-Sound: DOSBox-X answers a recording with 80h through the DMA
controller): conventional, upper memory (C4010h is really 249010h),
two EMS pages mapped out of order through the bounce buffer, and the
kernel refused.  86Box P3B-F with an NE2000 and an SB16: PCITEST,
NICIRQ, VPICTEST, VDSTEST, the four DPMI tests, TIMERTST, DMATEST (the
real 8237 and its card) and the IRQX pair, all passed.  86Box 486
(vli486sv2g, no PnP BIOS - Charlie's 486) with Creative's SB32 PnP:
everything off but the CD-ROM's port; /A gave Audio 220 330 388, IRQ 5,
DMA 1 5 - CTCM's own - WaveTable 620, Game 200, StereoEnhance 100;
DMATEST found the card and recorded through it; IO=240 moved it, OFF
switched it off, IO=220 brought it back.  MASM-clean, 113 files;
SYMCASE clean.

TRAPS MET.
  - v86_claim spends AL: a loop that keeps its port in EAX claims one
    port and then whatever the bit mask says, for ever, and the boot
    stops at "Starting PM-DOS...".
  - wasm's case folding, twice: VT_STUB and vt_stub, SB_RESET and
    sb_reset.  And PowerShell's: a [string] parameter $Cfg and a local
    $cfg are one variable, and an 86Box configuration written through
    it is one line, which 86Box answers by becoming an IBM PC.
  - DOSBox-X's -silent switches the sound devices off whatever the
    configuration says: no BLASTER, no SB in MIXER.  DBXRUN -Sound
    leaves it off; the dummy video driver is what keeps the window
    away.
  - DOSBox-X's Plug and Play cards are read-only: their resource data
    and registers read, a write to any register is ignored.  Writing
    is tested on 86Box (run86.ps1-style, started minimized and never
    activated, closed with WM_CLOSE).
  - RUNTESTS splits -Run on commas, so "ISAPNP 1.0 IO=220,330" cannot
    be a test there.
  - WIN.INI's run= is a LIST of programs: a second word is a second
    program, not an argument.

FOUND AND LEFT.
  - [Done 2026-10-03: see "THE VECTOR TABLE A BIOS CALL RUNS WITH".]
    THE REAL-MODE VECTOR TABLE AGAIN.  A kernel call into the BIOS runs
    with the guest's vector table and the BIOS's own masks, so an
    interrupt a box's handler hooks is handled THERE when it arrives
    during one - and if the protected-mode side had already queued it
    for the box, it is delivered a second time afterwards.  IRQXTEST's
    clock handler saw it: one call in real mode for every interrupt,
    tens of thousands of calls the clock had not asked for when a test
    read the time (2Ch, which is INT 1Ah in real mode) on every turn of
    a loop.  Keeping a box's owed lines shut during BIOS calls cures
    the second delivery and was tried - and taken out again, because a
    BIOS waits on its own interrupts there (a SCSI card's ROM on its
    card's, the RTC's waits on IRQ 8), and one owed to a box that is
    not running would never be released.  It belongs with the
    real-mode IVT question that is Charlie's to decide.  A handler that
    asks its device, as real ones do, takes a second delivery as
    nothing.
  - Windows 3.1 in standard mode starts, on this kernel and the old
    one alike, and its timer messages never arrive (WINDRV's one-second
    SetTimer never fires), so it never exits; its DOS session hangs as
    before.  386 enhanced mode does not start on either kernel, on
    DOSBox-X or on 86Box.
  - BIN\ and IMAGES\ on S: were not rebuilt (they hold the 2026-10-02
    kernel, from before the SCSI work as well).

NOT DONE.  An auto-initialising DMA transfer through the bounce buffer;
a client with only a real-mode handler, in protected mode when its
interrupt comes (the fifth of the PCI entry's list); an interrupt for a
resident driver while a native program makes no DOS calls at all; a
TSR popping up from the native prompt (INT 9 into an excursion).

NOT VERIFIED.  Real hardware, any of it - ISAPNP on the 486 with its
own card is the one that matters.  A 16-bit DMA channel moving data
(DOSBox-X has no 16-bit recording); a refused auto-init; two channels
wanting the bounce buffer at once.

THE VECTOR TABLE A BIOS CALL RUNS WITH, AND THE INTERRUPTS IT LOST
(2026-10-03)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Left open by the kernel's memory protection two days ago (written up
at the end of this entry, which it never was), and found again by the
entry above: when the kernel called the BIOS, the BIOS ran with the
vector table every DOS box writes.  Charlie chose a copy of it taken
when CONFIG.SYS is finished.  Testing that found the 8259s losing
interrupts on every call, which the copy made it possible to stop.
New: IOS_RMFREEZE (rm_freeze, rq_down and rq_up in IO\RMCALL.INC),
IORM.ASM's RMT_IRQS entries with rq_timer, rq_rtc, pic_down and
pic_up, vd_freeze, BIOS_IVT, GV_BIDTR and six more globals, and
TOOLS\RMIVT.ASM.  PMIO.SYS 54,666 to 54,937 bytes, PMDOS.SYS 138,994
to 139,000.  Still v0.61.

THE TABLE AT 0:0 IS EVERY PROGRAM'S.  A DOS box writes it with 25h and
a DPMI client with 0201h, and rm_int loaded it - LIDT base 0 - and
turned interrupts on for the call, because the BIOS's disk code waits
on them.  So whatever a program had put on a vector the BIOS reaches
during a call ran in real mode, inside the kernel, with paging off:
the timer and INT 1Ch, the clock's interrupt, INT 15h, and INT 13h,
1Ah, 14h and 17h themselves, which the kernel calls by number.  Three
things followed from that:
  - No page is read-only in real mode, so any 16-bit program, or any
    DPMI client through 0201h, could write anywhere in memory.  That
    undid the protection below.
  - A program that died with INT 1Ch hooked took the whole machine
    down at the next diskette read, where in a box only the box would
    have gone.
  - An interrupt protected mode had already owed to a box was also
    run down there, so the box had it twice (the entry above).
RMIVT on the old kernel: its INT 1Ah hook was called in real mode on
all 100 of a hundred 2Ch calls, on every machine.

1.  THE COPY (rm_freeze, IOS_RMFREEZE).  dos_entry calls it once,
after config_run, scsi_start and cd_announce and before the first
shell: 1K at BIOS_IVT, the last of the gap under SCSI_BUF, on a page
ring 3 cannot write and no box can reach.  GV_BIDTR is the IDTR
rm_land loads - {3FFh, 0} until then, {3FFh, BIOS_IVT} after; park_land
still loads rm_idtr, because a park hands the machine over and the
table at 0:0 goes with it.  WHY AFTER CONFIG.SYS: a DEVICE= driver or
an INSTALL= program that hooks the BIOS is in the copy, and the
kernel's calls go on reaching it; what AUTOEXEC.BAT runs, and
everything after, is a program.  A box's own INT 13h, 1Ah and the
rest still go through the box's own table.  Two things in the copy
are changed:
  - INT 4Bh is vd_old, the vector from before the kernel put its VDS
    stub there.  That is what vd_rmdown gives a call anyway: the stub
    is a HLT that only means something in a box (vd_freeze).
  - The sixteen interrupt lines go to IORM.ASM's RMT_IRQS entries, at
    IRQ_BASE and up (see 3).  Each entry notes its line in GV_RMOWED
    and far-jumps on to where the line went in the copy (RMT_IRQORIG).
    So the BIOS's handler runs, or a CONFIG.SYS driver's, and nothing
    a program hooked since.
The vectors the BIOS reads as data are read at 0:0 by address and not
through IDTR, so GV_RWDPT and the fixed-disk tables still work: the
diskette table at 1Eh, and the fixed-disk tables at 41h and 46h.

rq_up hands the noted lines on afterwards, because the box's handler
is not in the table the BIOS was given:
  - a tick goes to vpc_tick;
  - a box's line goes to vpc_raise, which owes it only if the box has
    the line open;
  - a line the kernel owns outright is its owner's and is not handed
    on.
Two interrupts on one line during one call become one.

2.  TWO LINES ARE NOT PASSED STRAIGHT ON.
LINE 0 (rq_timer).  The ROM's INT 08h counts 40:6C once an interrupt.
While a game ran the timer four times as fast, the clock therefore
counted four times as fast for the length of every call; RMIVT
measured 89 to 116 ticks in two RTC seconds on DOSBox-X and 91 to 102
on the Pentium II.  rq_timer keeps VTIMER's whole-tick count down there:
vt_div and vt_acc go down as GV_VTDIV and GV_VTACC (rq_down) and the
count comes back (rq_up).  Only whole ticks go on to the ROM; the rest
are ended there.
LINE 8 (rq_rtc), FOUND BY THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS.  A program
running the clock's periodic interrupt for itself (IRQXTEST does)
reads register C in its own handler.  The ROM's handler, given that
interrupt instead, read register C itself, found a periodic interrupt
with no wait of its own to time, and did what IBM's does: switched
the periodic interrupt OFF.  On 86Box IRQXTEST got 29 periodic
interrupts where it had had 375.  So line 8 goes to the BIOS only if
the BIOS is timing a wait with it (BDA_RTCWAIT, 40:A0h bit 0) or no
box is listening (GV_RMBOX, set by rq_down).  Otherwise it is masked
for the rest of the call, EOIed, and owed, and the box's own handler
reads register C afterwards.  375 again, and none in real mode.

3.  THE 8259s LOST WHAT WAS WAITING IN THEM, ON EVERY CALL - old, and
not this change's, but the copy is what made it fixable.  The thunk
moved the vector bases both ways, and a base takes a fresh ICW1, which
resets the controllers' request latches.  So an interrupt that arrived
while the switch had interrupts off was delivered on neither side.
With nothing but BIOS calls going on, that cost a tenth of the clock
on 86Box's Pentium II and a quarter on its 486, on the old kernel as
on the new one.  IRRDIAG, a diagnostic build that counted IRQ 0
waiting at each re-initialisation (scratch, not in the tree), found
16 ticks counted and 18 waiting at the normal rate, and 20 counted and
64 waiting at four times the rate.  Both add up to the 36 that two
seconds should give.  A keystroke or a mouse byte arriving in the same
window went the same way.  Since rm_freeze, a BIOS call leaves the
bases where protected mode keeps them:
  - pic_down and pic_up write only the masks, and the copy's IRQ_BASE
    to IRQ_BASE+15 point at the RMT_IRQS entries.
  - 08h to 0Fh and 70h to 77h in the copy stay as they were, for
    anything that calls them as software interrupts.
  - A line the BIOS's masks shut now waits in the controller for
    protected mode instead of being lost.
  - Before CONFIG.SYS is finished, and for a park, the bases move as
    before (GV_PICKEEP, and GV_PICKEPT so that rm_toprot knows which
    way it came).
After this change the clock read 36 or 37 at both rates on all three
emulated machines.  IRQXTEST's "calls the clock did not ask for" on
86Box went from about 16,000 to 1: that number was this too.

WHAT IS LOST BY THE COPY.  A TSR that adds to the BIOS and is loaded
from AUTOEXEC.BAT - a printer redirector on INT 17h, a FOSSIL on
INT 14h, an INT 13h or INT 1Ah extender - no longer sees the kernel's
own calls, so it misses DOS-level printing to PRN and the rest.
CONFIG.TXT says to load such a thing with INSTALL= or DEVICE=.  A
box's own calls to the same vectors are unaffected.

VERIFIED.
  - RMIVT, six checks on seven lines, new kernel against old:
      DOSBox-X:              every line OK; the old kernel fails 1, 3,
                             4b and 6.
      86Box p3bf (PII):      every line OK, 36 and 36; old 100, 22,
                             20,607 calls to IRQ 8 in real mode,
                             31 and 91.
      86Box vli486sv2g:      every line OK, 36 and 36; old 100, 14,
      (Award, 66 MHz)        6,129, 27 (FAILED) and 40.
      p3bf booting off a     every line OK.
      1542CF's BIOS disk:
    IRQXTEST passes on all three emulated machines, with 0 calls made

  - The disk a 1542CF's BIOS serves, booted from and used for
