FOUND AND LEFT.
  - rq_rtc masks line 8 for the rest of a call.  A BIOS that started a
    clock-timed wait of its own later in the same call would wait for
    nothing.  None of the calls the kernel makes is such a wait (INT
    15h AH=83h or 86h), though a BIOS could call one from inside
    another.
  - A key typed during a BIOS call goes through the BIOS's INT 09h
    into the buffer, as before, and a box TSR's INT 09h hook does not
    see it.
  - A BIOS that writes a vector into 0:0 in the middle of one of its
    own calls would not have that vector used.  None of the machines
    tested does this.

NOT VERIFIED.  Real hardware.  A DEVICE= driver on INT 13h (an
INSTALL= TSR on INT 1Ah was tested, at the same point in the boot).
Any BIOS but DOSBox-X's and two Award ones.

THE PROTECTION THIS FINISHES (2026-10-01, NOT WRITTEN UP THEN).
Charlie asked how to stop D32 and DPMI programs writing over the
kernel, and agreed to the first two steps.
  1.  THE KERNEL'S PAGES ARE READ-ONLY TO RING 3.  pg_protect clears
  PG_WRITABLE on every page in the KPROT_* ranges:
    - the stub, the GDT, the globals and XFER (1000h-3FFFh);
    - PMDOS.SYS;
    - 180000h-21FFFFh: the page tables, KBSS, the bounce buffers,
      PMIO, the IDT, the TSS and the kernel stacks;
    - pg_hiram's tables (GV_PGHILO and GV_PGHIHI).
  CR0.WP stays clear, so ring 0 is not affected.  Page 0 stays
  writable, because a DOS program must be able to write the IVT.  The
  A20-off alias copies the HMA's sixteen entries, so the protection
  follows it.
  2.  THE KERNEL ASKS BEFORE IT WRITES FOR A PROGRAM.  usr_wok
  (IOS_USRWOK) asks whether ring 3 could have written a range itself.
  It is asked before every store the kernel makes into memory a
  program chose:
    - buf_ok;
    - a box's stack at v86_run, v86_fault and v86_irqexit (v86_stkok);
    - a client's interrupt frame (vpc_pmchk) and dpmi_enter;
    - 0300h's word copy, and 000Bh, 0300h, 0303h and 0500h
      (dpmi_esdiw);
    - VDS 8103h and 8105h (vd_ddsok);
    - mouse function 16h;
    - XMS 0Bh, which also got real bounds (xms_where).
  Further, DPMI 000Ch refuses a descriptor that is not code or data,
  and the LDT is unloaded for a native child (XN_LDTR) and a native
  handler (RC_LDTR).
What that left, as of this entry:
  - THE BIOS CALL'S VECTOR TABLE: done above.
  - DMA: the 8237 is covered, since VDMA refuses a buffer the program
    could not write.  A PCI card's bus-mastering, and CF8h/CFCh, are
    still open to a box.
  - Pages in the arena are still writable through a DPMI client's
    flat selector.  That is other programs' memory and not the
    kernel's, and would be step 3.
  - There are no hostile test programs proving each protection.

EXPANDED MEMORY GOES TO LIM 4.0 (2026-10-03)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for LIM 4.0 for RMDOS, since 32-bit programs have no
use for it.  It went into DOS\EMS.INC, the manager the DOS boxes
already had, and not into RMDOS.SYS - the first paragraph below says
why.  46h now answers 40h, and every function and subfunction from
4Fh to 5Dh is served.  New: TOOLS\EMS4TEST.ASM (22 checks); the HLT a
56h target returns to, recognised in vdm_halt and in the DEVICE=
excursion (ems_iscb, ems_callret); status codes 90h-A4h, EMS_KEEP,
EMS_CALLSTK and EMS_PMAPENT/EMS_PMAPLEN in PMDOS.INC.  EMS_MAXH 32 to
64, EMS_MAXPAGES 512 to 2048 (8MB to 32MB, 4.0's ceiling), and the
handle table moved to _KBSS.  PMDOS.SYS 139,000 to 141,718 bytes.
Still v0.61.

WHY NOT RMDOS.SYS.  RMDOS runs only while the kernel is parked under
Windows 3.1 standard mode.  Paging is off, there is no V86 monitor,
and the upper memory is gone - park_chaincut ends the chain at 640K
because the UMBs were arena pages under page tables that no longer
exist.  A manager with none of that has nothing to map a window with:
it could only copy 16K in and out of a frame carved from conventional
memory at every map, and a frame that costs 64K below 640K, under a
Windows that swaps DOS programs to disk, is not one anybody would
switch on.  The 16-bit programs that can ask for expanded memory are
the ones in DOS boxes, and that manager is where 4.0 went.

WHAT 4.0 ADDED, AND HOW EACH ONE IS DONE HERE.
  4Fh  partial page map.  The array is a count and then, per window,
       its segment and its 4Eh dword - 2 + 6n bytes - so a restore
       needs nothing but the array and touches only those windows.
  50h  several windows in one call.  55h and 56h take the same list.
  51h  reallocate.  See ONE BLOCK, below.
  52h  attributes: volatile only.  Non-volatile is 91h, anything else
       90h.  A pool rebuilt at every boot has no other honest answer.
  53h  names, eight bytes in the row.  A name another handle has is
       A1h; the empty name is everybody's.
  54h  the directory: the list, a search by name (an empty name is
       A1h, an unknown one A0h), and the number of handles (64).
  55h  map and jump.  INT 67h is trapped, not reflected, so the
       guest's CS:IP is two fields in vdm_ctx and a jump is changing
       them.
  56h  map and call.  See THE CALL, below.
  57h  move and exchange, up to a megabyte, with every refusal the
       specification lists: 92h to 98h, A2h, 83h and 8Ah.
  58h  four mappable pages, the frame's, numbered 0 to 3.
  59h  a raw page is 16K, and there are no alternate or DMA register
       sets.
  5Ah  standard and raw pages, the same 16K, and 0 is allowed.
  5Bh  set 0 and a context save area in the caller's memory.  No
       alternate sets: 03h and 05h answer BL = 0, and any set but 0
       is 9Ch.
  5Ch  nothing to prepare.
  5Dh  the access key.  The first 00h or 01h hands one out; with the
       functions off, 59h/00 and 5Bh are A4h.
And the old ones: 44h's FFFFh unmap is official now, and 43h still
refuses no pages, which is what 5Ah is for.

HANDLE 0 IS THE SYSTEM'S, as 4.0 says: always open, counted by 4Bh,
listed by 4Dh and 54h, emptied but not closed by 45h, and owned by
the kernel so that no program's exit sweep reaches it.  A handle is
now the index of its row and row 0 is that handle, so a program's
first allocation still gets handle 1.  EMSTEST's check 7 had asserted
"one handle open" and now counts against what was open before it
started, which it always should have: a TSR with a handle failed it
too.

ONE BLOCK PER HANDLE, KEPT.  The v0.41 roadmap suggested a list of
blocks per handle.  One block is what makes 57h a memmove and a window
a base plus an offset, so 51h does the work instead:
  - fewer pages: the windows onto the pages going come down
    (ems_cutwin) and the block shrinks where it stands, or is freed
    at 0;
  - more pages: arena_resize grows the block where it stands if the
    arena has free space after it.  Otherwise the handle MOVES - a new
    block, the pages copied, the old block freed - and every window
    showing one of its pages is pointed at the page's new home
    (ems_rewin).
The new block's owner is the ROW's owner, not whoever is running
(ems_blkown).  A TSR's handle grown while another program has the
machine must not be swept when that program ends.

A MAP LIST BECOMES FOUR WINDOW STATES.  50h, 55h and both of 56h's
maps go through ems_listmap, which reads the whole list and reduces it
to KEEP, UNMAPPED or a 4Eh dword for each window before any window
moves.  Applying the pairs one at a time would read the list while the
windows change, and the list is allowed to be in a window.  It also
makes "nothing changes unless every pair is good" free.  ems_setmap
(48h, 4Eh/01, 5Bh/01) copies its sixteen bytes in first for the same
reason, and 4Fh/01 copies its array in.

THE CALL.  56h's far call is 55h; the return is the part with
something to it.  The target's RETF lands on a HLT at EMSH_RET in the
EMMXXXX0 paragraph, and what that HLT needs is on the guest's own stack
under the return address: a signature, the old map as four window
states, and the caller's CS:IP - 26 bytes, which is what 56h/02
reports.  Nothing is held in the kernel between the call and the
return, so calls nest, and a target that never returns costs nothing.
The old map is read at the call and not at the return, because the
caller's list may be in a page the new map takes away.  A handle freed
while the target ran is 83h at the return, and a page shrunk away is
8Ah.  A HLT there with no frame under it ends the box, since there is
no caller to go back to.

94h IS THE ONE OVERLAP THAT ADDRESSES CANNOT SHOW.  A conventional
side inside the frame and an expanded side in the same handle can be
the same memory at two addresses.  ems_alias asks the map, window by
window, whether any window the conventional side crosses is showing a
page of the expanded side.

TWO THINGS A PROGRAM CAN LEAVE BEHIND, and ems_relown clears both when
it ends: 5Bh's save area pointer, which points into the program's own
memory and would have 5Bh/00 writing into whatever is loaded there
next; and 5Dh's key, which nobody is left to give back.

NOT DONE: pages mapped into conventional memory.  4.0 allows it, and
it is what Windows 3.0 real mode and DESQview used to give each
program a bank of its own.  The page tables would take a conventional
page as readily as a frame page.  The reason is the rest of the
kernel, which treats a linear address below A0000h as the physical
one - ata_dmaok for one - so a hole made there by a guest would be a
disk transfer into the wrong memory.  58h offers the four frame pages,
which the specification permits and which is all DOSBox's 4.0 manager
has ever offered.

VERIFIED, DOSBox-X headless, 486, 32MB, EMS=AUTO, frame at E000h:
EMSTEST 14/14 and EMS4TEST 22/22.  EMS4TEST checks memory wherever
there is memory to check: a grown handle still holds what was written,
a 57h move lands across a page line where two windows can see both
halves, a 56h target sees one map and its caller gets the other back,
and 55h's target finds the page it mapped.
CHECK 5 NEEDED A SECOND VERSION.  It grows a handle past a neighbour
so that the handle has to move, then looks through a window that was
onto it.  The first version read the page's pattern through that
window and passed - and passed again with ems_rewin taken out and
every grow forced to move, because the old block, freed, still held
every byte.  A stale window reads the right answer.  It now WRITES
through the old window and reads through one mapped after the grow.
With that, the same control fails at check 5 alone, and the forced
move with ems_rewin left in passes.  A check that cannot fail tests
nothing, and the only way to find out is to break the code on
purpose.
Also with EMS=: a 4MB 386 (AUTO, 109 pages); a 1GB Pentium with
EMS=D000 (2048 pages, the ceiling, and the segment arithmetic of 4Fh,
50h and 58h at a frame that is not E000h); and the 486 with UMBTEST,
MCBTEST, XMSTEST, DPMITEST and TSRTEST in front and both EMS tests run
twice, the second runs showing the first left nothing behind.  All
clean; what differs from the no-EMS baselines is the frame itself
(the header paragraph in the chain, upper memory ending at E000h, and
64K more XMS because the frame's pages are not backed).
86Box agrees: p3bf, Pentium II, 64MB, EMS=AUTO puts the frame at
D000h there, and EMSTEST 14/14, EMS4TEST 22/22.
Regression: RUNTESTS -All, the seven machines without EMS=, 74 of 76
the same on every one.  RMFIND and RMTEST moved only because \TESTS
has one more file and the disk 9 fewer free clusters (EMS4TEST.COM,
and PMDOS.SYS three clusters longer); both are re-recorded.
MASM 6.13 is clean on DOSMAIN.ASM, EMSTEST.ASM and EMS4TEST.ASM.

NOT VERIFIED: the 486; real programs that use 4.0 - ones
that grow a handle with 51h, overlay managers on 55h and 56h, RAMDRIVE
/A; 56h from a DEVICE= driver's INIT, which is wired up but has no
test.  EMS4TEST is not in RUNTESTS' default list, because no baseline
machine boots with EMS=.

SAFE MODE: SHIFT OR F5 AT "STARTING PM-DOS..." (2026-10-03)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for a safe-mode boot: hold Shift, or press F5, while
"Starting PM-DOS..." is on the screen, and CONFIG.SYS and AUTOEXEC.BAT
are bypassed, with a message saying so; and a blank line after the
"Starting" message.  It is DOS 6's clean boot (sysinit2.asm kbd_read
and disable_autoexec in S:\DOS6SRC), and works the way that one did.
F8, the line-by-line confirmation, is not done.  Still v0.61.

WHAT A BOOT DOES NOW.
  - PMIO prints "Starting PM-DOS..." and a blank line, and puts 40:6C
    in GV_BOOTTICK (GV_BASE+0D4h).
  - kb_init clears the BIOS's ring and 40:17, as it always has.  First
    kb_bootkeys notes in GV_BOOTKEY (GV_BASE+0D8h) whether a Shift was
    down and whether an F5 was anywhere in the ring - a key pressed
    while the files were loading counts, as it did under DOS 6, and a
    Shift held since power-on need not repeat for the kernel to see
    it.
  - config_run reads CONFIG.SYS into cfg_buf as before, then walks it
    once for SWITCHES= alone (CFG_PASS_KEYS, a new first walk), then
    calls cfg_keys - before a single statement is acted on.
  - cfg_keys waits until 37 ticks after GV_BOOTTICK, ending early at a
    key in the ring, a Shift in 40:17, or anything in GV_BOOTKEY; HLT
    between looks.  Then: Shift down, or the first key in the ring is
    F5, or GV_BOOTKEY says either - and every F5 at the front of the
    ring is taken off it, because people press it more than once and
    the rest would reach the prompt.  A first key that is not F5 is
    left alone and the boot is normal.
  - Bypassed: "Safe mode: skipping CONFIG.SYS and AUTOEXEC.BAT." and a
    blank line, " /D" is appended to shell_tail, and config_run
    returns without a walk.  With no CONFIG.SYS at all the keys are
    still looked at, since they are how AUTOEXEC.BAT is skipped.
The two seconds are two seconds of the clock RUNNING: 40:6C stands
still from the CLI in the real-mode stub to the STI in pm_entry.
Measured on DOSBox-X: 2.4 s from the message to the first CONFIG.SYS
line - 0.4 s of probing with interrupts off before the mouse line
went up, then the 2.0 s wait.

SWITCHES= IS HALF REAL.  /N turns the keys off and /F skips the wait
(a key pressed before it still counts), as in DOS 6; /K, /W and /E
stay accepted and inert.  cfg_switches is in phase CFG_PASS_KEYS in
cfg_phaseof, so the main walk skips it.  DISK\CONFIG.SYS had
SWITCHES=/F, written when it did nothing - left there it would have
taken the wait away from every image built from that file, and
tapping F5 at the message would have missed most of the time.  It is
SWITCHES=/K now.

/D IN BOTH SHELLS.  DOS 6's COMMAND.COM took /D as "no AUTOEXEC.BAT
and no date and time prompt" (init.asm, PrdAttm), and IO.SYS added it
to the shell's tail for a clean boot.  CMD.EXE had no /D: cmd_startup
now sets noauto_flag and skips bat_launch of AUTOEXEC.BAT when it is
set.  The 16-bit COMMAND.COM accepted /D and ignored it - its header
said so - so COMMAND /P /D ran AUTOEXEC.BAT anyway, which 6.22's does
not; in_noauto now skips in_autoexec, date and time with it.  Both /?
screens list /D.  The /D stays on shell_tail for the session, so a
shell that is reloaded after a fault does not run AUTOEXEC.BAT either.

Files: INC\PMDOS.INC (GV_BOOTTICK, GV_BOOTKEY, BOOTK_*), IO\IORM.ASM
(the two globals), IO\IOPM.ASM, IO\KEYBD.INC (kb_bootkeys),
DOS\CONFIG.INC (CFG_PASS_KEYS, BOOTKEY_WAIT, cfg_keys, ck_any,
cfg_switches, msgCfgSafe, cfg_nokeys, cfg_nowait), DOS\DOSMAIN.ASM
(comment), CMD\BATCH.INC, CMD\CMD.ASM, CMD\COMMAND\INIT16.INC,
CMD\COMMAND\HELPTEXT.INC, DISK\CONFIG.SYS, DISK\CONFIG.TXT (the keys
in the introduction, a SWITCHES= entry).  PMIO.SYS 54,937 to 55,039
bytes, PMDOS.SYS 141,718 to 142,055.

VERIFIED on DOSBox-X, headless.  The keys were put in before "boot"
by two tiny programs run in DOSBox-X's own DOS: INT 16h AH=05h for
F5, and bit 1 of 40:17 for a Shift.  The test CONFIG.SYS had SET and
a bad line; AUTOEXEC.BAT echoed and wrote two files.
  - No key: the blank line, the bad line reported, AUTOEXEC.BAT run.
  - F5, and Shift: the safe-mode line, no CONFIG.SYS error, no files
    written, a clean prompt.
  - F5 with SWITCHES=/N: a normal boot.  F5 with "switches = /k /f":
    safe mode.  F5 with no CONFIG.SYS: safe mode, AUTOEXEC.BAT
    skipped.  No CONFIG.SYS and no key: AUTOEXEC.BAT runs.
  - Timing, from screen captures at 70 frames a second: 2.0 s from
    the mouse line to the first CONFIG.SYS line; none with
    SWITCHES=/F, and none with a key waiting.
  - Control: the S:\BIN kernel with the same F5 boots normally.
  - A TEST-ONLY variant whose kb_init puts the BIOS's keys back into
    the ring, and its Shift into kb_flags, instead of GV_BOOTKEY - so
    the keys reach cfg_keys the way one pressed during the wait does:
    three F5s all taken off (clean prompt), Shift via 40:17 bypasses,
    and "x" then F5 boots normally with no wait.
  - COMMAND /P /D from AUTOEXEC.BAT: straight to its prompt.  The old
    COMMAND.COM ran AUTOEXEC.BAT nine times over, until "Program too
    big to fit in memory".
  - MASM 6.13: all 115 .ASM files clean.
Regression: RUNTESTS -All, 76 of 76 the same on all seven machines,
with no baseline re-recorded (its CONFIG.SYS has no SWITCHES=, so
every row now waits the two seconds).

VERIFIED BY CHARLIE on 86Box (the PM-DOS VM, after S:\BIN, HD16.IMG
and PMDOS.IMG were brought up to date): F5 or Shift pressed by hand
at "Starting PM-DOS..." bypasses the startup files.  That was the one
test headless runs could not make - DOSBox-X's AUTOTYPE crashes it.
NOT VERIFIED: the 486.  F8 is not done.

THE CLEAN-SHUTDOWN FLAG, AND CHKDSK AT BOOT (2026-10-03)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for a partition dirty flag and CHKDSK on boot.  The
flag is kept by the kernel, in a new DOS\VOLFLAG.INC, and the check is
run BY THE KERNEL, before the shell, the way NT's autochk runs before
anything else - so it does not depend on which interpreter SHELL=
names, and nothing has touched the disk when it starts.  Still v0.61.

WHICH BIT.  Windows 95's: bit 15 of FAT entry 1 on FAT16, bit 27 on
FAT32, set meaning clean.  Using the same one means a disk Windows 98
left dirty is checked here and one PM-DOS left dirty is checked by
ScanDisk there, and every FORMAT ever written, ours and MKDISK
included, already leaves it set.  FAT12 has no spare bit, so
diskettes have no flag; neither do a loaded block driver's units, a
CD-ROM or a mounted image, which are not this kernel's disks to vouch
for.  vol_vf in vol_state (out of a pad byte, so VOL_STATE_SIZE does
not move) says whether the loaded volume has it.  The bit beside it,
Windows' "no disk error" bit (14 / 26), is left exactly as found:
nothing here does the surface scan it asks for.

WHEN IT GOES OFF, AND WHEN IT COMES BACK.  CACHE.INC already promises
that at every commit point - the prompt (CMD.EXE and COMMAND.COM both
call 0Dh before printing one), a program starting, a program ending,
2Fh's commit - the disk says what the filesystem says.  So a volume
is consistent at a commit point unless a file is open on it with
writes its directory entry does not have yet (SFTF_DIRTY), and the
bit follows exactly that:
  - OFF before the first write after the volume was last marked
    clean.  disk_write calls vfl_touch, which sets DRVF_DIRTY FIRST
    (the bit's own write comes back through disk_write), writes FAT
    sector 0 to every copy with the bit off, and pushes those sectors
    out of the cache at once (cache_flushrange), so the mark is on the
    disk ahead of anything written after it.  If fatsec_buf holds
    sector 0 it gets the bit too, or its next flush would put the old
    bit back.
  - ON at the end of dos_commit (vfl_cleanall), after both flushes,
    for every DRVF_DIRTY volume that is not held, if the cache owes
    nothing at all and no SFT on the drive has SFTF_DIRTY.
Turning the machine off at the prompt therefore leaves every volume
clean; so does a crash in a game that writes nothing.  A crash while
a program has a file half written leaves that volume dirty, which is
the truth.  The cost is one sector per FAT copy when a volume goes
dirty and again when it comes back: per command that writes, not per
write.  A redirected program costs four of them, because the create
of the redirect file dirties C: and 4Bh's commit cleans it again
before the program writes; that was judged cheaper than leaving every
long-running program's drive dirty from its start.

RAW WRITES TOO.  vol_syncdrv has a MODE 2: mode 0, plus vfl_touch on
every volume in the range - asked for by the three writers that know
they are writing: INT 26h (disk_absgo, by the service), 21h/7305h
(f75_write) and a DOS box's INT 13h write (i13_flush, by
i13_iswrite).  A disk utility stopped halfway is precisely the volume
that wants checking.  And a raw write may land ON the bit: mode 1
afterwards calls vfl_after, which reads it back when the range held
sector 0 of a FAT copy.  CHKDSK /F is the case - it writes back the
FAT it loaded before its first write turned the bit off - and
vfl_after turns it off again.  F1h AL=0Dh/0Eh (FDISK's) does not sync
at all and does not mark; i13_reflect (unknown INT 13h functions)
unmounts the whole disk, and the remount reads the bit.

WINDOWS 3.1.  RMDOS writes without knowing any of this, so park_go
marks every volume with the flag dirty after its commit
(vfl_parkmark), vfl_parked keeps every commit from cleaning one, and
park_recover clears it after park_remount.  A crash inside Windows is
then a check at the next start, as it was on Windows 95.

FOUND OFF, AND HELD.  A volume found dirty at a mount that the kernel
did not make dirty (DRVF_DIRTY clear) was left that way by a crash or
another system, and gets DRVF_HOLD: no commit cleans it, because only
a check knows whether it is sound.  Found clean, both flags go - a
FORMAT, or another system's checker, has said so.  The two flags are
DRV_FLAGS bits 20h and 40h in the volume table rather than vol_state
bytes, because a remount re-reads the bit and must know whether the
kernel put it there: SYS writing a boot sector unmounts the volume it
has just written files to, and the remount must not take the kernel's
own mark for a crash.  vfl_found is the one rule, used by the mount
(vfl_mounted, out of the FAT sector fat_checkmedia already reads - it
now reads the LIVE copy, fat_rdcopy) and by vfl_after.

CHKDSK SAYS SO through the new 21h/F1h AL=1Dh: DL = drive (0 =
default), bits 16-23 of EAX = VLF_QUERY or VLF_CHECKED, answer EAX =
VLS_KEPT/DIRTY/HOLD.  VLF_CHECKED drops the hold; the next commit -
CHKDSK's own reset, or its 4Ch - turns the bit on.  CHKDSK calls it
(sys_mark_checked, before the final reset) after a whole /F run, or
after a look without /F that reported nothing (errors_seen, the
cross-link count), and never when part of the tree was not processed
(st.ftrunc) or the run ended early.  A DOS BOX CAN ONLY QUERY:
vdm_do21 hands the kernel AX, not EAX, so the function bits never
arrive - true of every F1h family that takes one there (12h, 14h,
16h, 1Ah, 1Ch).  Noticed, not changed.

AT BOOT, after CONFIG.SYS and rm_freeze, vfl_bootscan mounts every
volume that can have the flag (crit_busy, so a bad one is quiet now
and complains at its first real use as before) and lists the held
ones in ack_list.  Mounting them all at boot is new; each costs a few
sector reads.  shell_restart then calls ack_next before loading the
shell: CHKDSK X: /F is loaded into the shell's slot and started the
way the shell is, and its 4Ch at depth 0 comes back to shell_restart
like the shell's would - so the next drive, then the shell, follow on
their own, and ^C or a fault in CHKDSK skips that drive and no more.
CHKDSK.EXE is looked for beside shell_name, then in the root of the
boot drive (shell_dflt's letter).  AUTOCHECK=ON|ASK|OFF in CONFIG.SYS
(cfg_autocheck; ON the default): ASK takes Y or N from the keyboard,
OFF only names the drive.  A safe-mode start turns ON into ASK
(cfg_keys), since CHKDSK at boot could be what needed one.  The
messages:
    Drive C: was not shut down properly. Running CHKDSK C: /F.
    Drive C: was not shut down properly. Run CHKDSK C: /F now (Y/N)?
    Drive C: was not shut down properly. Run CHKDSK C: /F to check the drive.
    Cannot find CHKDSK.EXE to check drive C:.
CHKDSK /F still asks "Convert lost chains to files (Y/N)?" when it
finds some, as it always has, so a boot can wait for an answer.

TOOLS\VFTEST.ASM -> \TESTS\VFTEST.COM (new, in BUILD.CMD, both MKHD
lists, the floppy and RUNTESTS): ten checks of the bit as the kernel
reports it and as 7305h reads it off the disk - after a commit, a
file open and written, a commit with it open, closed, a delete, a
letter that does not exist, and raw writes of FAT sector 1, FAT
sector 0 and the boot sector.  It holds everything it prints until
the end, because its output goes to a file on C: and the first
version's own lines kept C: dirty.  VFTEST Q prints one line of
state; VFTEST HANG writes a file, leaves it open and spins, for a rig
to pull the plug on; HANGC commits first, so the clusters are on the
disk and the directory entry is not - a lost chain.

SHUTDOWN.EXE: THE POWER SWITCHED OFF THROUGH ACPI (2026-10-04)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for a new external command, SHUTDOWN.EXE, that switches
off a machine with ACPI and a soft power switch, and on one without
ACPI just says "ACPI not found." and stops.  Still v0.61.

THE KERNEL DOES IT, IN ONE CALL: 21h/F1h AL=1Eh.  A program at ring 3
can reach neither the tables (physical memory, usually just above
what E820 calls usable) nor the port, and only the kernel knows what
it still owes the disks.  SHUTDOWN.EXE (CMD\SHUTDOWN, 756 bytes)
parses its tail and turns the call's error into a sentence.  /?
anywhere on the line is help and any other argument is "Invalid
parameter": a command that switches the machine off must not do it
because a switch it does not know was mistyped.

THE ORDER, in fF1_power:
  1. find ACPI (IOS_ACPI, ACPF_FIND) - before anything is written, so
     "ACPI not found." leaves the machine exactly as it was;
  2. every open file that has been written to gets its directory
     entry written (sft_flush on each SFT, as 68h would): nothing will
     ever close it now;
  3. dos_commit, which also puts back each volume's clean-shutdown bit
     (VOLFLAG.INC);
  4. a block still owed is a write that failed: ERR_WRFAULT, as 1Bh;
  5. ACPF_OFF, which comes back only if the machine is still running
     three seconds after the write: ERR_STAYEDON.
New errors beside ERR_DISKFULL's 70h: ERR_NOACPI 71h, ERR_NOSOFTOFF
72h, ERR_STAYEDON 73h.  SHUTDOWN says "ACPI not found.", "ACPI
soft-off not supported.", "A disk could not be written. The computer
was not switched off.", or "The computer did not switch off.
Everything has been written to the disks, so the power can be
switched off by hand." - and "This version of PM-DOS cannot switch
the computer off." to a kernel without AL=1Eh.  ERRORLEVEL 1 for all.

IO\ACPI.INC (PMIO, IOS_ACPI = IOSVC+100h):
  - the RSDP, in 16-byte steps through the EBDA's first kilobyte
    (40:0Eh) and E0000h-FFFFFh, believed when its first 20 bytes add
    up to zero;
  - the RSDT, or from 2.0 the XSDT when the RSDT pointer is 0 and the
    XSDT is below 4GB; its entries for 'FACP'.  Every table goes
    through pg_mapphys first, 32 bytes past its length, so a malformed
    \_S5_ at the very end reads memory rather than faults;
  - the FADT: SMI_CMD, ACPI_ENABLE and ACPI_DISABLE, PM1a/PM1b event
    and control, the PM timer.  A 1.0 field of 0 falls back to its
    2.0 GAS when that names an I/O port; TMR_VAL_EXT for 32 bits;
  - \_S5_ IS SEARCHED FOR, NOT RUN: NameOp, optional '\', '_S5_',
    PackageOp, PkgLength, count, integers (Zero, One, Ones, or a
    byte, word or dword after its prefix) - in the DSDT, then each
    SSDT.  An _S5_ worked out in a Method is "no soft-off";
  - the write, as Linux makes it: ACPI mode first if SCI_EN is clear
    (ACPI_ENABLE to SMI_CMD, up to three seconds for SCI_EN, and the
    write is made anyway if it never comes); the fixed-event status
    cleared (8731h); SLP_TYP alone into PM1a and PM1b, then again with
    SLP_EN; three seconds of the PM timer (reads of port 80h without
    one), interrupts off throughout.  Still running: both control
    registers put back as found, ACPI_DISABLE if this put the firmware
    into ACPI mode, and CF;
  - ACPF_REPORT: what was found, in registers.
F1h AL=1Eh bits 16-23: PWF_OFF 0, PWF_QUERY 1 (ACPF_REPORT's
registers, on "no soft-off" too).  A DOS box passes AX alone, so it
can only switch off.  HWPROBE prints the query as its last section,
"ACPI:" - the ports, the sleep types and where in the DSDT they came
from - so a machine that will not switch off can be reported on.

THE THING TO KNOW: A BIOS CAN NAME A SLEEP TYPE ITS CHIPSET DOES NOT
HAVE.  86Box's ASUS P3B-F (440BX, PIIX4E) and ASUS CUV4X-LS (VIA
686B) both give \_S5_ = Package (4) {7, 7, 0, 0} - with \_S0_ {5,5},
\_S1_ {6,6} and \_S3_ switched off by a mangled name - although
PIIX4's soft-off is SLP_TYP 0 and 6 and 7 are reserved (the 82371EB
datasheet, and coreboot's PIIX4 table).  Two ASUS BIOSes on unrelated
chipsets using the same reserved values looks like firmware that traps
the SLP_EN write in SMM and does the switching itself.  86Box does not
emulate that, and its PIIX4 switches off on type 0 only, so on those
two boards no ACPI operating system can switch 86Box off and SHUTDOWN
says "did not switch off".  The kernel writes what the DSDT says, as
Windows and Linux do, and does NOT second-guess it per chipset.  (The
P3B-F's \_PTS, which is not run here, only stores the state in CMOS
through ports 72h/73h.)  Found with two TEST-ONLY PMIOs: one handing
back the 16 bytes around \_S5_ in the report registers, one copying
the whole DSDT (9,786 bytes) to B9000h for a DOS box to save.

VERIFIED:
  - 86Box ASUS P5A (ALi M1543C, \_S5_ {5,5}, which 86Box's ALi
    switches off on): 86Box closed itself 16 seconds into the run.  A
    file ECHO wrote just before was on the disk; a CMD /C whose
    redirected output ("HELLO") was still open when the power went
    left OUT.TXT at 7 bytes; C: clean.  NEGATIVE CONTROL, a TEST-ONLY

  - 86Box VS440FX at 512MB (Charlie's VM; PIIX3 has no ACPI): "ACPI

  - DOSBox-X without acpi=: "ACPI not found.", ERRORLEVEL 1; /? and

  - DOSBox-X with acpi=1.0: the tables are at FFFB0000h (pg_mapphys

VBE AND THE LINEAR FRAME BUFFER, FOR A NATIVE PROGRAM (2026-10-04)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for VBE 2.0's linear frame buffer for D32 programs.
Still v0.61.

A NATIVE PROGRAM COULD NOT HAVE A GRAPHICS SCREEN AT ALL.  It has no
BIOS and its segment is its slot (RING3.INC), so it could neither set
a mode nor reach video memory.  21h/F0h has done a text screen's work
for it since EDIT; nothing did a graphics screen's.  So there are two
new things: a call that asks the video BIOS for the program, and a
descriptor that reaches the frame buffer.

21h/F1h AL=1Fh, the function in bits 16-23 of EAX, native programs
only (DOS\VBE.INC; the list is with the VBF_* equates in PMDOS.INC):
  VBF_INFO 0     EDI -> 512 bytes: 4F00h's block, asked for as "VBE2".
                 Its far pointers name the ROM or XFER_BUF, neither of
                 them the program's, so the mode list is copied into
                 the block's reserved area (110 modes at most), the
                 four strings into its OEM area (64 bytes each), and
                 the pointers come back as the program's own.  EAX =
                 the version, ECX = the modes.  A 1.x block's vendor,
                 product and revision come back 0: they were reserved
                 bytes then, not pointers.
  VBF_MODE 1     CX = a mode, EDI -> 256 bytes: 4F01h's block.
  VBF_SET 2      EBX as 4F02h's BX.  A VBE mode must ask for the
                 linear frame buffer (bit 14); a VGA mode (below 100h)
                 must not, and is set with AH=00h.  -> EAX = SEL_VBE,
                 ECX = the bytes it covers, EDX = bytes per scan line
                 (VBE 3.0's linear one when there is one).
  VBF_RESTORE 3  what this program's end would do, now.
  VBF_PALETTE 4  4F09h: BL 00h/80h set, 01h read, ECX entries from
                 EDX, 4 bytes each at EDI.  The DAC's ports when the
                 BIOS has no 4F09h - a VBE 1.2 BIOS, or none at all in
                 mode 13h.
  VBF_BIOS 5     bits 24-31 of EAX = 03h, 06h, 07h or 08h, passed
                 through with EBX, ECX and EDX: the mode now, the
                 logical scan line, the display start (page flipping),
                 the DAC's width.  They take numbers and give numbers,
                 so there is nothing to copy and nothing kept to
                 spoil.
New errors after ERR_STAYEDON: ERR_NOVBE 74h, ERR_VBEFAIL 75h (the
BIOS said no).  Also ERR_BADDATA (a mode or palette range that cannot
be asked for), ERR_NOMEM (the frame buffer would not map), ERR_ACCESS
and ERR_FUNC.  r3_pflags gives EDI as a pointer to 0, 1 and 4 only.

THE FRAME BUFFER IS A SELECTOR: SEL_VBE, 004Bh, the GDT's tenth entry.
A pointer in the program's segment can only name its slot, and a
descriptor based on the frame buffer is the only way to give it that
and nothing else.  DPL 3 data, based where the buffer physically is -
mapped there by IOS_MAPPHYS, as DPMI 0800h maps, so linear is still
physical - and as long as all of video memory (4F00h's TotalMemory),
so one page can be drawn while 4F07h shows another; in pages past
1MB.  When a processor without 4MB pages runs out of device tables,
one screen.  A VGA graphics mode gets A0000h for 64K (the CGA modes
B8000h for 32K), a text mode no selector.  With no mode set it is
EMPTY, not absent - expand-down, limit 4GB: loadable, nothing in it -
because the kernel reloads the caller's ES on the way out of every
INT 21h and a program may still hold SEL_VBE there after its mode has
gone.  Absent, that would be a fault in the kernel.  IORM's GDT grew
from nine to ten, and gdtr, idtr_pm and rm_idtr moved out from behind
it to behind the RMT_IRQS entries, which it would otherwise have run
them into (the .ERRE there fired); an .ERRNZ now checks the GDT is
GDT_ENTRIES long.

A PROGRAM DRAWS THROUGH ES: REP MOVSD from a picture in its own slot
is the natural shape (VBETEST /S draws a scan line at a time that
way), or a far pointer.  ES and not FS or GS, because DS and ES are
what every DOS call gives back: FS and GS come back NULL from any call
that went through rm_int - rmc_back loads them with SEL_DATA32, and
the return to ring 3 drops a ring-0 selector.  That is true of every
native program and is not new; VBE.INC says it because a graphics
program is the one that will want FS for its screen.

WHAT A PROGRAM SETS, ITS END PUTS BACK.  4Ch calls vbe_exit for the
depth that is ending, after the mouse's ms_exit; r3_fault calls it
BEFORE it writes "*** Program fault", or the report would go into the
graphics screen and then be wiped by the mode 4Ch put back.  Kept by
EXEC depth (vbe_prev, vbe_dset): a depth's first VBF_SET remembers the
mode then current, and its end sets that again - a parent's VBE mode,
with SEL_VBE describing the parent's frame buffer again, or the text
mode the first VBF_SET found (the BIOS data area's mode, and the 8x8
or 8x14 font for 43/50 or 28 lines).  A parent's mode that will not
set again falls back to text.  The screen's contents are not kept.

THE VIDEO BIOS RUNS IN THE THUNK, with XFER_BUF as the block it
answers into (4F00h clears a kilobyte of it: some BIOSes write past
512), and with the vector table rm_freeze took after CONFIG.SYS - so
a VBE driver (UniVBE, Display Doctor, a card maker's VBE 2.0 TSR) has
to be loaded with INSTALL= to be seen by a native program.  From
AUTOEXEC.BAT it serves DOS boxes only.

ONLY THE LINEAR FRAME BUFFER.  A VBE mode without bit 14 is refused:
banked drawing would be a trip to real mode for every 64K.  Mode bits
9 and 10 are let through although VBE reserves them, because a
program sets what the BIOS lists and DOSBox-X lists 200h to 213h.
Bit 11 (a CRTC block) and bits 12-13 are refused.

TOOLS\VBETEST.ASM -> \TESTS\VBETEST.EXE (D32): BUILD, both MKHD lists
and RUNTESTS' default list; not the floppy.  Twelve checks - the info
block and its pointers, every mode's 4F01h, VBF_SET's selector (LSL,
LAR, VERW, 4F03h), all of video memory written and read back through
it, 4F07h, the palette there and back, ten refusals, a child's mode
13h and this one's back after it, mode 13h's window, VBF_RESTORE
(4F03h and an empty SEL_VBE), a child that ends in a mode, and one
that FAULTS in one (/F, through a null pointer: 255, and the first
mode back).  VBE 1.x passes check 1 and skips the linear ones: that
is the BIOS's age, not a failure.  A listed mode the BIOS will not
describe is counted and said, not failed - only a refusal that is not
ERR_VBEFAIL, or a list with nothing describable, fails check 2.
VBETEST /L lists the modes; VBETEST /S [mode] draws a gradient in a
white frame until a key - straight sides mean the pitch is right,
smooth colours mean the masks are, and an 8-bit mode gets a 3-3-2
palette to show the same picture, a scan line at a time through ES.

ITS OUTPUT WAITS IN A BUFFER while the screen may be graphics - unless
standard output is a file (4400h bit 7 clear), when each check's line
is written as it is decided and then 0Dh, so that a check that hangs
the machine leaves the lines before it on the disk.  0Dh and not 68h,
because fn68 does nothing for handles 0 to 2 ("the standard handles
are devices or files nobody else can flush") - so a program run as
"X > FILE" cannot commit its own output, only the cache.  After a hang
the file says 0 bytes and the lines are in a lost chain, which the
CHKDSK the next boot runs turns into FILE0000.CHK; the rig found them
by searching the raw image.  That rule about 68h is older than this
and was left alone.

Files: DOS\VBE.INC (new), DOS\DOSMAIN.ASM, DOS\INT21.INC (F1h AL=1Fh,
4Ch), DOS\RING3.INC (rpf_vbe, r3_fault), IO\IORM.ASM, INC\PMDOS.INC
(SEL_VBE, GDT_IDX_VBE, GDT_ENTRIES, VBF_*, VBM_*, VBE_*, VBI_*, VMI_*,
VMA_*, ERR_NOVBE, ERR_VBEFAIL), TOOLS\VBETEST.ASM (new), TOOLS\
RUNTESTS.PS1, BUILD.CMD, MKHD.CMD, DISK\CONFIG.TXT (INSTALL=: a VBE
driver goes there), BASELINE (RMFIND, RMTEST and VBETEST, seven rows).

S:\BIN (PMIO.SYS, PMDOS.SYS, TESTS\VBETEST.EXE), IMAGES\PMDOS.IMG (the
scratch BUILD's floppy, its kernel and CONFIG.TXT byte-checked),
IMAGES\HD16.IMG (FATREPL: those, CONFIG.TXT, and VBETEST.EXE in
\TESTS; a copy booted to the prompt, another ran VBETEST 12 of 12) and
the 86Box VM's two copies brought up to date.  Not HD32, HDBIG or the
two other floppies.

THE VM CANNOT SHOW IT AS IT IS: its GD5436 is VBE 1.2.  With
gfxcard = voodoo3_3k_pci it can - run86 on the VM's own machine
(VS440FX, Pentium Pro 166, 512MB) with that card: 12 of 12.

NOT VERIFIED: real hardware; a VBE driver under INSTALL=; a C program
drawing through a far pointer (no C binding exists - DOSINT.ASM
style, it would be one INT 21h); DPMI clients' own VBE (0300h and
0800h, untouched by this).  NOT DONE: banked modes (4F05h); 4F0Ah's
protected-mode interface; keeping the text screen's contents across a
graphics program; a mouse cursor drawn by the driver in a VBE mode
(its table knows the VGA modes only).

v0.62 - SCSI, LIM 4.0, VBE, ACPI, SAFE MODE, AND A DISK THAT KNOWS IT
        WAS NOT SHUT DOWN (2026-10-04)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for everything since 0.61 to be wrapped up, summed up
and committed, and for the number to say so.  INC\PMVER.INC now says
62.  The entries above, from "FDISK'S SCREEN AGAIN" on 2026-10-01
down to "VBE AND THE LINEAR FRAME BUFFER", are this release, and so
are the 2026-10-01 commits that have no entry of their own (RUNTESTS,
BUILD hang, the cache commit, EXECLEAK).  Most of those entries end
"Still v0.61"; that is left as written.  This entry is the list.

PROGRAMS AND MEMORY
  - A native program is not 512K any more.  Its slot is an arena
    block, 48h grows it, and a nested EXEC leaves the parent where it
    is.  Page tables cover all of RAM below 4GB; BIGMEM takes 3GB in
    one block on the 3GB machine.
  - Kernel memory is read-only to ring 3, and a pointer a program
    hands the kernel must be one the program could write itself
    (IOS_USRWOK).
  - A failed EXEC gives the kernel stack back.  Each one used to cost
    64 bytes, until the machine triple-faulted (the R3TEST "hang").
  - LIM 4.0 in the DOS boxes: 46h answers 40h, 4Fh to 5Dh are
    served, 64 handles, 32MB.
  - VBE 2.0's linear frame buffer for D32 programs: 21h/F1h AL=1Fh
    sets the mode and SEL_VBE reaches the screen.  The old mode comes
    back when the program ends or faults.

DISKS
  - DMF diskettes read and write; the BIOS's diskette table is
    lengthened for the call.  FORMAT /F:DMF and /F:1.68 make one.
    DISKCOPY and DISKCOMP take DMF, and a disk and its copy compare
    OK, as they do under 6.22.
  - RMDOS takes a 720K disk's geometry from its boot sector, and no
    file on a diskette wraps at 64K any more.
  - The clean-shutdown bit (Windows 95's, in FAT entry 1) is kept on
    FAT16 and FAT32.  A volume found dirty at boot gets CHKDSK /F
    before the shell.  AUTOCHECK=ON|ASK|OFF.
  - FDISK has DiskStat's layout: partitions drag with the mouse,
    changes wait for W, U undoes, F formats, the extended partition
    moves, and a resize can change the cluster size.
  - The cache is written back when a DOS program ends and before any
    program starts.

DEVICES
  - SCSI CD-ROMs: a native Adaptec 154x and BusLogic driver, the Pro
    Audio Spectrum's 53C80, and any card with an ASPI manager.
    SCSI=ON|OFF.
  - INT 08h and 1Ch run in a DOS box, and the clock stays right under
    a fast timer.  A resident driver's interrupt is served at the
    prompt.  The 8237 is virtualised: a transfer runs in place, is
    moved, or is bounced.  ISAPNP.EXE lists ISA Plug and Play cards
    and sets their resources.
  - A BIOS call runs with a copy of the vector table taken after
    CONFIG.SYS.  The 8259s are no longer set up again for every call.
    That used to lose a waiting interrupt each time, and the clock
    ran slow.

BOOT AND POWER
  - Safe mode: Shift or F5 at "Starting PM-DOS..." skips CONFIG.SYS
    and AUTOEXEC.BAT.  SWITCHES=/N turns the keys off, /F the wait.
  - SHUTDOWN.EXE writes back every file and cache, then switches the
    machine off through ACPI (21h/F1h AL=1Eh).
  - 21h/F1h AL=1Bh writes every cache and restarts the machine.

BUILD, TESTS AND FILES
  - Every .ASM file assembles with MASM 6.13 as well as wasm.
  - DISK\CONFIG.SYS holds settings only.  DISK\CONFIG.TXT explains
    every statement and goes on every image.
  - RUNTESTS.PS1 runs the tests unattended on seven DOSBox-X machines
    against BASELINE: 78 tests on each.  BUILD hang reports a hang or
    an exception on port E9h.
  - New tests: SLOTTEST, BIGMEM, EXECLEAK, TIMERTST, IRQXTEST,
    IRQXWAIT, DMATEST, RMIVT, EMS4TEST, VFTEST, VBETEST.
  - DISK\*.BAT and DISK\*.TXT are in git now, so a clone has
    everything BUILD.CMD and MKHD.CMD read.

PMIO.SYS is 56,507 bytes and PMDOS.SYS 146,002.

THE STAMP.  Three files read the equate.  PMDOS.SYS has it in two
places, CMD.EXE and COMMAND.COM in one each.  The rebuild changed
those four bytes and nothing else: every other file the build made
came out byte for byte as it was under 0.61.  On a copy of HD16
booted headless, VER, COMMAND /C VER and CMD /C VER all said "PM-DOS
version 0.62", with no mismatch line.  S:\BIN, IMAGES\PMDOS.IMG,
IMAGES\HD16.IMG and the 86Box VM's two copies carry it.  HD32,
HDBIG, PMDOSATA and PMDOSFDD were not rebuilt; each is an older
build whose kernel and shells match each other.  MULTI has no
system files.

NOT VERIFIED, from the entries above: none of the new hardware work
has run on a real machine (SCSI, ACPI power-off, DMF formatting,
VBE).  No real LIM 4.0 program has run.  Windows 98 has not met a disk
PM-DOS left dirty.  NOT DONE: F8 at boot, banked VBE modes.

DOS PROGRAMS OFF THE SHELF: A COMPATIBILITY SWEEP (2026-10-04)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for as many ordinary 16-bit DOS programs as it took to
find what PM-DOS gets wrong, downloaded from the Internet Archive and
WinWorld and deleted afterwards.  He was at the machine, so all of it
ran in DOSBox-X with no window (486, 32MB, a fresh 64MB HD16 per run,
the program grafted on with FATPUT), and every difference was checked
against the same lines run under DOSBox-X's own DOS before it was
called a bug.  Keys went in through the rig's KEYFEED; sound was
measured off the capture's audio track.

WHAT RAN.  Real mode: Commander Keen 1, Wolfenstein 3D, Prince of
Persia, Scorched Earth, Lemmings, SimCity, Monkey Island (EGA), Leisure
Suit Larry 1, Digger, Norton Commander 5, DOS Navigator 1.51, QEdit,
Turbo C 2.01 (TCC and the IDE), Turbo Pascal 7 (TPC), QuickBASIC 4.5
(the IDE, BC, LINK, and the program they made), ARJ 2.82 (add, test,
extract, list), the Word 5.5 and QuickBASIC self-extractors, and the
Heretic, Descent, Duke Nukem 3D and Warcraft installers.  Protected
mode: PKZIP/PKUNZIP 2.04g, DOOM 1.9, Heretic, Rise of the Triad,
Magic Carpet, Warcraft, Quake 1.06, Descent, Duke Nukem 3D.  With a
Sound Blaster 16: Wolfenstein, DOOM, Heretic, Quake, Duke.

FIXED, DPMI.  Most of what broke was the host.
  - 0306h, the raw mode switch, did not exist; PKZIP 2.04g uses
    nothing else.  Real mode now runs at the box loop's own level and
    protected mode is entered afresh from it, so nothing is parked and
    the real-mode half may even go resident (dpmi_rawrm, dpmi_rawpm).
  - The first switch kept the client's general registers, as the
    specification says it must; PKUNZIP read its arguments off BP.
  - 0202h/0203h, exception handlers, with a frame on a locked stack
    and the default handler reporting as before.  0301h/0302h.  000Ch
    had never worked.  0009h no longer forces Present and 0006h reads
    a descriptor that is not present (RTM loads segments on demand).
    0503h moves a block it cannot grow, which DJGPP's sbrk expects.
  - PSP:2Ch is the environment's selector while a client runs, and
    selector 0040h is the BIOS data area, both by convention.
  - A selector the client has freed is nulled on the way back rather
    than faulting the kernel: Quake frees its own DS.
  - INT 21h from a client: 25h and 35h are the protected-mode vectors
    (the kernel's 25h used to build a RING-0 gate to client code), 50h
    takes a selector, and 2Fh, 34h, 52h, 51h/62h, 1Bh/1Ch, 63h and
    5D06h answer in selectors.
  - The "MS-DOS" extension (INT 2Fh 168Ah, the LDT alias) is built
    and GATED OFF.  Borland's RTM finds it and then unloads itself
    with 50h to its own PSP and 4Ch, expecting DOS to resume at PSP:0Ah
    on the parent's PSP:2Eh stack.  PM-DOS keeps neither, so with the
    extension on, the wrong program ended.  Without it RTM says there
    are no DOS extensions and stops cleanly.

THE INTERRUPT FLAG A POPF PUTS BACK.  DOOM with a Sound Blaster
configured stopped at I_StartupTimer(), even with no card in the
machine.  DMX saves its flags, says CLI and later POPFs them.  At IOPL
0 the CLI faults and is emulated, but the POPF neither faults nor
changes IF, so the client's virtual flag stayed off and its next tick
was owed for ever.  The same goes for a handler that ends with a plain
IRETD.  The stack says when either has happened: once ESP is back
above where it was when the flag went off, the routine has returned or
the frame has been popped.  So that point is noted, for a handler's
frame and for a CLI already known to be one of these, and the next
look (every tick, and every chance to deliver an interrupt) turns the
flag back on.  A CLI not known yet is learned by the timer: off for
110ms with its routine already returned, it is believed on and the CLI
goes into a table of sixteen.  DMX needed four, once each.  A program
that keeps interrupts off on purpose and waits where it is, as
DPMIIRQ's check 4 does for a third of a second, is left alone up to a
second.  Single-stepping to the POPF was tried first and dropped: DMX
builds a volume table inside one of these sections.  DOOM, Heretic and
Quake now play with sound throughout (pm3_ifwatch, VM86.INC).

FIXED, THE DOS BOX.
  - PUSHFD, POPFD and IRETD were emulated sixteen bits wide, which
    unbalanced DOS/4GW's stack in its 486 test; it then went raw and
    died on LGDT.  The 66h prefix is honoured now, AC and ID are kept
    where the processor has them, and FLAGS bit 1 reads as set.
  - THE THUNK'S FRAME SAT IN DOS'S COMMUNICATION AREA.  RMFRAME was at
    500h, where BASIC keeps the INT 1Ch vector it hooks (0512h).
    QuickBASIC saved the timer vector there, every BIOS call the
    kernel made overwrote it, and QB put the result back on its way
    out.  The next timer tick then ran whatever program was loaded
    where that pointed, so BC crashed after QB had run.  The thunk's
    data is at 600h now, and nothing below 600h is the kernel's.
  - INT 21h 37h (the switch character) answers as MS-DOS 6 does.

FIXED, CMD.EXE.  "IF ERRORLEVEL == 1" was a syntax error.  COMMAND.COM
skips any of its delimiters after NOT, ERRORLEVEL and EXIST, so "==",
"=" and "," all read as a blank there; Heretic's INSTALL.BAT is
written that way.  CMD.EXE does the same now (if_kw).  PM-DOS's
COMMAND.COM was already right.

NOT FIXED.
  - Turbo Pascal 7's TPX, and anything else on Borland's RTM, until
    EXEC keeps PSP:0Ah and PSP:2Eh the way DOS does.
  - Duke Nukem 3D's sound says "not responding" here, but the control
    hung too with the configuration I wrote by hand, so nothing is
    proven either way.
  - Anything that reads keys through its own INT 09h could only be
    watched, not played: Descent was left at its pilot name.  Nothing
    was tried with a mouse.

TESTS.  RUNTESTS: CTRYDMP and PROBE13 differ by FLAGS bit 1 and RMTEST
by four clusters (the kernel grew), and all three were re-recorded on
all seven rows; then 78/78 on each.  DPMIIRQ and DPMII32 caught the
first version of the interrupt-flag change.  SYMCASE is clean, and
MASM 6.13 assembles IOPM, IORM, DOSMAIN, CMD, COMMAND and the boot
sectors; three "jmp short i21_return" had grown out of its reach.

PMIO.SYS is 57,267 bytes and PMDOS.SYS 149,686.  S:\BIN (PMIO.SYS,
PMDOS.SYS, CMD.EXE), IMAGES\PMDOS.IMG (the scratch BUILD's floppy),
IMAGES\HD16.IMG (FATREPL, then a copy booted headless: VER in both
shells, DPMIIRQ and DPMII32 pass) and the 86Box VM's two copies carry
it.  HD32 and HDBIG were not rebuilt.  Nothing here has run on real
hardware.  Still v0.62.


WINDOWS 3.1 IN 386 ENHANCED MODE (2026-10-05)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for PM-DOS to get on with Windows 3.1's 386 enhanced
mode.  Until now 1605h with DX bit 0 clear was vetoed (WINDOWS.INC),
with a message saying WIN386 wanted the ring-0 seat PM-DOS was in.
True, and beside the point: standard mode already got the machine by
PARKING - PM-DOS leaves protected mode, RMDOS.SYS serves DOS from
conventional memory, and the guest's INT 2Fh returns in real mode - and
an empty seat is exactly what a V86 monitor wants too.  So the veto is
gone, both modes park, and everything that follows is what WIN386 then
asks of the DOS underneath it, which is RMDOS.

WHAT RUNS.  On 86Box (p3bf, Pentium II 450, 64MB, GD5436), from
AUTOEXEC.BAT: WIN /3 starts, the desktop comes up, WINDRV.EXE (run=
in WIN.INI) WinExecs a batch file, which runs in a DOS virtual machine
through the 16-bit COMMAND.COM - VER, DIR, a program and its
errorlevel, COPY/TYPE/REN/DEL, a pipe, a nested COMMAND /C - to the
end, WINDRV asks Windows to exit, Windows exits, RMDOS hands back,
PM-DOS unparks and AUTOEXEC carries on - and the DOS boxes after it
work (HELLO, ARGS, TIMERTST, a COMMAND /C batch: run e35).  Windows' own clock runs
(GetTickCount advances with the BIOS count, and a 1000ms timer
delivers one WM_TIMER a second, to the queue and to a TimerProc).  WINDRV
now polls with PeekMessage and writes a sample line every so many
turns - the three clocks it can see - instead of waiting on the timer
it is measuring.

THE TRAPS, IN THE ORDER THEY CAME.  Each one stopped the startup dead
with a message that named something else; the real cause was found by
tracing RMDOS on port E9h under DOSBox-X (BUILD rme9) and by reading
WIN386.EXE's real-mode half with MS-DOS 6.22's DEBUG, and the fix was
then proved on 86Box.

  1. XMS PRESERVES WHAT IT DOES NOT RETURN.  WIN386's loader reads
     itself into extended memory with 0Bh (move) in a loop whose
     running count is in ECX - the upper half included - and RMDOS's
     XMS driver (RMXMS.INC) came back with ECX and the upper halves of
     EAX/EBX/EDX changed.  "Cannot load WIN386.EXE" at once.  rx_entry
     now saves and restores every register it is not defined to
     return: 88h keeps EAX/ECX/EDX whole, 8Eh keeps EDX, all else only
     AX/BX/DX.  The spec says so; HIMEM does so; nothing before Windows
     noticed.
  2. THE UNPARK TRIPLE-FAULTED on its first V86 entry.  rm_park kept
     GDT, IDT and CR3 for the way back (a BIOS call needs those too)
     and nothing else, because DOSX leaves the rest alone.  WIN386
     loads its own TSS, LDT, CR0 and CR4.  rmp_back (RMCALL.INC) now
     puts back CR0 whole, CR4's PSE bit (pg_cr4back, PAGING.INC), the
     task register - busy bit cleared in the descriptor first, or LTR
     refuses - and the LDT.
  3. "CANNOT USE A DEVICE SPECIFIED IN THE SYSTEM.INI FILE" meant
     DOSMGR's real-mode init returned error 2, which it does when the
     list of lists is not below 64K linear: it wants to patch and
     instance DOS's data through 16-bit offsets from zero.  RMDOS's
     published data (LoL, SDA, the Win386_DOSVars table, the CDS, the
     NUL/CON/AUX/PRN headers) now lives in PM-DOS's own DOS data
     segment at 0400:0000, which RMDOS saves on entry and puts back on
     the way home (rd_lowsave/rd_lowrest; RL_* in RMDOS.INC lays it
     out; PARK.INC checks the sizes at assembly time).
  4. "THE XMS DRIVER COULD NOT BE INSTALLED" / "cannot find an XMS
     driver": V86MMGR hooks the XMS entry by patching the HIMEM-shaped
     prologue - jmp short, three NOPs - and will not hook one above
     1MB.  RMDOS was in the HMA because WIN386's header asks for every
     paragraph (MAXALLOC FFFF) and left nothing low.  Two fixes: the
     entry has the prologue, and vl_winres (VDM.INC) reserves 64K
     under WIN386.EXE's own block at EXEC time - it knows the name -
     which park_loadrm then takes (park_resseg).
  5. "INSUFFICIENT MEMORY OR ADDRESS SPACE": V86MMGR splits
     conventional memory at WIN386's PSP into "DOS, global" below and
     "VM, local" above, and a DOS above the PSP is in the wrong half.
     Hence BELOW WIN386, which is what 4 does.
  6. THE SYSTEM FILE TABLE SCAN.  DOSMGR opens CON five times and
     looks for the five handles in the SFT to learn the entry size;
     RMDOS's entries are now DOS 4's 3Bh bytes with the fields where
     DOS keeps them (SFT_* in RMFILE.INC, sft_setdev).  The LoL's
     SFT pointer, CDS pointer (DOS-shaped, 58h a drive, RL_CDS) and
     device chain are all real.
  7. "KERNEL: UNABLE TO OPEN KERNEL EXECUTABLE".  KRNL386.EXE finds
     its own path after its environment's strings, and had no
     environment: RMDOS made it AFTER the program's block, and a
     MAXALLOC-0 program is given the largest block entire, so there was
     nowhere left.  fn4B (RMMEM.INC) now makes the environment first,
     as msproc.asm does, stamps it the parent's until the PSP exists
     and gives it back if the EXEC fails.  Standard mode never showed
     it because its memory happened to be in two pieces.
  8. TWO MACHINES INSIDE ONE DOS.  Once a DOS VM ran, the System VM
     and the DOS VM were both in INT 21h at once - 0Ah at a prompt is
     a call that waits - and RMDOS gave the second caller "the next
     stack", which was the one the first was standing on.  Stacks are
     SLOTS now (stk_take/stk_free, six of them, first free, given back
     by where SP is), and every call is a DOSMGR critical section
     (crit_in/crit_out: INT 2Ah 8001h/8101h, as MS-DOS 5 does, which
     RMDOS claims to be) released only round the console wait's INT
     28h.  INT 25h/26h take one too.  The SDA is synced into the
     published copy at the places DOSMGR may swap it.
  9. THE FIRST DOS BOX AFTER WINDOWS WAS DEAD.  HELLO ran, printed
     nothing and came back with errorlevel 0; so did everything 16-bit
     after it, while CMD.EXE's own commands were fine and MEM /D showed
     the arena untouched.  park_restvecs put the whole 20h-2Fh snapshot
     back - the table as it stood at 1605h, when WIN386's real-mode
     half still had its hooks in - after Windows had unhooked them and
     just before park_release freed the block they pointed into.  Only
     the vectors RMDOS took (the ones pointing into its image) go back
     from the snapshot now; the rest stay as Windows left them.
     Standard mode never showed it: DOSX hooks nothing there first.
 10. ODDS AND ENDS found on the way: fn30 AL=1 answers BX=0 (OEM, and
     the 'DOS in HMA' flag clear); fn34/fn52/fn5D point into the low
     block; 1607h/BX=15h callouts answered (RMINFO.INC i2F_devcall:
     CX=0 version, 1 SDA, 3 instance list, 4 and 5 patching, none);
     XMS 10h answers B1h not B0h when there are no UMBs; the NUL
     device's name was " NUL" from a dword constant.

WHAT DOSBOX-X CANNOT DO.  Enhanced mode does not run under DOSBox-X:
in the System VM a plain byte store into RMDOS's own data - the same
instruction, address and value that succeed on the previous call -
ends Windows, every time, at the same place.  86Box runs the same
image through without it.  So every enhanced-mode proof is an 86Box
run (rig: winrun.ps1 -On86 -> run86.ps1, 86Box minimized and never
touched, closed with WM_CLOSE, files read back out of the image), and
the port E9h trace is standard-mode only.  Standard mode still starts
and exits under both (s1, with nothing started from it).

A DOS SESSION FROM STANDARD MODE DOES NOT COME BACK ON DOSBOX-X, and
did not before this work either: with the 0.62 binaries in the same
rig (run c62) WINDRV starts WINDOS.BAT, WINOLDAP writes its swap file
(~WOA100F.TMP), sets the break flag, and the next thing the machine
does is run into an invalid opcode for ever, with no INT 21h in
between - the same picture with and without this work (s3, s4, c62).
Found while checking that standard mode was not broken; not chased.
RMDOS sits first fit above DOSX, which is inside what WSWAP swaps
out, and that is the first thing to look at.

NOT DONE.
  - A DOS session started from standard mode, on DOSBox-X: see above.
    Not tried on 86Box.
  - A park with a file open is allowed when the file is CMD.EXE's own
    redirection (WINTEST showed it: its output after the park went to
    RMDOS's console).  park_filesopen looks at the box's handles only.
  - RMDOS still starts every drive at the root; the current directory
    the box had is not carried across.  As before.
  - The HWPROBE output for the 486's PS/2 mouse is still awaited.

TESTS.  WINTEST used to send 1605h with DX bit 0 clear and expect the
veto; sent now, it parks the test run - the rest of its output went
to RMDOS's console - so it prints a line and leaves the question to
PARKWIN.COM.  RUNTESTS -All, seven rows: four answers moved and were
re-recorded, WINTEST (the new line), RMTEST (nine fewer free clusters:
RMDOS.SYS is 8K bigger on the test disk), CACHETST ("a write is owed"
0005 for 0004 on every row but the 386: the same layout shift) and
SFTSCAN, which scans conventional memory after PARKWIN has parked once
and finds RMDOS's own file table in the freed image - its entries are
3Bh apart now, and it has two more with names.  Then 78/78 on each
row.  wasm and MASM 6.13 both
assemble RMDOS.ASM (with and without RMDOS_E9), DOSMAIN, IOPM and
IORM.  The one-letter progress marks that found the DOSBox-X store are
gone again; the E9 trace keeps its instruments (INT 21h lines, XMS,
INT 15h, 2Fh, EXEC environments, disk requests, the MCB chain, the
invalid-opcode hook).

FILES.  DOS\WINDOWS.INC (1605h parks in either mode, veto and message
gone), VDM.INC (vl_winres), PARK.INC, RMDOS.ASM, RMINFO.INC,
RMFILE.INC, RMFILE2.INC, RMNAME.INC, RMCON.INC, RMMEM.INC, RMDISK.INC,
RMXMS.INC, RME9.INC, RMDBG.INC, INT21.INC, VOLFLAG.INC (comment),
IO\RMCALL.INC, IO\PAGING.INC, INC\RMDOS.INC (RMDOS_VER 0103h),
TOOLS\WINDRV.C, TOOLS\WINTEST.ASM, BASELINE\*\ (RMTEST, WINTEST, CACHETST
and SFTSCAN re-recorded), DISK\CONFIG.TXT (two sentences: Windows, not
"enhanced mode").

PMIO.SYS is 57,347 bytes, PMDOS.SYS 149,593 and RMDOS.SYS 36,705.
S:\BIN (PMIO.SYS, PMDOS.SYS, RMDOS.SYS, TESTS\WINDRV.EXE and WINTEST.COM),
IMAGES\PMDOS.IMG (the scratch BUILD's floppy), IMAGES\HD16.IMG (FATREPL,
CONFIG.TXT too) and the 86Box VM's two copies carry it.  HD32 and
HDBIG were not rebuilt.  Nothing here has run on real hardware.  Still
v0.62.


WINDOWS PROGRAMS OFF THE SHELF: THE ENHANCED-MODE SWEEP (2026-10-05)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for Windows 3.1 in 386 enhanced mode to be tested the
way the DOS boxes were: programs fetched from the Internet Archive and
WinWorld, run, and seen to work - most of them, not every edge.  He was
away from the keyboard, so 86Box could be used; it was never clicked
or typed at.

THE RIG.  TOOLS\WINSWEEP.C (WINSWEEP.EXE, Win16): named in WIN.INI's
run=, it reads C:\SWEEP.LST, one program a line (NAME|command|seconds|
keys), makes the program's directory current, WinExecs it, waits,
writes the screen to C:\SHOTS\NAME.BMP (a DIB at the display's own
depth), lists its windows, closes it (one WM_CLOSE to its main window,
a "save changes?" box answered by button id), and logs every step to
C:\SWEEP.TXT a line at a time.  NAME?file skips a line once the file
exists (an installer), NAME!file until it does.  A DOS box (a window of
class tty) is left to end by itself - WINOLDAP answers WM_CLOSE with a
system-modal box that stops everything.  The scratch script wsweep.ps1
builds a 128MB disk with the system, the Windows tree, the programs
(FATPUT, one root directory each), the list and the PIFs, runs it on
86Box through run86.ps1 (now with -Visible, -Shot, a PrintWindow of the
86Box window at the end, and -Geometry), and brings the pictures back
(fatx.pl, BMP -> PNG).  Under WIN /S on DOSBox-X the same script runs
with the port E9h trace (-Dbx -E9), which is how the two RMDOS bugs
below were found.

THE CONTROL.  C:\DOSBoxRoot\RIG\dos5.vhd, the real MS-DOS 5 disk, is a
dynamic VHD; vhd2raw.pl writes it out flat, FATPUT grafts the same
Windows tree onto it as \WIN with the same programs and driver, and
run86 -Geometry '63, 16, 1024' boots it.  Every failure was run there
before it was blamed on PM-DOS, and three of five were the program.

WHAT RAN (86Box, p3bf, PII-450, 64MB, the VGA driver at 640x480x16, no
sound card).  Windows' own: Write, File Manager, Control Panel,
Windows Help, Clipboard Viewer, PIF Editor, Registration Editor.  Two
windowed DOS boxes at once, each running a batch (VER, DIR, TIMERTST)
through PM-DOS's COMMAND.COM and closing by itself; a file handle held
open across both still read afterwards.  Games: SkiFree, Chip's
Challenge, JezzBall, Rodent's Revenge (VB1), Tetris 2.0, Taipei, Pipe
Dream, WinRisk, Minesweeper, Reversi, Memory Blocks, Neko, Castle of
the Winds, WinTrek, TDK Pinball, Glider 4.0, SimEarth, The Even More
Incredible Machine, Shanghai II, Brickbuster, Monopoly Deluxe.
Applications: Mortgage Designer, Micrografx Designer 3.1, ToolBook
1.5, FormTool Gold, Calmira 3.31, ASCII Chart, a VB2 calendar
(VBRUN200), FreeCell Plus (VB3), Windsock, WinSpeed, the PC Magazine
Windows benchmark.  MSD and a full-screen DOS box take the display, and
the in-guest pictures cannot show them - not tried further.

WHAT PM-DOS HAD WRONG, all in RMDOS, all found through the trace under
WIN /S and confirmed on 86Box:

  1. IOCTL 4408h/4409h/440Dh/440Eh were "invalid function".  Calmira
     asks all four for every drive letter while it starts and raised an
     "Error" form for each refusal - fifteen of them before the Delphi
     "An error has occurred in your application" box.  fn44 (RMFILE2.INC)
     now answers 08h (removable, from the volume table, no mount), 09h
     (remote: no, after checking the drive), 0Bh (retry count,
     accepted), 0Eh (one letter), and 0Dh/60h (device parameters from
     the volume's BPB).  The first version of 60h mounted the drive,
     which READ A: - an empty drive under Windows is a critical error
     nobody can answer, and Calmira stopped there instead.  A floppy
     drive now answers with a 1.44M default, unmounted, as DOS does.
  2. 2Ah GAVE THE DATE AS 2026-00-00.  fn2A made the year with "mul
     cx", which writes DX, and DX held the BIOS's month and day.  Every
     program under Windows on PM-DOS got month 0, day 0; a C runtime
     turning that into a day of the year gets -1 and searches its
     months table for ever - that was Monopoly Deluxe and Brickbuster,
     "WinExec never returns, no window".  Found with TOOLS\SPYTICK.C
     (an INT 8 hook in protected mode that writes the interrupted
     CS:IP to port E9h; the loop was in Monopoly's own code, decoded
     from POLY.EXE) and confirmed by TOOLS\TIMEPROB.C, which prints the
     DOS date and time and every clock a Windows program can see.
     Now imul, and 2Ah answers the day of the week too (rd_weekday).
  3. INT 2Fh 1000h, "is SHARE loaded?", was not answered.  Win32s
     Setup stops to say SHARE.EXE is not loaded (and goes on); Office's
     installers refuse.  RMDOS says yes now (i2F_share): 5Ch has always
     succeeded there, and there is one program and one DOS, so nothing
     to conflict with - what is NOT there is the refusal of a
     conflicting open, said plainly in the source.

THE CLOCKS ARE OTHERWISE RIGHT.  TIMEPROB on PM-DOS and on MS-DOS 5:
GetTickCount, GetCurrentTime, 40:6C, MMSYSTEM's timeGetTime, the 8254
(mode 2 as VTD shows it) and the RTC all move at the same rates; a
protected-mode INT 1Ch hook is called on neither (Windows does not
reflect a V86 INT 1Ch upward) and an INT 08h hook on both.  The one
difference: PM-DOS leaves IRQ 8, the RTC, unmasked at the slave PIC
(1Ch against 1Dh).  Nothing was seen to mind.

WHAT WAS NOT PM-DOS, by the control: Shanghai II's close wedged the
first driver on MS-DOS 5 too (two WM_CLOSEs at once, one inside the
other's "save?" box); SimEarth and The Incredible Machine want their
own directory current, as Program Manager would give them; Tetris
needs its mnemonic as a character; VB programs need VBRUN100/200/300
in SYSTEM; a windowed DOS box must be left to end by itself.  All of
that is the driver's, and it learned each one.  Brickbuster hung on
MS-DOS 5 as well in its one control run and runs here now with the
date fixed; whatever the control saw was not looked into.

OPEN.
  - Monopoly Deluxe runs (the board, its About box) but WinExec does
    not return to the driver on PM-DOS until it ends, as it does at
    once on MS-DOS 5.  Not understood; with or without its directory
    current.
  - MSD and full-screen DOS boxes: not observable from inside Windows,
    so not tried further.
  - The installers were not got through.  Win32s 1.30, Paint Shop Pro
    3.12, After Dark 2.0c, Video for Windows 1.1e and QuickTime 2.1.2
    all start, draw their dialogs and copy files (Win32s got through
    Disk 1 and into Disk 2; Paint Shop Pro filled C:\PSP and asked for
    a Program Manager group), but driving a setup from a list of keys
    sent at fixed times is a project of its own: Enter on a copy
    dialog is Cancel, Microsoft Setup's dialogs are not dialogs (class
    "Stuff-Shell"), and each product has its own flow.  Nothing in
    what they did do looked like PM-DOS's fault once SHARE was
    answered.  Word 2.0 and Excel 4.0 were fetched and unpacked (their
    disks merged into one directory each) but not started.
  - WINSWEEP's picture names are 8.3: NAME_10 and up fail.

TESTS.  RUNTESTS -All after the three RMDOS changes: RMTEST (one
cluster of free space), CACHETST (the owed count) and SFTSCAN (RMDOS's
addresses in freed memory) moved with RMDOS's size and layout, as they
