A DISK CACHE UNDER WINDOWS: RMDOS GETS SMARTDRV'S JOB (2026-10-06)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for disk caching in RMDOS to help Windows along - a new
cache started when Windows starts was fine by him - and that it look
like SMARTDRV to the programs that ask: shrinkable for Windows, and
switchable off for Windows for Workgroups 3.11's 32-bit file access.

WHAT THERE WAS.  The kernel's cache (CACHE.INC) gives its chunks back
at the park (cache_park), because the pool RMDOS hands Windows is the
arena's free memory and a cache still holding chunks is memory Windows
never sees.  So from 1605h to the unpark every sector Windows wanted
of its DOS went to the BIOS - one INT 13h per sector (rd_xfer said so
and meant it), and under WIN386 every INT 13h is a trip through the
monitor.  RMFILE2's file_io moved one sector at a time through
rd_datbuf as well, so KRNL386 loading a 40K segment was eighty BIOS
calls and eighty copies.

WHAT SMARTDRV IS, read rather than remembered.  S:\DOS6SRC has
dev\smartdrv - SMARTDRV 4.10, "BAMBI" - and its int2f.asm is the whole
INT 2Fh AX=4A10h interface: BX=0 (AX=BABEh, DX:BX hits, DI:SI misses,
CX dirty, BP the version), 1 commit, 2 reset, 3 a drive's read/write
caching on or off (BP = the letter, DL = the verb, DL back = the
state: 80h no reads, 40h no writes, FFh not a drive it caches), 4 the
sizes.  THE SHRINK FOR WINDOWS IS SMARTDRV'S OWN DOING: on INT 2Fh
1605h it re-sizes itself to its second number, on 1606h back to the
first.  Windows asks for nothing.  WIN386.EXE's two 4A10h bytes are
"mov dx,[bx+10h] / dec dx"; Windows 3.1 only opens the SMARTAAR device
of the 3.x SMARTDRV.SYS (the open is in every trace), finds none, and
goes on.  And the WfW 3.11 side is in IFSMGR.386, not VFAT: at start,
for each drive it takes, BX=0 (is it there?), BX=1 (commit), BX=3 DL=0
(the state, kept), then BX=3 DL=4 and DL=2 (writes off, reads off);
at the end BX=3 DL=1 and DL=3 put back what it found.  Decoded from
the expanded VxD (the WfW disks are KWAJ-compressed; EXPAND.EXE under
headless DOSBox-X did them): 66 C7 45 1C 10 4A is Client_AX = 4A10h,
45 10 is BX, 45 14 is DX, 89 4D 08 is BP, then mov eax,2Fh / VMMcall
Exec_Int.

WHAT WAS BUILT: DOS\RMCACHE.INC.
  - A sector cache under rd_xfer, keyed by BIOS drive and absolute
    LBA like the kernel's, in elements of eight sectors with a bit per
    sector held.  Up to 1024 elements (4MB) from RMH_WINCACHE, which
    PARK.INC fills from WINCACHE= in CONFIG.SYS or an eighth of the
    pool.  The memory is an XMS block from RMDOS's own driver, taken
    in rd_entry BEFORE the IRET into Windows' loader, so that "how
    much is free" is already answered without it; locked, so its
    physical address is known.  Directory, chain heads and the 4K
    read-ahead buffer are in the image: the segment is 64K, the image
    was 37K, and it is 56K now (58K with the E9 trace) - inside
    PARK's 60K.
  - Read-through with read-ahead: a miss on less than an element reads
    the whole element into the buffer and keeps it (clipped at the
    volume's end; not while mounting, when the end is unknown).  A
    whole aligned element or more goes straight to the caller and is
    kept from there.  Write-through, always, write-allocate: the disk
    first, then the cache; nothing is ever owed and nothing can be
    lost by the cache being wrong, turned off or forgotten.  Floppies
    are never cached (no change line; rd_getvol re-mounts them).
    Replacement is a clock bit.
  - THE MOVER.  In real mode (standard mode, and WIN386's real-mode
    loader) rx_domove, RMXMS's own.  Under WIN386 the DOS is in V86
    mode and CR0 is not ours, so INT 15h AH=87h (rx_move15), which the
    monitor emulates - and the first V86 transfer proves it on a
    spare element (cm_selftest, a 512-byte pattern out and back)
    before any data depends on it; a mover that fails turns the cache
    off.  NOT the XMS entry under Windows: V86MMGR owns it, and what it
    does with a handle older than Windows is not a thing to lean on.
  - 4A10h answered as SMARTDRV 4.10 (cm_api): BX=0/1/2/3/4 as above;
    BX=3's off drops what is held for the drive and VF_NOREAD /
    VF_NOWRITE in the volume record keep it off; everything else is an
    IRET with nothing changed, which is what SMARTDRV chaining into
    nothing comes to.  No cache configured = no SMARTDRV (AX comes back
    as it went).
  - 1606h: with WINCACHE=...,LOG, RMCACHE.LOG on the boot drive - the
    counts and every 4A10h made (BX, DX, BP), written through RMDOS's
    own INT 21h from inside the broadcast.
  - rd_raw (RMDISK.INC), the BIOS transfer, now moves runs: cut at the
    track end on the CHS path, at a 64K boundary in memory, and at 127
    sectors.  file_io (RMFILE2.INC) moves whole sectors straight to
    and from the caller's buffer, as many as the cluster has left; the
    partial sector at either end still goes through rd_datbuf.
  - TOOLS: SDSTAT.COM (what 4A10h answers: version, hits, misses,
    sizes, a letter per drive with r/w) and TICKS.COM (40:6C as a
    number, for timing a batch from the outside).  WINSWEEP stamps
    every log line with GetTickCount now.

TWO BUGS OF THE FIRST BUILD, both found in one E9 trace under WIN /S:
  - cm_mask answered in AL, and AL is the low byte of EAX, which is
    the LBA in every caller.  An element found but not wholly held
    re-read sector 0xFE instead of 0x248: zeros, which a directory
    scan reads as its end - "Cannot find files needed to run Windows
    in standard mode" - and which the create of RMCACHE.LOG then
    WROTE BACK over the root directory's first sector.  The mask is in
    DL now.
  - rd_raw renormalised ES:BX and left ES changed for its caller, which
    the old one-sector loop also did, and which nothing minded until
    file_io's new run path used ES:DI again on the next pass.  Every
    register kept, ES included.
  The hit test was also inverted (any OTHER sector held read as a
  miss), so the first build never hit at all.

THE MOVER UNDER WIN386, which took three runs to settle.  The first
cache-on run (e3) ran every program and exited cleanly - the INT 15h
self-test passed - but its DOS-box batch, two COPYs of WIN386.EXE and
two DIR /S, took 81 s against 48 s with no cache at all.  So a second
mover was tried: the XMS entry, which under WIN386 is V86MMGR's
breakpoint and could do the copy in ring 0.  Its round trip PASSED
and Windows never left its logo (e4): V86MMGR took RMDOS's handle for
one of its own, moved the pattern into somebody else's memory and
read it back from there, which a round trip cannot tell from the
truth.  A handle issued before Windows is only V86MMGR's to serve
when it can read the driver's table - INT 2Fh 4309h, HIMEM's
HandleInfo, which RMXMS does not publish and whose semantics (V86MMGR
writes into it) were not going to be guessed at 1 AM.  cm_xmove stays
in the file for the day that is done; cm_selftest takes 87h only.
TOOLS\MOVEPROB.C is the instrument this left behind: 1000 XMS 0Bh
moves and 1000 INT 15h 87h moves of 2K from a DOS box, timed off
40:6C, with the 87h pair between two conventional buffers when the
monitor refuses the lock (V86MMGR does: error ADh).

AND ONE OF RMDOS'S, found by the timing batch: 02h, 06h and 09h wrote
straight to con_out, so "SDSTAT >> CACHEBOX.TXT" in a DOS box printed
on the box's screen and left the file with only COPY's lines in it -
COMMAND.COM's own ECHO and COPY go through 40h and were fine, which is
why nothing had noticed.  DOS sends all three through handle 1, and
so does RMCON.INC now (con_write): the file when redirected, the
console through dev_write otherwise, and a program with no handle 1
still gets the console.

WINDOWS FOR WORKGROUPS 3.11, which is where "disabled entirely"
comes from.  The eight disks (archive.org's MS_Windows-3, the retail
3.11) merged into one \WFW and SETUP /H:PMDOS.SHH - the automated
setup, network=nonet, Charlie's PMDOS.SHH for Windows 3.1 with a
[network] section - from AUTOEXEC on PM-DOS.  The first run stopped
on Setup's first screen: "The XMS driver you have on your system is
not compatible with Windows."  Its DOS half asks XMS 00h and wants
the driver revision in BX to be 0260h or more (SETUP.EXE 122AAh:
cmp ax,0200h / cmp dx,0260h), which HIMEM 2.60 - Windows 3.0's - was,
and the kernel's host said 0029h, PM-DOS 0.29.  Both hosts say 030Ah
now, HIMEM 3.10's number; the field means nothing else to anyone.
The second run got to Setup's next screen and stopped there: "The
programs below have been detected on your computer ... SUBST.EXE
(Unknown), JOIN.EXE (Unknown) ... press C to continue", which an
automated setup cannot.  Neither is loaded; Setup's DOS half reads
the current directory structures through the list of lists, the
kernel says FFFF:FFFF there because it has none, and whatever Setup
read at FFFF:FFFF had the SUBST and JOIN bits set.  OPEN: a CDS array
for the kernel's guests, in DOSDATA, like the one RMDOS builds for
Windows (RL_CDS).  So the install was done on real MS-DOS 5 instead
(the control disk, SETUP /H from AUTOEXEC, an upgrade over the DOS
VM's own Windows 3.1 - 273 files, 01:17 on 2026-10-06) and the
resulting C:\WINDOWS grafted onto PM-DOS's disk by the sweep rig
(-WinSrc), which is the WfW that then ran on PM-DOS.

AND THEN VSHARE.  The first WfW runs on PM-DOS stopped at "Cannot
load a device file that is specified in SYSTEM.INI:
C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM\vshare.386 - Press a key to continue".  On a real
DOS with SHARE.EXE loaded VSHARE does the same, so the first guess was
RMDOS's "SHARE is loaded" (i2F_share, from the Win32s finding of the
day before): the answer was made "no" under enhanced mode until 1608h
and "yes" after, which would have suited VSHARE and Win32s both.  It
changed nothing, and the expanded VSHARE.386 has no 1000h in it
anywhere - it never asks.  What it wants is DOS's own SHARE hook
table, which SHARE.EXE fills in DOS's data segment and which RMDOS
has not got; the gating was taken out again rather than left in on a
theory.  SETTLED that evening - see the entry below.  For the runs
below VSHARE was commented out of the grafted SYSTEM.INI.

WHERE WFW 3.11 STANDS ON RMDOS: ON ITS LOGO.  With VSHARE out it
loads its devices and puts the logo up, and stays there for the whole
run - with the cache (wfw_e), with the cache and device=vfat.386
(wfw_f), and with WINCACHE=OFF (wfw_g) alike, so whatever stops it is
not the cache's and was there before this work: RMDOS had never been
asked to run Windows for Workgroups until tonight.  No RMCACHE.LOG,
because 1606h never came, and so no record yet of IFSMGR's 4A10h
calls on this DOS - the IFSMGR half of "disabled entirely" is
answered by reading IFSMGR.386 rather than by seeing it done.  OPEN,
and the first thing to put the E9 trace on is not possible either:
enhanced mode does not run under DOSBox-X.  The WfW tree, installed
and ready to graft, is kept at S:\WFW311HD\WINDOWS beside the
Windows 3.1 one at S:\WIN31HD, with the PMDOS.SHH that made it; its
SYSTEM.INI has the VSHARE line commented out.  BOTH SETTLED THE SAME
EVENING, AND THE LINE IS BACK IN: see the entry below.

WHAT IT DOES FOR WINDOWS 3.1, measured on 86Box (p3bf, PII-450, 64MB,
the 1994 4500rpm disk model) with the sweep rig of 2026-10-05, the

So every program comes up a quarter to one second sooner and Windows

WINDOWS FOR WORKGROUPS 3.11 RUNS ON RMDOS (2026-10-06, evening)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked whether the WfW 3.11 items the cache entry above left
open could be fixed at all.  Two of the three could, and were, the
same evening: WfW 3.11 now comes up on RMDOS exactly as it installs
itself, VPD and VSHARE and all.  What stopped it, and how it was found
without a debugger that runs 386 enhanced mode, is below.

A TRACE FOR 386 ENHANCED MODE AT LAST.  The E9 trace (RME9.INC) needs
DOSBox-X, which cannot run enhanced mode, and the disk trace
(RMDBG.INC) stops what it watches.  Every character of the E9 trace
now goes through one routine, e9_putc, and two build targets give it
a second way out that 86Box can keep:

  rme9com   COM1, 115200 8N1, set up on the first character.  86Box
            4.2.1's serial passthrough (serial1_passthrough_enabled = 1
            and a [Serial Passthrough Device #1] section with mode = 0)
            serves the port as a named pipe, \\.\pipe\86Box\<name>,
            and a reader copies the pipe to a file until 86Box closes.
            THIS IS THE ONE THAT WORKS.  Windows takes the UART for
            itself as it initialises - VCD in 3.1, serial.386 and
            vcomm.386 as well in WfW - and the trace turns to noise from
            there, so a traced run comments out device=*vcd, *combuff,
            serial.386 and vcomm.386; nothing else changes.
  rme9lpt   LPT1, for 86Box's Generic Text Printer.  On the p3bf it
            records only the control bytes whatever order the data and
            STROBE are written in - the BIOS's own INT 17h too - so it
            is kept for another machine and not used.

The rig (in the session scratchpad: wsweep\tracerun.ps1 and
rig\pipe_reader.ps1, with wsweep.ps1's new -More, -Before and the
others) takes a Windows tree, comments out or overrides SYSTEM.INI
lines, runs it traced and prints what followed the 1608h broadcast.

AN ANSWER OF MS-DOS'S THAT RMDOS HAD WRONG.  WIN386 asks INT 21h
AH=DCh - NetWare's "connection number" - as it starts.  RMDOS failed
any function past its table with ERR_FUNC and the carry; MS-DOS
answers AL=0 and leaves the carry clear (DOS6SRC dos/msdisp.asm,
BadCall: setting it "may break some programs").  WfW read the 1 in AL
as a connection and took a different path through its file checks.
RMDOS now answers as DOS does (RMDOS.ASM, i21_bad).  Functions inside
the table that RMDOS does not serve still fail with ERR_FUNC.

WHERE IT STOPPED.  The trace runs up to the 1608h "Windows init
complete" broadcast and then stops for good: no INT 21h, no 2Fh, no
XMS call, nothing.  Windows 3.1 on the same rig follows 1608h at once
with VKD's keyboard flush (21h 0C06h) and the EXEC of KRNL386.  So the
stop was inside WIN386, with no DOS call to see.  SYSTEM.INI alone
narrowed it no further: every WfW-only VxD out, the network out,
WINCACHE=OFF, /D:X and /D:FSV all stopped the same way.  Then, by
moving whole pieces between the two Windows (dis\w3get.pl writes any
VxD out of WIN386.EXE's W3 bundle as a stand-alone .386, so that
device=*name can become device=C:\VX31\NAME.386):

  - WfW's own KRNL386, USER, GDI and shell on Windows 3.1's WIN386.EXE
    started and were loading Program Manager when the run's time ran
    out (wfw_n3).
  - WfW's WIN386.EXE with all twenty-five of its bundled VxDs swapped
    for 3.1's came up (wfw_a1) - and so did each half (a2, a3).  The
    one line every working run had lost and every stuck run had kept
    was device=*vpd: WfW's virtual printer device, which Windows 3.1
    has no copy of.
  - WfW as installed with only *vpd out came up (a4), and so did WfW
    with *vpd in and 86Box's LPT1 switched off (a5).

THE PRINTER PORT, A RED HERRING THAT FIXED SOMETHING ANYWAY.  A probe
of the state each DOS leaves (a scratch PICPROBE.COM on real MS-DOS 5,
and a new line of the E9 trace at RMDOS's birth, e9_ports, with all of
0:0-0:4FF) found one real difference: 378h's control
register.  POST leaves it with only the interrupt enable set - INIT low,
the printer held in reset - and IO.SYS's printer driver initialises
every port as it loads, leaving 0Ch.  PM-DOS never touched the ports.
The kernel now does what IO.SYS does, INT 17h AH=01h on each port the
BIOS listed, once at boot (prn_init in INT21.INC, called from
DOSMAIN.ASM after sft_init).  It changed the register to IO.SYS's
value and did not change WfW: it still stopped.  Kept, because it is
what every DOS program has been able to assume since 1981.

WHAT VPD REALLY DOES.  Its start-up (0x1B8 bytes, read with wdis
through a COFF wrapper and the VMM service names) reads SGRABLPT and
LPTxAUTOASSIGN, traps each printer port the BIOS lists, hooks INT 17h,
and asks DOSMGR to instance four DOS devices by name: LPT1, LPT2, LPT3
and PRN.  DOSMGR finds PRN in RMDOS's chain and asks DOS how big its
driver is - INT 2Fh 1607h CX=5 with ES:DI on the header (the trace now
prints ES:DI on 1607h lines: 0400:0340 is CON, which DOSMGR instances
for itself, 0400:0364 is PRN, which only VPD asks for).  MS-DOS sizes
a driver from the 'D' arena in front of it and answers 0 - "use your
own methods" - when there is none.  RMDOS answered 0 for everything.
Its four headers live in the borrowed DOS data block with no arena,
and DOSMGR's own method got PRN wrong; Windows then never returned
from the 1608h broadcast.  RMDOS now answers its own NUL, CON, AUX and
PRN with the exact size, the 18-byte header that is the whole driver
(RMINFO.INC, i2F_dm5), and WfW with *vpd active comes up.  The LPTn
names are not in RMDOS's chain; VPD's requests for them fail quietly.
Printing through VPD is untested - there is no printer in the rig.

VSHARE, AND THE DOS 5 LAYOUT.  VSHARE.386's real-mode start-up does
INT 21h 52h and reads the byte at offset 4 of the segment it gets:
DOS 5's DataVersion, 1 in DOS 5 and 6, which the DOS 6 source says SHARE
and the redirector check for compatibility (dos/msconst.asm).  Above 1
it refuses to load.  RMDOS's list of lists began at 0, so offset 4 was the
DPB pointer, FFh.  Its protected-mode start-up then works from a table
of DOS 5 offsets in that segment: the list of lists at 26h (the file
table chain, and the FCB table at +1Ah, which it reallocates if it
has the default four entries), SHARE's jump table at 90h (fifteen far
pointers, which it saves and fills with callbacks into itself, and
restores at exit), the SHARE flag at 303h (set to FFh), and SDA fields
from 320h up.  MS-DOS 5's own MSDOS.SYS agrees with the DOS 6 source
wherever it was checked (its data segment image starts at file offset
7EB0h: 90h holds the fifteen BadCall/OKCall pointers, 303h the SHARE
flag between CharCo, the switch character and MYNAME, 320h the SDA).

So RMDOS's block is laid out as DOS 5's now (RMDOS.INC): DataVersion 1
at 4, the MCB head at 24h and the list of lists at 26h, the DOSMGR
table and its variables at 60h-7Ah as before, an empty FCB table at
80h that the list's FCB pointer names, the jump table at 90h full of
far pointers to a RETF, the SHARE flag at 303h, the SDA at 320h (which
puts InDOS at 321h, where DOS 5 has it), the CDS array moved to 600h
and the CON/AUX/PRN headers after it.  RMDOS calls none of the jump
table and reads neither flag, and VSHARE's records of who has what
open are made only when DOS calls SHARE through that table - so,
loaded, VSHARE answers 2Fh/1000h itself and otherwise does nothing.
Which is what SHARE amounts to with one DOS and one machine under it.
VSHARE loads, and WfW with both lines active comes up (wfw_q1).

THE REGRESSION AND THE SWEEPS.  The regression is 78 of 78 on all seven
rows, twice, after SFTSCAN's baselines were re-recorded: its last two
lines are where "CON " turns up inside a loaded program's code, and
they move whenever RMDOS.SYS changes size.  MASM 6.13 assembles
RMDOS.ASM as released and in both trace builds.  On 86Box with the
release build, WfW 3.11 exactly as Setup left it - VPD, VSHARE and
the serial VxDs all in - ran the ten Windows programs of the cache
list and the CACHEBOX DOS box, with VSHARE loaded across that box's
start and end; the cache answered the box 18,570 hits to 1,204
misses.  Windows 3.1 ran the same list as well as it did this
morning.

AND ONE THING THAT IS NOT NEW BUT IS NOT RIGHT EITHER.  In all four
full-list runs this evening the second DOS box, DOSBOX1, stalled:
TIMERTST stops at "clock ticks in 2 RTC s" (it reads ports 70h/71h
until the RTC's seconds change) or the box closes and WINSWEEP never
logs another line, and Windows does not exit.  This morning's
delivered build does exactly the same today (full_old2), so it is
not tonight's; this morning's three runs of the same list, at 2-3 AM
with the host idle, never did it, and 86Box ran at 36-60% of real
speed tonight with the machine in use.  DOSBOX1 alone and CACHEBOX
then DOSBOX1 pass on both builds.  OPEN, and timing-dependent.


STILL OPEN:
  - IFSMGR.386 never loads on RMDOS.  Its real-mode start-up opens the
    "IFS$HLP$" device - IFSHLP.SYS, which WfW's Setup puts in
    CONFIG.SYS - and declines silently when the open fails.  RMDOS's
    device chain is NUL, CON, AUX and PRN, so WfW runs on RMDOS without

  - WfW's Setup still cannot run on the kernel (the FFFF:FFFF CDS of
    the kernel's own list of lists, above); the install at
    S:\WFW311HD was made on real MS-DOS 5.
  - Nothing here has run on real hardware.

S:\WFW311HD\WINDOWS\SYSTEM.INI has device=*vpd and device=vshare.386
back in, as Setup wrote them.  Files: DOS\RMDOS.ASM (i21_bad),
DOS\RMINFO.INC (i2F_dm5, rd_sysinit, the 1000h note), INC\RMDOS.INC
(the layout), DOS\INT21.INC (prn_init), DOS\DOSMAIN.ASM, DOS\RME9.INC

CONFIG.SYS DRIVERS UNDER WINDOWS, A REAL CDS, AND WFW'S SETUP ON THE KERNEL (2026-10-06/07)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for three things in order: the 16-bit drivers CONFIG.SYS
loads to work under Windows as well as on the kernel, so that
IFSHLP.SYS can load (and the rest); the kernel to have a current
directory array; and the DOS-box stall the WfW entry above left open.

ONE DOS DATA SEGMENT, MS-DOS 5'S SHAPE, ON BOTH SIDES.  A driver asks
34h and 52h once, at its INIT, on the kernel, and keeps the answers:
IFSHLP.SYS keeps InDOS, the SDA and the list of lists for as long as
it is resident, which under Windows means for as long as RMDOS is the
DOS.  So those addresses have to mean the same thing on both sides of
the handover, and they do now.  Segment 0400h is laid out as MS-DOS 5
lays its own out (DOS6SRC dos/msconst.asm), by both PMDOS.INC (DOSDATA)
and RMDOS.INC (RL_*), and PARK.INC checks every offset against the
other at assembly time:

    4       DataVersion, 1          D4h      the FCB table
    24h     MCB head, then LoL      DAh-10Fh CON, AUX, PRN headers
    48h     NUL, inside the list    110h     DOSMGR's DOS variables
    5Ah-6Ch the list's tail         130h     the country tables
    8Ch     UMB_HEAD                303h     SHARE's flag
    90h     SHARE's jump table      320h     the SDA (InDOS at 321h)
    D0h     a RETF                  340h     file table block 1 (11)
    600h    the CDS array           B80h     file table block 2 (53)

The segment is 17C0h bytes now, so a DOS box's arena starts at 57C0h
and conventional memory reads 618K, one less than before.  34h, 5D06h,
1Bh/1Ch and 63h answer 0400:offset, as DOS does - not flat addresses -
and RMDOS saves and puts back 0-BFFh around an excursion.

THE DEVICE CHAIN IS THE SAME CHAIN.  NUL, then every driver CONFIG.SYS
loaded, then CON, AUX and PRN, on the kernel and under RMDOS: RMDOS
takes the kernel's chain as it finds it (rd_chain) and unlinks only
the kernel's own devices whose entry points are HLTs into a kernel
that is not there (MSCD001), linking them back on the way home.  A
driver that hooked INT 21h or 2Fh at its INIT is still in front of
RMDOS, which goes in under it through the DOS vector stub (rd_vecs).

AND A HANDLE ON A DRIVER WORKS ON BOTH SIDES.  The kernel (DEVLOAD.INC,
INT21.INC) and RMDOS (the new DOS\RMDEV.INC) now do for a loaded
character driver what DOS6SRC's disk.asm does: open and close requests
for an OCRM driver, 4400h/4401h device information (EOF bit cleared by
a ^Z and set again by any write, even an empty one), 4402h/4403h IOCTL
read and write (the kernel bounces a buffer above 1MB), 4406h/4407h
status, 440Ch generic IOCTL, cooked reads that stop at CR or ^Z and
keep them, cooked writes that stop before a ^Z, raw mode as one
request, and a driver's error e as DOS error 13h+e.  A driver named
CON takes the console (ANSI.SYS) and a block driver's units are drives
under RMDOS too, uncached.  1607h CX=5 sizes a loaded driver from its
memory block, as DOSMGR asks.  IFSHLP.SYS itself was asked, from a DOS
program on both sides, exactly what IFSMGR asks it - the 8-byte
handshake, function 0's pointer and its version byte, function 8's
flags - and answers the same on RMDOS as on the kernel.

THE KERNEL HAS A CDS ARRAY.  The list of lists said FFFF:FFFF at 16h,
and WfW's Setup read its current directories out of whatever that
named, found SUBST and JOIN in force, and stopped to ask.  Now 600h
holds sixteen 58h-byte entries in MS-DOS 4's format - "C:\DIR" at 0,
4000h (physical) in the flags at 43h for a drive that exists, the
directory's cluster, 2 at 4Fh - refreshed from each volume's own
current directory (vdm_cdsfresh) whenever the list is, and RMDOS
starts each of its eight drives in the directory the kernel had.

FOUND ON THE WAY: EVERY EXCURSION SENT EVERY DRIVE TO ITS ROOT.  The
unpark remounts each volume, and a mount starts at the root, so a
program that parked from C:\WORK came back in C:\.  park_remount now
keeps each drive's directory across its mount and walks back into it
(cwd_here, shared with 3Bh).  FCBTEST's wildcard delete in the wrong
directory found it, by deleting its own output file.

THE TESTS.  IOCDEV.SYS is a character driver spoken to the way IFSMGR
speaks to IFSHLP; DRVTEST asks it fifteen things on the kernel and the
same fifteen on RMDOS after a park.  BLKTEST writes a file on
TESTBLK.SYS's RAM disk on the kernel, reads it and writes another on
RMDOS, and reads that back on the kernel.  CDSTEST reads the array
through the list of lists on both sides and checks the directory
survives the trip.  RUNTESTS's CONFIG.SYS loads IOCDEV.SYS and
TESTBLK.SYS from now on, which is why LOLTEST's chain rule is now "at
least four headers, and the last is PRN", and why MEM, HELLO and every
test that prints a segment moved: the RAM disk's 32K is below them.

IFSHLP.SYS VISIBLE - AND WINDOWS FOR WORKGROUPS HUNG BEFORE ITS LOGO.
With IFS$HLP$ in the chain, WfW stopped at the same place whether or
not IFSMGR and VCACHE were in SYSTEM.INI: DOSMGR's 5803h, and no DOS
call after it.  IFSHLP itself was innocent - with its hooks disabled,
its device attribute changed, both, it still hung, and so did a
do-nothing driver of the same size.  It was WHERE THE PARK LANDED, and
86Box bisected it to the paragraph: a 2,784-byte dummy driver let WfW
start and a 2,816-byte one did not (RMDOS at 0754h against 0756h).
Dropping vshare.386 from SYSTEM.INI let the bigger one start; a VSHARE
whose Device_Init returned at once started too, and one that returned
after its file-table walk did not.

VSHARE COUNTS A FILE TABLE THE WAY ONLY A TWO-BLOCK TABLE SURVIVES.  It
adds up a block, follows its next pointer, and stops when the first
word of the block it arrived at is FFFFh.  MS-DOS always has two
blocks, so it never gets past the second; RMDOS had one, whose next
pointer is FFFF:FFFF, and with A20 off in the virtual machine that is
0FFEFh - inside the 64K RMDOS parks in, in the sector cache's
directory.  An unused directory entry is all FFh, so VSHARE stopped if
the entry under 0FFEFh was still unused and walked memory for ever if
WIN386's own reads had filled it, which is where the size of a driver
in CONFIG.SYS came in; with WINCACHE=OFF the directory is zeros and it
would always have hung.  RMDOS's block now links to an empty last
block of its own (rd_sftend: FFFF:FFFF, count 0), the shape DOSMGR
expects too - it takes the empty block as the last and hangs its
PerVMFiles= block off it.  Every configuration that hung starts.

6504h.  IFSMGR asks for the file name upper-case table as it starts,
and RMDOS refused every table subfunction of 65h.  6502h and 6504h-
6507h now hand back the kernel's own tables, which RMDOS leaves where
they are in the segment, as the kernel answers them.

AND THEN IFSMGR ITSELF - STILL OPEN, AND FENCED OFF.  Past VSHARE,
IFSMGR.386 opens IFS$HLP$, completes the handshake, and Windows halts
inside IFSMGR's Device_Init: no message, and WIN386's real-mode exit
spins on its own "halt" flag (jnz $ at 5F1h of the loader), which is
what follows a fault, not a reported error.  An IFSMGR whose
Device_Init does nothing lets Windows start; patched IFSMGRs without
the version check, without the handshake checks, or cut off at
several later points all halt, but cutting IFSMGR short breaks its
later phases too, so those runs cannot place the fault.  It needs a
debugger that runs 386 enhanced mode.  Before today IFS$HLP$ was
invisible under RMDOS, IFSMGR never loaded and WfW ran without it; a
CONFIG.SYS with IFSHLP.SYS in it - Setup writes one - would now stop
Windows instead.  So drv_find (RMDEV.INC) refuses that one name for
now: IFSMGR and VCACHE decline in their real-mode start-up exactly as
before, IFSHLP stays loaded and in the chain, and WfW as Setup leaves
it - IFSHLP.SYS in CONFIG.SYS, IFSMGR, VCACHE and VSHARE in SYSTEM.INI
- runs the whole cache list on 86Box: the seven programs, the
CACHEBOX and DOSBOX1 boxes, and out.

WFW'S SETUP RUNS ON THE KERNEL.  With the CDS array it got past the
SUBST/JOIN question, copied its files, said it was starting Windows,
and came straight back.  A small TSR logging every EXEC to port E9h
showed why: it runs "c:\windows\system\dosx.exe " - SETUP.INF's
[winexec] spells the program "dosx.exe " - and the kernel said file
not found.  MS-DOS packs a name into eleven blank-filled bytes, so a
blank after the last character is padding (DOS6SRC fcb.asm,
NameTrans); fn_conv (FAT.INC) took any blank for long-name territory.
Trailing blanks are padding now and a blank inside a name is still
long.  (RMDOS's rd_name83 already behaved like DOS.)  The whole
unattended install then completes, under DOSBox-X and on 86Box alike:
DOSX starts, the kernel parks, Windows-mode Setup copies the rest, and
C:\WINDOWS has WIN.COM, WIN386.EXE, Program Manager and its groups,
with CONFIG.WIN and AUTOEXEC.WIN saved as the answer file asked.
And the Windows it installed runs: its C:\WINDOWS, taken off the
86Box disk and grafted onto a fresh one with IFSHLP.SYS in
CONFIG.SYS, ran the same cache list end to end.

THE DOS-BOX STALL - NOT REPRODUCED, STILL OPEN.  In all four of the
previous evening's full sweeps WINSWEEP stopped right after DOSBOX1
closed - its screenshot of the moment was a 0-byte file.  Today the
same list finished and exited every time: twice on the new build with
the host idle and once on the evening's own build; then once each

one block too far reads cache-directory bytes that change as the
cache fills, and the full list fills it furthest - but nothing in
Windows 3.1 has been shown to walk that way, and a stall that will
not happen proves nothing either way.

Regression: RUNTESTS re-recorded twice on all seven rows (81 tests a
row now), then 32 more passes beside the 86Box runs: one SFTSCAN
difference on one row, once - the test reports where "CON " lies in

in both trace builds.

Files: INC\PMDOS.INC, INC\RMDOS.INC, DOS\VDM.INC, DOS\DEVLOAD.INC,

IFSMGR.386 LOADS: TWO FILE TABLE BLOCKS WITH NOTHING IN THEM (2026-10-07)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked two things: whether WfW 3.11's IFSMGR.386 and 32-bit
file access can be made to work, and whether the real-mode disk cache
works.  The cache does, IFSMGR does now, and 32-bit file access is a
project of its own - what it needs is at the end.

THE CACHE WORKS, and IFSMGR leaves it alone.  The CACHEBOX step of the
WfW sweep prints the cache's own figures from a DOS box under Windows:
with IFSMGR loaded, 18,633 hits to 1,219 misses by the end, C: read-
and write-cached, and copying WIN386.EXE a second time cost one miss.
IFSMGR turns SMARTDRV's caching off drive by drive (4A10h BX=3) only
when VFAT.386 - 32-bit file access - is loaded (obj3 CD84h, behind a
flag set only when 1684h finds an API for device 0486h, VFAT's);
without it, it makes no 4A10h call at all, as with SMARTDRV on DOS.

WHY WINDOWS STOPPED.  The entry above left IFSMGR halting Windows in
its Device_Init with no message, and RMDEV.INC refusing it IFS$HLP$ so
that it never got that far.  The trace ended at IFSMGR's close of
IFS$HLP$ after the handshake; the next DOS call was Windows on its way
out.  The answer was in one of that night's patched IFSMGRs, unread:
the one whose per-VM set-up (obj1 33DCh) returned at once got past
the halt into its drive loop - 4408h, 440Dh and 3200h for every
letter - and stopped later, for want of what that routine sets up.
The routine's first call (obj1 0BCAh) copies the address of every
entry in DOS's file table into a table of IFSMGR's own, a block at a
time from LoL+4, and then every entry of the FCB table from LoL+1Ah:

    movzx ecx,word [block+4]        ; the block's count
    next: stosd / add eax,3Bh / loop next

A count of 0 is four thousand million entries, and RMDOS had two
blocks of 0: rd_sftend, the empty block added the night before so
that VSHARE would stop walking off a one-block table, and the FCB
table, a six-byte header at 0400:00D4 with no room for an entry.  The
STOSD wrote over ring-0 memory until it met a page that was not
there.  MS-DOS never builds either - FILES=5 or less makes no second
block at all, and FCBS= runs from 1 to 255 (DOS6SRC
bios/sysinit1.asm) - and the kernel already knew it: VDM.INC leaves
its second block out of the chain rather than publish it empty, "a
walker is entitled to stop at one or divide by it".

THE FIX.  rd_sftend holds one entry.  RMDOS never hands it out
(sft_alloc looks in rd_sfts) and its zero reference count says free to
anything else; DOSMGR still hangs its PerVMFiles= block off it, and
VSHARE's look one block ahead is satisfied as before.  The FCB table
is MS-DOS 5's default, FCBS=4,0, in RMDOS's own segment beside the
file table (rd_fcbtab), each entry 'A' throughout but for a zero
reference count and position, as SYSINIT fills them.  Four with none
protected (LoL+1Eh) is what VSHARE swaps for sixteen of its own, as it
does on DOS.  0400:00D4-D9 is unused now.  drv_find gives out
IFS$HLP$ like any other name, and IFSHLP.SYS in CONFIG.SYS - where
WfW's Setup puts it - means what it means on DOS.

WfW as Setup leaves it - IFSHLP.SYS in CONFIG.SYS, IFSMGR, VCACHE and
VSHARE in SYSTEM.INI - now starts on RMDOS with IFSMGR loaded: IFSHLP
is activated (it hooks 2Ah and 17h, which it does only when IFSMGR
calls it), and the whole cache1 list ran and Windows exited, on the
install made on real DOS and on the one Setup made on the kernel,
both on 86Box.

32-BIT DISK ACCESS, TRIED AND PUT BACK.  With 32BitDiskAccess=ON,
Windows stopped on RMDOS before any VxD's Device_Init, at a message
and a wait for a key: "The Microsoft Windows 32-bit disk driver
(WDCTRL) requires MS-DOS version 3.10 or later."  The version was not
the question.  WDCTRL's real-mode start-up (WIN386.EXE, its segment at
26000h) asks DOS 3.2's "set disk interrupt handler", 2Fh AH=13h -
DS:DX the INT 13h handler the DOS's disk calls reach, ES:BX the vector
put back at a reboot, both swapped for the caller's pair (DOS6SRC
bios/msint13.asm, Orig13 and Old13) - and a DS that comes back
unchanged reads to it as a DOS too old to have the call.

Answering it was tried: both pointers from the INT 13h vector at
rd_vecs, kept and reported, never called.  WDCTRL then got the ROM's
F000:1CD6, put the pair back, and stopped on the hardware instead -
"validation failed at phase 03, 3F".  Its phases compare INT 13h
AH=08h, called straight into the ROM, with the BIOS's own fixed-disk
table at INT 41h: heads, sectors, and at phase 3 the cylinders, where
it wants the table to count two or three more than AH=08h's highest,
the IBM AT's arithmetic.  Phases 0 to 2 passed - the ROM call worked,
and the heads and sectors agreed with the table - so the table it read
is the BIOS's own, and only the BIOS's cylinder arithmetic is off.
This machine's BIOS (86Box p3bf) is the one WDCTRL refuses, and RMDOS
has no part in that comparison.  (A real MS-DOS 5 control on the same
machine never reported either way: the rig - WINSWEEP from C:\WFW on
the DOS VM's disk, no window - produced nothing even with 32-bit disk
access off, so it proves nothing.)

And the answer broke the ordinary path, with 32BitDiskAccess=OFF.
BLOCKDEV's real-mode start-up asks the same question on every start
(after looking for SMARTDRV's double buffer, SMARTAAR) and swaps the
pair straight back; what it keeps is a flag for its protected-mode
half that DOS has the call.  With that flag, BLOCKDEV allocates a V86
call-back and has the code to make it the handler DOS's disk calls
reach (obj1 0074h), telling INT13.386 that DOS disk I/O now comes
through it (INT13 service 3) and chaining what INT13 does not take to
the old pointer.  On MS-DOS it does come through it: IO.SYS's disk
driver issues INT 13h, and IO.SYS's own INT 13h hook, in the vector
table since boot, calls through Orig13 (msbio1.asm, call_orig13).
RMDOS issues INT 13h straight at the vector and would never call the
pointer it accepted.  Both WfW sweeps on that build lost the CACHEBOX
DOS box in its second DIR /S - "This application has violated system
integrity due to execution of an invalid instruction" - where the
build without the answer had run the list clean twice.  That BLOCKDEV
and INT13 acting on a promise RMDOS does not keep is the cause is the
reading of the code, not something watched happening.  Windows 3.1
ran its own list clean on the same build.

So the answer is out again and 2Fh AH=13h is unanswered, as before.
Doing it properly means doing what IO.SYS does: an INT 13h hook of
RMDOS's own in the vector table that jumps through Orig13, taken off
again on the way home (park_restvecs puts back only 20h-2Fh).  That is
the first step of the work below, and it can only be proved on a
machine whose BIOS WDCTRL accepts.

32-BIT FILE ACCESS - WHAT IT TAKES.  Read out of IFSMGR, it is four
things, and the fourth is most of the work:

  1. 21h/32h has to answer a DPB.  For each fixed drive IFSMGR asks
     4408h, 440Dh 0860h and 3200h, and a drive with no DPB is marked
     as not its own (obj3 C925h).  RMDOS answers 32h with an error and
     its list of lists says FFFF:FFFF where the DPB chain starts -
     which IFSMGR also walks, from LoL+0 with the link at +19h, to
     answer 32h for a drive it has taken (obj1 0989h).  From FFFF:FFFF
     that walk leaves the virtual machine.  Nothing reaches it today:
     IFSHLP sends 32h and 1Fh to DOS unless IFSMGR owns the drive.
  2. Its INT 25h probe has to reach INT 13h as IO.SYS sends it.  It
     hooks V86 INT 13h, reads each fixed drive's sector 0 through INT
     25h, and learns the BIOS unit and the partition's CHS from the
     call that comes through - but only an AX=0201h into its own
     buffer (ES its segment, BX=0012h).  RMDOS's INT 25h goes through
     the cache, which reads a 4K element ahead into its own memory,
     and rd_raw renormalises every buffer to BX < 16.
  3. BlockDev has to know the disk, which in WfW 3.11 means 32-bit
     disk access: IFSMGR asks BlockDev for the INT 13h unit, and the
     only other flag it would accept instead (08h in its drive table)
     is set nowhere in IFSMGR.  That needs 2Fh AH=13h done as above,
     and a BIOS WDCTRL accepts - another 86Box machine, or real
     hardware.
  4. Then the real work.  IFSMGR takes a drive by rewriting its CDS
     entry (obj1 2514h): flags OR C000h, its own handle at +49h, 2EB2h
     at +4Dh, the path cut to "C:\".  From then on a DOS sends every
     operation on that drive - opens, finds, EXEC's own reads, the
     closes at a process's end - to the redirector interface, INT 2Fh
     11xxh, with the request in the SDA: the names, ThisSFT, ThisCDS,
     the attributes (IFSHLP's own table points at SDA+1Ch, +24Bh and
     +27Eh).  RMDOS has no redirector interface, and its SDA is the
     first 1Ah bytes.  Without both it would go on reading and writing
     a volume VFAT also owned - two file systems on one FAT, with two
     caches over it.

The fourth is also what WfW's own network client needs, and what
MSCDEX-style CD-ROM redirection uses, so it is worth more than 32-bit
file access alone.

Regression: RUNTESTS on all seven rows differed from the old
baselines only where RMDOS.SYS's size reaches - one more 2K cluster
of it (RMTEST's free space), where a new file's clusters then land
(CACHETST's dirty elements, five to four) and where "CON " lies in
memory (SFTSCAN) - and was re-recorded and matched 81 of 81 on every
row on a confirming pass.  On 86Box, with IFSHLP.SYS and IFSMGR: the
cache1 list to the end on both WfW installs, and Windows 3.1's own
list as the control.  MASM 6.13 assembles RMDOS.ASM plain and in both
trace builds.

Files: INC\RMDOS.INC, DOS\RMFILE.INC, DOS\RMINFO.INC, DOS\RMDEV.INC,
BASELINE\.  RMDOS.SYS is 57,466 bytes (59,819 with the COM trace);
PMDOS.SYS, PMIO.SYS, CMD.EXE and COMMAND.COM are unchanged.
S:\CPP\PM-DOS\BIN\RMDOS.SYS, IMAGES\PMDOS.IMG (the scratch
build's floppy), IMAGES\HD16.IMG (FATREPL in place; a copy boots
headless to the prompt), BASELINE\ and the 86Box VM's two images
carry it, each copy byte-checked against the RMDOS.SYS the sweeps
ran.  Still v0.62, uncommitted, and nothing here has run on real
hardware.


32-BIT FILE ACCESS: A REDIRECTOR INTERFACE, PARAMETER BLOCKS, AND
INT 13h AS IO.SYS HAS IT (2026-10-07)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Charlie asked for the four things the entry above said 32-bit file
access needs, the redirector first: INT 2Fh 11xxh and a whole SDA,
drive parameter blocks, an INT 25h that reaches INT 13h as IO.SYS
sends it, and 32-bit disk access.  RMDOS has all four now, and WfW
3.11's 32-bit file access runs on it: IFSMGR takes C: - its CDS flags
C000h, 4409h's answer 0840h - and the whole sweep list runs on top of
VFAT, every file a DOS box copied coming back byte for byte.  It needs
a 32-bit disk driver BlockDev knows the disk by: WfW's own WDCTRL, on a
BIOS WDCTRL accepts, or LRGDISK.386 (the next entry) on any IDE disk.

THE REDIRECTOR INTERFACE (DOS\RMNET.INC, new).  IFSMGR.386 takes a
drive by marking its CDS entry as a network drive's (C000h), and from
then on a DOS hands everything about that drive to INT 2Fh AH=11h,
which IFSHLP.SYS passes up to IFSMGR.  What the redirector is given
is MS-DOS's own working state, in the SDA at DOS 5's offsets: the
name in OPENBUF and its offset in WFP_START, THISCDS, THISSFT, SFN,
JFN and the handle's address, SATTRIB, the DTA - and for an open or a
create one more word, pushed just before the INT, which IFSHLP takes
from SS:SP+8 inside its own handler.  RMDOS's SDA was the first 1Ah
bytes; it is laid out to 2E0h now, which is where the CDS array
starts (RMINFO.INC, SD_*; RMDOS.INC, RL_SDALEN).  Read out of
IFSHLP.SYS: its INT 2Fh handler (07A4h) sends AH=11h to a table at
073Ah, whose path-call entries look at THISCDS (SDA+282h) and the
name at WFP_START (SDA+292h), whose file calls check the entry's
device pointer for IFSMGR's 0001:0001, and whose find-next reads the
search block at the DTA; its INT 21h side (0498h) sends opens,
creates, finds, renames, deletes, the directories and EXEC to DOS
and only reads, writes, closes and seeks on IFSMGR's own handles
straight to IFSMGR - so all of those reach RMDOS for a claimed drive.

Each call fills in what MS-DOS 5 fills in, in its order, out of
DOS6SRC dos/open.asm, create.asm, close.asm, disk.asm, dircall.asm,
isearch.asm, search.asm, finfo.asm, dinfo.asm, delete.asm, rename.asm
and handle.asm:

  3Dh/3Ch/5Bh   net_open: an entry marked busy, a handle written to
                point at it before the call, 1116h/1117h with ES:DI the
                entry, the mode (no-inherit bit taken out and kept in
                the flags afterwards) or the attribute and "create new"
                pushed; a failure gives both back
  3Fh/40h       1108h/1109h, the buffer in the SDA's DTA brought under
                16 as $READ does, the count cut to its segment; a read
                of nothing is not sent, a write of nothing is (truncate)
  3Eh, closes   1106h - the redirector drops the count, not DOS
  42h AL=2      1121h for a file opened deny-none or deny-read
  57h set       DOS's flags word: not clean, do not stamp at close
  41h 43h 39h   1113h, 110Fh/110Eh, 1103h, 1101h, 1105h (and the name
  3Ah 3Bh 56h   copied into the CDS, as $CHDIR does), 1111h with the
                new name as the SDA's second
  4Eh/4Fh       111Bh/111Ch with the DTA pointed at SEARCHBUF, and the
                twenty-one bytes and the entry turned into the caller's
                DTA as FindSet does; 4Fh knows a redirector's search by
                bit 7 of its first byte, which no drive of RMDOS's has
  36h 1Ch 1Bh   110Ch
  4409h 440Ah   1000h for a redirector's drive; the flags for a handle
  EXEC          through the same open, read and close
  4Ch, 31h      1122h for every process that ends, and 111Dh once its
                handles are closed, as reset_environment and DOS_ABORT do

and RMDOS's own INT 2Fh, the bottom of the chain, now fails any
unanswered 11xxh with AX=1 and the carry, as MS-DOS's does - it used
to answer AL=0 and no carry, which a request reads as done.

A REDIRECTOR'S FILE IS NOT ONE OF RMDOS'S.  The redirector keeps what
it likes in the bytes RMDOS keeps its own file state in, so every
handle call asks first whether the entry is one (sft_isnet).  Not by
bit 15 of the flags word alone, as MS-DOS asks: RMDOS's own devices
keep 4400h's answer in that word, 80D3h for CON, whose high byte is
the device header's and has bit 15 set - and the first test child to
end had its inherited CON, AUX and PRN closed through the redirector.
A redirector's entry is a file, so bit 7 tells them apart.

AND A DRIVE THE REDIRECTOR HAD COMES BACK STALE.  While IFSMGR holds C:,
VFAT writes its FAT and directories through the disk driver; when
Windows ends the letter is RMDOS's again, and its FAT window,
directory sector and cached sectors are from before.  So a volume is
marked VF_STALE when rd_getvol finds its letter a redirector's, when
SMARTDRV's interface is told to start or stop caching it (what IFSMGR
says round VFAT's use of a disk), or when its parameter block's access
byte says FFh; the first use after the letter is RMDOS's again writes
anything RMDOS itself dirtied, drops the rest and the cache's copy, and
mounts the volume again (RMDISK.INC, vol_forget).

FOUND ON THE WAY: AN EXEC'D CHILD RETURNED TO ITS PARENT ON THE CHILD'S
STACK.  fn4B puts RMDOS's call depth back to nought before it jumps to
the child, and the terminate code decided "the parent is waiting in a
call" from that depth, so it never was: every EXEC'd parent resumed on
the stack its child had been standing on, in the child's freed memory.
COMMAND.COM reloads its own stack after an EXEC, as DOS 2 made everyone
do, and never showed it; PARKEXEC had been passing on the child's
leftovers.  MS-DOS resumes the parent on the stack its PSP stamp names.
RMDOS now asks whether the parent's stamped frame returns to exactly
this process's terminate address - which exec_psp copied out of that
frame - and if so the parent is waiting in the EXEC that started it.
No table, so the same segment being a PSP in two virtual machines
cannot confuse it.

PARAMETER BLOCKS.  IFSMGR asks 4408h and 3200h for every hard disk and
will not take a drive without a block; it then reads the header the
block's driver pointer names, to see whether the drive is Stacker's or
DoubleSpace's (obj3 C6B3h).  RMDOS has DOS 4's 21h-byte blocks now,
after its CDS array in the low block (RL_DPB), chained from LoL+0, each
present drive's CDS pointing at its own, filled in at every mount
(dpb_fill), and naming a header of RMDOS's own, RMDISK, whose entries
answer any request "unknown command, done".  1Fh and 32h answer with
them; a redirector's drive gets FFh, as DOS gives it, and so does
FAT32, which a DOS 4 block cannot describe.  The block's access byte
set to FFh means build it again, as in DOS.

INT 25h AS IO.SYS READS.  IFSMGR learns which BIOS disk a letter is on,
and where on it the drive starts, by hooking INT 13h and reading the
drive's sector 0 through INT 25h into its buffer at offset 0012h; the
answer it takes is an AX=0201h at exactly that ES:BX (obj3 C578h).
RMDOS's INT 25h went through the cache, which reads a 4K element into
its own memory, and rd_raw brings every offset under 16.  A read now
goes to the BIOS as IO.SYS's disk driver sends it - AH=02h, a track's
worth at most, straight into the caller's buffer (i25_bios) - and falls
back to the old way for a diskette, a driver's unit, a sector past
cylinder 1023 or a refusal.  The cache writes through, so going round
it reads what it would have.

2Fh AH=13h, DONE THE WAY IT HAD TO BE.  The entry above answered it and
took it out again: WfW's BLOCKDEV.386 put a handler of its own in as
Orig13 and told INT13.386 that DOS's disk calls came through it, and
they did not.  IO.SYS keeps a hook on INT 13h from boot that goes on
through Orig13; RMDOS has one now (i13 in RMDOS.ASM, in the table while
RMDOS is the DOS and taken out on the way home, since PM-DOS puts back
only 20h-2Fh), every INT 13h it makes goes through it, and 2Fh AH=13h
swaps Orig13 and Old13 exactly as int2f_replace_int13 does.

32-BIT DISK ACCESS NEEDS A BIOS WDCTRL ACCEPTS, and that is now
measured rather than guessed.  WDCTRL's real-mode start-up (WIN386.EXE
+26000h, 0818h) calls INT 13h AH=08h through Orig13 and compares it
with the table INT 41h names: heads, sectors, and the table's cylinders
against AH=08h's highest plus 2 or plus 3 - the IBM AT's arithmetic,
which keeps a cylinder for diagnostics.  WDPROBE (scratch) prints the
three under real MS-DOS 5: 86Box's p3bf fails the third; the asus386
(highest 3FDh, table 3FFh) and the vli486sv2g, ASUS's VL/I-486SV2G
(3FEh against 400h), pass - both with the NVRAM of Charlie's DOS VM,
whose Windows 3.1 Setup had put device=*wdctrl in SYSTEM.INI for that
reason.

THE SWEEPS (86Box, WINSWEEP's list, scratch wsweep\run_vl.ps1 and
run_lrg.ps1; IFSBOX now also prints INT 13h AH=08h and what 2Fh AH=13h
holds, as seen from a DOS box):

  vli486sv2g, 504MB, WfW as Setup leaves it - all twelve programs,
  both DOS boxes, Windows out.  With 32-bit disk access (WDCTRL) the
  same, and 2Fh AH=13h in a DOS box now names Windows' own handler
  (FEDB:0D67) where the ROM's was.  With 32-bit file access as well:
  C: is IFSMGR's (C000h), the list runs to the end, Windows exits, and
  every copy and every INT 13h read and write in IFSBOX is right - WfW
  as Microsoft shipped it, on RMDOS.
  p3bf, 2047MB (BIOS 519 x 128 x 63), LRGDISK and VFAT: C: is IFSMGR's
  (C000h), the list runs to the end, Windows exits, every copy
  compares, and the cache's counts stand still through CACHEBOX - VFAT
  has the drive and VCACHE is its cache.
  p3bf, WfW as Setup leaves it, both installs, and Windows 3.1 as the
  control - the sweeps that broke CACHEBOX when 2Fh AH=13h was first
  answered: all three run the list to the end and Windows exits, as
  they did before 2Fh AH=13h was answered at all.

NETTEST.COM (TOOLS, new; RUNTESTS, after CDSTEST) is the test with no
Windows in it.  On the kernel it parks itself; on RMDOS it takes the
highest letter with no drive the way IFSMGR takes one, hooks INT 2Fh,
and serves a handful of files out of its own memory, checking every
call it is handed against what MS-DOS would have handed it - WFP_START
and the name, THISCDS, ES:DI, the busy mark, the handle pointing at
the entry, a transfer's offset under 16, a search's DTA at SEARCHBUF,
PROC_ID - and printing the 11xxh calls each step caused: create,
write, both seeks, close, open, read, the dates, the IOCTLs, dup,
create-new refused, the attributes, find first and next, rename, the
directories with a relative name inside one, free space, TRUENAME, a
wildcard refused before the redirector hears, EXEC of a program on the
drive and a child that ends with a file there still open, an open
nobody answers giving its handle back, and the letter put back.  Then
what IFSMGR asks of C: before it takes it: 4408h, 32h and the block's
driver, the chain from LoL+0 and C:'s CDS naming the block, INT 25h of
sector 0 into xxxx:0012h seen on INT 13h as 0201h at that buffer with
DL=80h, and a handler given to 2Fh AH=13h seeing the next read.

ALSO: PARK.INC's PARK_SLACK is 256 bytes (16 paragraphs), as the HMA
